summary: Auto-track bridges (R8 items 10/11): one river level per crossing, shore-shaped banks, seam-free ground slabs
detail: [R8 BRIDGE 2026-08-30] TD5RE-only, td5_trackgen.c. Third round on 'tiles alternating with water under the bridge end' (seed 99991 span 1031) and second on 'pillars not reaching the ground'. INSTRUMENTED FIRST: new tg_r8_bridge_diag (TD5RE_R8_BRIDGE_DIAG=1) dumps per-span node/deck/water/bed/bank/pier numbers for every bridge span, which is what identified THREE independent causes rather than the one both previous rounds assumed. (a) tg_bridge_water_y decided 'is this crossing over water' with a biome test evaluated PER SPAN, and tg_biome_for_span DITHERS per span inside a biome blend band -- so seed 777 span 165 took the dry-gorge branch while 164 and 166 took the sea branch and the river surface stepped 1239 units down for exactly one span, dragging the bed, the bank depth and the pier foot with it. Now a RUN vote (tg_bridge_run_is_water) plus the run MINIMUM sea level, so a crossing has one surface. MEASURED max water-surface spread within a run: 1405 -> 0 (99991), 6577 -> 0 (777). (b) The R7 submerge ramp moved BOTH profile points together, making the bank a flat SHELF whose single height ramped from road level to below the water -- so it sat ABOVE the river for every span the ramp had not finished, which is both ends of every run. Rewritten as a shore: the inner point carries the ramp (bank top), everything past one 6000-unit bank face is pinned fully submerged, so the only ground above the surface is a slope. MEASURED spans with the outer bank above water: 55 -> 3 (99991), 109 -> 5 (777); residuals are the run-START spans where the deck meets the ground and there is no gorge. (c) tg_emit_ground evaluated the cross-section ONCE at span si and applied it to both the near AND far edge of the slab, so any span-varying profile stepped at every span boundary -- up to 1529 units of vertical crack per span inside a bridge run, with water showing through. Now sampled at si and si+1 and interpolated across, so consecutive slabs share an edge by construction, on any profile. Also fixed the gorge outer edge, hard-coded to the pre-R6 24000 verge while the ordinary skirt had been narrowed to 12000 (measured 11864-unit lateral jump between spans 1000 and 1001). PIERS (item 10): RE-MEASURED FROM SCRATCH rather than citing R7. Every pier foot on both seeds sits at least 400 units BELOW the water surface -- 0 of 39 (99991) and 0 of 85 (777) stop short -- across all four and all eight runs. Pier HEIGHT is therefore not the defect. The (b) shelf floating above the river beside the pier is the most likely thing being read as 'the pillar does not reach the ground', and it is now gone. NOT INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED: no frame isolates a pier foot against the water line, so item 10 is reported as most-likely-resolved-via-(b), not as proven. A/B gate TD5RE_R8_BRIDGE_WATER=0 restores the R7 behaviour; matched-pose oblique frames taken at span ~1043. CONFIRM BY DRIVING: AUTO-GENERATED (DefaultTrack 60) seed 99991 across 1000-1039 and 1640-1679 and seed 777 across 160-199 -- look under and beside the deck for slabs standing above the water and for steps between consecutive ground slabs.

summary: Auto-track tunnels (R8 items 4/17/18): unbanded portal headwall, no grass median in a bore, longer bores and decks
detail: [R8 BRIDGE 2026-08-30] TD5RE-only, td5_trackgen.c. (item 4) 'the tunnel textures on span 477 still look weird, I do not want this grey-ish texture, the one with lighter gray stripes'. Third round on this mouth and the first with the page DUMPED rather than argued about by id: new TD5RE_R8_TEXDUMP=1 writes every assembled 64x64 page to log/tgpage_NNN.ppm. The page actually chosen at 477 is 301 (TD5_TG_PAGE_R7_BRIDGE+0) and the dump shows exactly the reported artefact -- a near-white coping band across the top rows plus a dark form-course line every 20 rows. TWO causes, both fixed: the page carried the banding, AND the jamb face is 4100 units tall while V was scaled by the 3000-unit world tile, so the page repeated 1.37x up each jamb and the bright band reappeared a third of the way up, twice, on both jambs of every mouth. New page TD5_TG_PAGE_R8_BRIDGE+1 is cast concrete with NO axis-aligned banding (two coprime low-frequency patch fields, hashed vertical weather streaks, narrow 96..171 palette), and portal V now maps over the FACE 0..1 so no face can sample the page twice vertically. Verified selected: R8TDIAG reports portal_page=352 at all four mouths on 99991 and all eight on 777. HONEST LIMIT: the round asked for art MINED from re/assets rather than authored. Shipped level textures are unnamed tex_NNN.png with no catalogue of which is a portal headwall, and identifying one was out of reach this round -- this is an authored replacement, with both the removed page (301) and the chosen page (352) dumped so the swap is auditable. Knob TD5RE_R8_PORTAL=0 restores the R7 page and mapping. (item 17) 'avoid green medians within tunnels like on span 562' -- the fork gore takes its surface from the BIOME ground page, and a biome does not stop at a portal, so where a fork runs through a bore (seed 777 fork 510-631 crosses tunnel 560-579, biome ALPINE) the median between the two carriageways was grass, indoors. The bore now decides what is legal inside it: the gore surface becomes a new bore-floor concrete page (R8_BRIDGE+0) and a PLANTED avenue median becomes the concrete-barrier treatment, both only for spans actually enclosed, so the material change lands on the portal line. Knob TD5RE_R8_BORE_MEDIAN=0. Inventory confirms the emitter fires at 560-579 on seed 777, which contains the reported span 562. (item 18) 'you can make longer tunnels and bridges' -- bridge runs 40 -> 56 spans, tunnel runs 20 -> 32. The bridge crown stays at 2000 and the grade cap gets LOOSER, not tighter: peak slope is H*PI/RUN, so 2000*PI/56 = 112 units per span (grade 0.075) against 157 (0.105) before. IMPORTANT SIDE EFFECT, which is why this is a gate: runs are chosen by hashing si/RUN, so changing RUN does not lengthen the existing crossings, it REPARTITIONS the track into an entirely new set. On seed 99991 the four bridges at 1000-1039 / 1160-1199 / 1320-1359 / 1640-1679 become two at 1176-1231 / 1400-1455 and the two tunnels become one at 1248-1279 -- the spans the user reported (477 and 1031) then contain no crossing at all. Both layouts are therefore verified separately: items 4/10/11/13/17 at the spans the user named with TD5RE_R8_LONGRUN=0, and race completion with it on. Default ON. summary: Auto-track fork: median fills the gap between the split carriageways

Cause: the main (left) and branch (right) half carriageways only touch at the fork and rejoin; where the branch bows away, the strip between the main right edge (road centre, lateral 0) and the branch left edge (branch_shift + width/4) had no mesh and showed the void, because the ground skirt only covers OUTSIDE the full road width, not this interior gore. summary: Auto-track fork REDESIGNED native-faithful: splits down the middle, no widening ramp
detail: [AUTOTRACK NATIVE FORK 2026-08-25] TD5RE-only, td5_trackgen.c. User asked whether the fork matched native TD5. It did NOT -- I inspected level014 (a shipped track with a fork) and found: native forks split a CONSTANT-WIDTH road DOWN THE MIDDLE into two HALF-width carriageways (level014: 6-lane road -> 3 main + 3 branch at the type-8 span), the carriageways run apart, then MERGE at a type-11 span back to full width that STAYS wide (4+4 -> 8). No widening ramp, no convergence bow. Also native lane_bitmask=0 everywhere (which confirmed the earlier slow-lane fix). My old impl instead WIDENED the approach 4->8 (a ramp = the weird beginning) and CONVERGED the corridor back onto the main line keeping 4 lanes (the weird ending), which also caused the two full-width roads to overlap (the walker flicker / invisible walls). REDESIGN: the lanes-wide road now splits into MAIN (left half, lanes/2, centre +width/4) over ring spans F+1..F+LEN and BRANCH (right half, lanes-lanes/2, centre -width/4 + outward bow) over the appended corridor; the fork span F and rejoin span R stay FULL width. tg_branch_shift rewritten (right-half + bow, TD5_TG_BRANCH_BOW); the fork/main/rejoin strip spans get dedicated rows (tg_patch_span) at the split widths; the road MESH follows via a new wscale param on tg_road_edge/tg_emit_road_quad (0.5 for the half carriageways). Because the two halves are OPPOSITE halves that only bow apart, they never share ground -> no walker flicker; and because the rejoin is the road OWN width there is no forward lane-drop to strand -> and lanes(R) > lanes(R-1) so the type-11 REVERSE split fires too (branch is now reverse-drivable, unlike before). VERIFIED by frame (seed 123456789): at span 596 the road forks into two carriageways down the middle with lanes=4 (NOT the old widened 8) and AI cars taking each prong; the corridor is a 2-lane carriageway. Drive traces: only 1-2 branch<->main crossings over a full pass (the legitimate fork + rejoin junctions, not flicker); reached the corridor end and merged. FULL selftest suite 58/58 PASS incl. Moscow+Pelton golden traces (redesign is inert with branches off / on shipped tracks). SUPERSEDES the earlier notes that the rejoin stays 4-lane and the branch is not reverse-drivable. CONFIRM BY DRIVING: AUTO-GENERATED (DefaultTrack 60, branches+scenery, AI_BRANCH_PCT 50) -- the fork should look like the road dividing in two (no bulge), each carriageway half width, merging cleanly at 641. Watch for: the corridor is narrow (2 lanes of a 4-lane road); a GORE between the carriageways where they bow apart may show ground/void mid-branch (ground under the gore is not specially filled yet); wall_clear in the race trace is meaningless on branch spans (span_norm-based). KNOWN NEXT: fill the gore ground; consider a wider base road so the half carriageways are 3+ lanes.

summary: Auto-track branch: fixed invisible walls at the merge (walker main<->corridor flicker)
detail: [AUTOTRACK BRANCH WALKER-COMMIT 2026-08-25] TD5RE-only, td5_track.c td5_track_update_actor_position. User: driving the branch, invisible walls where the original road merges. ROOT CAUSE (from the race.log minimap trace): a branch corridor runs BESIDE the main road it forked from (spans ring+1..ring+LEN parallel to the main F+1..F+LEN, both full drivable roads with their own collision rails). In the overlap region the chassis reference point sits inside BOTH roads quads, so the position walker (UpdateActorTrackPosition) re-located the car ACROSS the ring boundary frame to frame -- the logged span oscillated e.g. 612(main)<->1812(corridor), both normalising to 612. Each flip swaps the collision rails to the OTHER, laterally-offset road, so the car is shoved by the wall of the road it is not currently on = invisible walls. FIX: a guard in the chassis wrapper (NOT the byte-faithful recursive core) snapshots the span, runs the walker, and if the span crossed the branch<->main ring boundary FROM A PLAIN INTERIOR span (type != 8/9/10/11), reverts to the snapshot -- because a branch<->main transition is only legitimate through a junction span (type 8 fork, 9/10 sentinels, 11 rejoin). So the car stays committed to the road it is on and only crosses at real junctions. Inert on every non-forked track (s_span_count == ring), and it does not touch the walker core. VERIFIED: scripted drive down the corridor now reports 0 branch<->main crossings (span monotonic 1823..1838; was oscillating); FULL selftest suite 58/58 PASS including the Moscow+Pelton golden traces, so no native-fork or sim regression. CONFIRM BY DRIVING: on the AUTO-GENERATED track (DefaultTrack 60, TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_BRANCHES=1 + SCENERY=1) take the branch and drive through the rejoin at span 641 -- the car should hold the corridor and merge without hitting invisible walls. STILL OPEN (separate, known): the corridor road is only DRAWN while the player is on the branch, so the branch prong ahead looks roadless as you approach the fork on the main line (render walk centres on the normalised span); and the branch is not reverse-drivable.

summary: Auto-track: outer lanes no longer secretly slow the car (were an off-road surface)
detail: [AUTOTRACK SLOW OUTER LANES 2026-08-25] TD5RE-only, td5_trackgen.c. User: the lanes that make the car go slower have the same road texture as the rest. Cause: every autotrack span set its lane bitmask (span byte +0x02) to 1|(1<<(lanes-1)) -- the OUTER lanes. surface_type_for_span_lane (td5_track.c:2895) turns a MARKED lane into (surface_attr>>4)|0x10 and an unmarked lane into surface_attr&0x0F. With surface_attr 0x11 that is outer=0x11, inner=0x01. td5_track_surface_is_slow returns 1 for ANY surface with the 0x10 bit, so the two outer lanes were an alternate/off-road (slow) surface -- phys_surface_grip/drag sap grip and add rolling drag there -- while textured identically to the fast inner asphalt. So drifting wide silently slowed the car with no visual cue. FIX: emit lane bitmask 0 at both span-emit sites (main tg_emit_span_range and the corridor/pad tg_append_span), so every lane resolves to the low nibble 0x01 = dry asphalt, full grip, not slow. Also makes the AI (which reads the same surface to avoid slow lanes, td5_ai.c/td5_ai_traffic.c) treat the whole road as drivable. VERIFIED: builds clean, autotrack generates, selftest smoke exit 0; the fix is deterministic (bitmask 0 -> surface 0x01 for all lanes -> surface_is_slow=0). CONFIRM BY DRIVING (feel): on the AUTO-GENERATED track drift from the centre out toward either road edge -- the car should hold speed the whole width now, where before the outermost lane on each side dragged it down. Regression: shipped tracks untouched (this is in the generator); AI pace on the autotrack may change slightly since it no longer routes around phantom slow outer lanes.

summary: Auto-track: closed the road-to-grass gap (terrain meets asphalt flush)
detail: [AUTOTRACK ROAD-GRASS GAP 2026-08-25] TD5RE-only, td5_trackgen.c tg_emit_ground. User saw a thin gap/lip between the road edge and the grass. Cause: the ground skirt used a uniform TD5_TG_GROUND_DROP (70) on ALL its vertices, so the whole skirt -- including the INNER edge that meets the road -- sat 70 units below the road surface, leaving a thin void at the road edge. Fix: the inner skirt edge (the 4 points coincident with the road left/right edge) now sits at ROAD LEVEL (nly/fly, no drop); only the OUTER edge keeps the drop, giving a gentle embankment. Inner edge and road edge share the same line (they meet, do not overlap), so no z-fight. VERIFIED by frame (seed 123456789, autotrack, no branches): road meets ground flush, no lip. Selftest smoke passes. Affects all autotrack biomes (this is the shared ground emitter); no shipped track. CONFIRM: drive the AUTO-GENERATED track and look at the road edge -- terrain should meet the asphalt with no gap on straights and gentle curves. Known minor: on TIGHT curves the ground inner edge is a straight near-far chord while the road edge is subdivided/curved, so a hairline gap can still appear mid-span on sharp bends.

summary: Auto-track: branch corridor now has a road surface (was bare ground)
detail: [AUTOTRACK BRANCH CORRIDOR ROAD 2026-08-25] TD5RE-only, td5_trackgen.c. The branch corridor was DRIVABLE (strip collision) but had NO road mesh -- a car on the branch drove on bare ground, no asphalt or lane lines (user-reported). ROOT CAUSE, and it was a latent OOB bug: tg_emit_models receives the FULL strip span count nspans (with a branch that is ring + 1 + LEN, e.g. 1841), but the centerline NodeList nl only holds the main-ring nodes (1801). The per-span loop read nl->v[si] for the pad + corridor spans (si >= ring), which is OUT OF RANGE, so it emitted garbage meshes that frustum-culled to nothing -- hence no visible corridor road. FIX: derive the real main ring (ring = nspans - 1 - LEN when branches active), skip the pad span, and for each corridor span emit a road quad at the CORRECT bowed geometry -- tg_emit_road_quad(nl, F+1+k, lanes, tg_branch_shift(k), tg_branch_shift(k+1)) -- the same shift the corridor strip rows use, so the visible road lines up with where the car drives. tg_road_edge/tg_emit_road_mesh were refactored to take a lateral shift (tg_emit_road_quad; the plain road is shift 0,0). The renderer reaches these via the secondary branch loop (td5_render_mesh.c:2631, active when player_branch_span>=0) which calls td5_track_get_display_list(branch_span) -> MODELS.DAT entry branch_span>>2, and those entries now hold real corridor road. VERIFIED by frame (seed 123456789, branches+scenery, spawn on the corridor raw ~1823): the car is centred on asphalt with dashed lane lines following the bow, where it was bare ground before. Selftest smoke 12/12. Only affects the autotrack with TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_BRANCHES=1 + TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_SCENERY=1; no shipped track (inside the generator). CONFIRM: launch AUTO-GENERATED (DefaultTrack 60) seed 123456789 with both knobs on, spawn on the corridor (raw>=1801) or set TD5RE_AI_BRANCH_PCT=100 and watch an AI take the branch -- there should be a textured road under the whole corridor, aligned with the car. KNOWN LIMIT: the corridor road is drawn by the branch loop only when the player is ON the branch (player_branch_span>=0); approaching the fork on the MAIN line, the branch prong ahead may still show no road until you commit to it (the main entry walk is centred on the normalised span). Left as a follow-up.

summary: Auto-track scenery: branch no longer clips buildings; ground reads flat not distorted
detail: [AUTOTRACK SCENERY 2026-08-25] TD5RE-only, td5_trackgen.c. Two visual fixes spotted in the AI-branch frames. (1) BRANCH CORRIDOR THROUGH BUILDINGS: buildings sit width/2 + gap + footprint from the road centre (INDUSTRIAL gap 3000..9000), and the branch corridor bows ~1.9 road-widths in the -n->tz direction over its parallel main spans -- the side<0 building side -- reaching well past the near buildings there, so branch traffic drove straight THROUGH them (and the chase cam ended up inside a building, filling the screen with a blown-up wall face). Fix: tg_building_for_span suppresses side<0 buildings across the fork approach + corridor span range [F-BRANCH_WIDEN, F+BRANCH_LEN+1] when branches are enabled; far side>0 buildings and every span outside the fork are untouched. Only matters with TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_BRANCHES=1. (2) DISTORTED GROUND TEXTURE filling the background: two compounding causes. (a) CITY and INDUSTRIAL biomes floored their ground skirt with the WALL page (building concrete + window grid); stretched over the undulating skirt the grid warped into a rippled look. Added a dedicated flat TD5_TG_PAGE_GROUND (concrete/gravel grain, NO lines) and pointed both biomes ground_page at it (PAGE_COUNT 5->6). (b) THE REAL culprit for the far-ground shimmer: the ground skirt UVs ran U 0..4 across the full 24000-unit width while V advanced one tile per ~1500-unit span -- a ~4:1 lateral STRETCH that smeared the texture AND defeated the (isotropic, box-filter) mipmaps, so the far ground aliased/rippled. Fix: outer U = GROUND_WIDTH/SPAN_LENGTH so tiles are SQUARE; the mips then minify cleanly and the ground reads flat to the horizon. FIELDS/FOREST (green page) were never affected. VERIFIED by frame (seed 123456789, branches+scenery, AI field at the fork): the corridor car drives on clear road (was buried in a building at span ~608), and the background ground is a uniform flat concrete surface (was a rippled scaly sheet). Selftest smoke 12/12. CONFIRM: launch AUTO-GENERATED (DefaultTrack 60) seed 123456789 with TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_SCENERY=1 in a CITY or INDUSTRIAL stretch -- the ground should read as flat concrete with no rippled/smeared texture to the horizon; then TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_BRANCHES=1 and drive the branch (spawn raw>=1801) -- no buildings in the corridor. Regression: the ground-page swap + UV change affect ALL autotrack CITY/INDUSTRIAL spans (not gated) but no shipped track (this is inside the generator); the building suppression is gated on branches. Watch for: the near-road ground tiling at 1500 units could look busy on a dead-flat stretch (it did not in the frames, the texture is flat noise); and a bare right verge over the ~48-span fork range where buildings were suppressed.

summary: Auto-track: AI cars take the branch as an alternate line (route variety)
detail: [AUTOTRACK AI BRANCH ROUTE-VARIETY 2026-08-24] TD5RE-only, td5_ai_driver.c. Makes a configurable fraction of the AI field take the branch CORRIDOR at a fork instead of all holding the main line, so a forked track shows two lines of cars. Knob TD5RE_AI_BRANCH_PCT (0..100, DEFAULT 0 = off, no car diverts). WHY IT WAS DEFERRED and how this avoids the trap: the driver model passed fork_diverge=0 because early attempts half-committed to tight forks and clipped the divider. Two things make it safe now. (1) A fork widens its approach to main+branch lanes, so a WIDE span (lane_count>=6) IS a fork approach -- the only place the branch lanes exist -- and the change only engages there; on normal road it is inert and the car holds the main racing line, so no right-hug/clip. (2) SCOPED to the autotrack branch feature: s_branch_feature = td5_env_flag_off("TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_BRANCHES") (that helper means "opt in" despite the name), so with branches OFF the aim logic is byte-identical to before -- ZERO change to every shipped track, the golden-trace races, and native forks (level013/014), which keep their existing centre aim. FIXES A PRE-EXISTING BUG found on the way: the driver aimed at lane_count/2, which on an 8-lane fork is lane 4 = the DIVIDER, and the walker counts sub_lane>=main_lanes as the branch -- so a centre-aiming car drifted onto the branch BY ACCIDENT (measured: at pct=0 before the fix the car took the corridor). Now the aim is decisive: main carriageway = lane_count/4 (low lanes) by default, branch carriageway = 3*lane_count/4 (high lanes) + fork_diverge=1 for a branch-taking slot. The split is symmetric about lane_count/2 because the widen keeps the original road on the low lanes and extends the branch to the high side. WHICH cars: driver_slot_takes_branch(slot) is a deterministic per-slot hash (stable across a race, spreads slots so small percentages are not all slot 0), so a fixed reproducible fraction diverges. VERIFIED (AI-driven slot 0, seed 123456789, branches+scenery on, spawn before the fork): pct=0 -> car stays on the main road (max raw span 667, never > ring 1800), took_corridor=false; pct=100 -> car drives the corridor spans (max raw 1840), took_corridor=true; both clean exit code 0, no crash.log. Selftest smoke 12/12 with the feature off. CONFIRM: launch AUTO-GENERATED (DefaultTrack 60) seed 123456789 with TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_BRANCHES=1, TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_SCENERY=1, a full field (opponents 5), and TD5RE_AI_BRANCH_PCT=50; watch the field SPLIT at the fork (span 600) -- roughly half the cars peel onto the side corridor and rejoin at span 641, the rest stay main. Check none clip the divider or spin at the fork/rejoin. Regression: with the knob absent/0 AND/OR branches off, the AI line is unchanged everywhere (the gate early-outs). NOT DONE: (a) no captured FRAME of the field splitting (trace-verified only; the countdown-cam framedump timing made a clean shot awkward, same as the branch merge frame); (b) not tuned for how MANY cars should take it by default or whether it should scale with rubber-band/skill (currently a flat hash fraction); (c) corridor is ~1.05x the main length (a gentle bow) so taking it is route variety, NOT a shortcut -- if it should be a real strategic alternate the corridor geometry would need to differ in length.

summary: Auto-track: branch forks recombine via a type-11 rejoin (converge + merge)
detail: [AUTOTRACK BRANCH TYPE-11 REJOIN 2026-08-24] TD5RE-only, td5_trackgen.c, default OFF via TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_BRANCHES=1. Upgrades the branch fork from a one-way soft merge to a recombining split. TWO changes. (1) GEOMETRIC CONVERGENCE: tg_branch_shift previously ended the corridor a full road width off the main line (-width at k=LEN), so the corridor hard-linked back across a lateral gap -- the soft-merge snap. It now peels off at the fork (-width) and ramps back to 0 by the corridor end, plus a mid-run outward bow (sin) for visible separation, so the side road curves back onto the main line before it rejoins. (2) TYPE-11 REJOIN: the rejoin span R = fork + 1 + corridor_len (a main-ring span) is marked span_type 11 (JUNCTION_BWD) and back-linked to the corridor SENTINEL_END (index ring+LEN) via a new tg_set_span_type_prev helper that touches only the type byte and link_prev, leaving R's 4-lane main rows intact. R KEEPS 4 lanes on purpose: the forward walker has no lane-drop path (only the type-8 fork narrows forward; the type-11 forward case falls through to default, which adjusts sub_lane by HEIGHT not lane count), so an 8-lane R followed by the 4-lane R+1 would STRAND the high sub-lanes off the road. A 4-lane convergence merge (dest_lanes == cur_lane_count, zero sub_lane delta) is the only forward-safe recombine for a road that resumes at normal width. WHY THE OLD wall_clear PANIC WAS A FALSE ALARM (recorded so a THIRD session does not re-trip it): the race trace wall_clear column (td5_game.c:5233) is computed by projecting the car onto the span_norm (normalised MAIN-road) rail. On the bowed corridor the car is legitimately offset from the main line, so wall_clear reads large NEGATIVE -- it is a diagnostic artifact, NOT a containment failure. The real wall resolver on forward races (td5_track_resolve_wall_contacts, geo_active is false forward) reads track_span_raw and the span own left/right_vertex_index, which the corridor has its own bowed rows for, so the corridor IS contained. WALL_CLEAR IS INVALID ON ANY BRANCH SPAN (span_raw > ring); do not read it there. VERIFIED: drove a car down the corridor (spawn StartSpanOffset ~1812, lands raw ~1827; note the ~15-span spawn-ahead, and spawning past ~raw 1836 lands the car beyond the finish and breaks). airborne_mask 0 the whole corridor (on the surface, contained), monotonic progress, no teleport, and wall_clear recovered -1974 -> +14 as raw went 1834 -> 1839 (the corridor converging onto the main line -- exactly the convergence fix working). Selftest smoke 12/12 with the knob off. CONFIRM: launch AUTO-GENERATED (DefaultTrack 60) seed 123456789 with TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_BRANCHES=1 + TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_SCENERY=1; the fork is fixed at span 600, corridor 601..640, rejoin 641. Drive the main line through 600..641 (already sane: 0 teleports, wall_clear positive). To exercise the branch itself, spawn on the corridor (raw >= 1801). Watch the side road curve out and back and merge at 641. NOT DONE / follow-ups: (a) the branch is NOT drivable in REVERSE -- with lanes(R)==lanes(R-1) the type-11 reverse split never fires; a reverse-drivable dual carriageway needs the whole fork..rejoin region held at double width, a larger change; (b) the AI drives the corridor SLOWLY (~12 spans in 240s), possibly because the negative wall_clear-style rail read makes the DRIVER model think it is off-rail -- investigate whether the AI pace model reads a span_norm rail on branch spans; (c) no picture-perfect chase-cam merge frame yet (the one captured caught the countdown), though it does show the two carriageways with cars on each. Regression: knob OFF => the branch block early-outs, elevation/strip byte-unchanged, shipped tracks untouched.

summary: Auto-track: deliberate bridges (road climbs over chosen runs, barriers on the deck)
detail: [AUTOTRACK DELIBERATE BRIDGES 2026-08-24] TD5RE-only, td5_trackgen.c, default OFF via TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_BRIDGES=1. WHY: after the elevated-gate fix earlier the same day, bridges stopped appearing entirely, CONFIRMED BY EYE on the frames. That was correct but left a content gap: the elevation profile is 2..6 sine waves over ~1800 spans, so its wavelength is 300..900 spans and across the +/-8 span local-terrain window it is essentially straight. Measured local convexity peaks near 160 against a 900 threshold, so the road can never rise above its own surroundings fast enough to count as a bridge. FIX: bridges are now PLACED, not detected, exactly as tunnels and branch forks are. tg_span_in_bridge_run(si) hashes si/TD5_TG_BRIDGE_RUN (24) and picks ~1 run in 8 past the grid, stateless so the generator, the deck emitter and the guardrail gate all agree without passing anything around. MEASURED 10 runs, 240 of 1800 spans (13%); crown spans for seed 123456789 are 132, 324, 444, 636, 828, 948, 1140, 1452, 1644, 1764. tg_apply_elevation then flattens each run to its own chord and adds a raised-cosine hump (zero value AND zero slope at both ends, so it splices in without a kink). EMISSION KEYS OFF THE RANGE, NOT THE LIFT, on purpose: 9 of the 10 runs get grade-clamped and the lowest crown is only +778, whose lift is under the 900 threshold, so a lift-keyed emitter would silently drop most of them again. THE TRAP THAT COST A ROUND HERE, worth reading before touching this: hump slope SUPERPOSES on the sine profile slope. A 1300 crown over 24 spans is 0.113 grade on its own, comfortably under the 0.120 cap, but on top of the existing profile it pushed the worst span to 0.169, and tg_apply_elevation's rescale is GLOBAL -- it multiplied the WHOLE track by 0.708, so merely enabling bridges flattened every hill on the map by 29%. That is why each run is flattened to its chord first (which also removes the base slope from the grade budget) and each hump height is then clamped to the leftover budget. Verify the fix held by confirming there is NO "elevation rescaled" line in log/race.log with bridges on. VERIFIED SO FAR (frames in .happy-share/cmt79nam90739s2262ypsdlv2/): the climb is real (POS y=113 at span 615 versus y=905 at span 645 inside run 624..647); guardrails DO render and DO appear on the deck, proven by a controlled A/B at span 645 with identical POS and camera where the only difference is the barriers (brg3_ON_ondeck_span630.png versus brg3_ON_rails_ondeck_span630.png); self-test smoke 12/12 PASS with bridges off. NOT VERIFIED, needs a human: (a) the DECK SLAB and PIERS are still effectively invisible from any on-road camera, because tg_emit_bridge puts the deck at y-300 with half-height 200 (i.e. tucked under the road) and piers every 4th span extending downward -- so an elevated stretch reads as "road on a hill with barriers", not obviously as a bridge. If it should read as a bridge, the deck needs structure ABOVE the road surface or the piers need to be visible from the side. (b) DRIVING IT: raising the road changes the STRIP, which is the surface the car actually drives on, so climb, AI pacing and crest jumps are all in scope -- one earlier capture at span 634 showed WHEELS: LR (a single wheel in contact) at speed 203, which may be a normal crest or may be a launch, and was NOT chased down. Drive several runs at speed and watch for airborne spans and AI pacing changes. (c) whether ~1 run in 8 is the right frequency. Regression: with the knob OFF the elevation path is byte-unchanged (the run loop early-outs), shipped tracks are untouched, and generation still delivers 1800 spans.

summary: Auto-track: bridges no longer under 87% of the road; optional corner guardrails
detail: [AUTOTRACK ELEVATED-GATE FIX + GUARDRAILS 2026-08-24] TD5RE-only, td5_trackgen.c. TWO things, one root cause. ROOT CAUSE: elevated was measured as span_y - ground_y where ground_y was the GLOBAL MINIMUM elevation of the whole 1800-span track. On any rolling track that is true for almost every span, so tg_emit_bridge was emitting a deck slab (plus a pier every 4th span) on 87% of spans -- MEASURED 1576/1800. This shipped in Phase 1 and is why MODELS.DAT was 4.40 MB. FIX: a new tg_local_ground_y(nl, si) takes the CHORD between the window endpoints (span si-W and si+W, W = TD5_TG_LIFT_WINDOW = 8, knob TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_LIFT_WINDOW 1..200) and lift is measured against that. Grade-invariant BY CONSTRUCTION: on any constant grade the midpoint of the two endpoints equals this node own height, so lift is exactly 0 no matter how steep, and only local CONVEXITY -- road humping over ground that falls away both sides, which is what a bridge IS -- gives positive lift. MEASURED RESULT: MODELS.DAT 4.40 MB down to 2.27 MB, identical on all 3 seeds tested. CONSEQUENCE THAT NEEDS A HUMAN EYE: with the correct local measure this generator essentially NEVER reaches 900 units of local convexity (seed 123456789 peaks near 160, seed 42 near 200, seed 777 does not reach 100), so BRIDGES NOW EFFECTIVELY NEVER APPEAR. That is believed correct -- the 87% was pure artifact -- but it IS a visible content change and nobody has looked at a frame. TD5_TG_BRIDGE_MIN_LIFT stays 900 deliberately: the deck is 780 tall and the pier is lift*0.5, so lowering it to force bridges back yields a deck buried in the road and a pier too short to see. Making bridges a real feature again means PLACING them deliberately the way tunnels and branch forks are (a chosen span range with elevation driven to suit), which is NOT done. GUARDRAILS (new, default OFF, opt in with TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_GUARDRAILS=1): one prism per side per gated span, emitted in the per-span loop rather than the box pass because that pass recovers offsets by dividing appended bytes by piece count, which only holds for same-sized boxes. Own texture page (page 4, steel with a shadow gutter). Gate = elevated OR bend, EXCLUDING tunnel interiors (walls already read as a boundary) and the branch fork mouth (a barrier would visually wall off the corridor). Bend threshold TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_RAIL_DEG10 defaults to 50 (5 deg of heading change per span), CHANGED from 15: at 15 it railed 62% of spans, i.e. down every straight, which is the opposite of the intent. MEASURED at 50: 14% / 14% / 11% of spans on seeds 123456789 / 42 / 777, and MODELS.DAT 2.27 up to 2.49-2.56 MB. Curvature is the stable signal; coverage barely moves between seeds, unlike the elevation gate. CONFIRM: (a) launch the AUTO-GENERATED track (DefaultTrack 60) with TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_SEED=123456789 and NO guardrails, and confirm the road no longer looks like it is on a continuous viaduct -- compare against the old 05_bridges.png, and confirm nothing now looks like it is floating with its deck removed; (b) relaunch with TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_GUARDRAILS=1 and confirm barriers appear THROUGH CORNERS and not along straights; (c) drive into a barrier and confirm the visible barrier line coincides with where the car actually stops -- the rails are derived from the span edge points, whereas collision comes from the STRIP rail vertices via td5_track_resolve_wall_contacts, and those two are NOT proven to agree; (d) check log/race.log for the guardrails on N/1800 spans (X%) line and treat 0% or ~100% as the gate being wrong. Regression: shipped tracks are untouched (this is all inside the generator), and generation must still deliver the full 1800 spans with no boxed in warning.

summary: Auto-track acute sections throw sharper (~176deg) switchbacks
detail: [AUTOTRACK ACUTE CURVES 2026-08-23] TD5RE-only, td5_trackgen.c. The procedural centerline walk clamps each span's heading to a budget measured from the +X axis; that clamp is what makes the walk NON-TRAPPING (with |dev|<=limit every span advances the axis coordinate by >= span_len*cos(limit)>0, so the coordinate is strictly increasing and two nodes far enough apart in span index can never coincide -- self-intersection is geometrically impossible, not merely rejected). Previously ALL sections shared one 80deg budget (a 160deg max switchback) and the adjacent-skip exemption window was a hardcoded 25. CHANGE 1: ACUTE sections now use a sharper budget (default 88deg, knob TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_ACUTE_DEG 80..89) so they swing up to ~176deg, close to a hairpin; straight/curve/dual-lane keep the 80deg spine budget. cos(88deg) is still >0 so forward progress -- and the non-trapping proof -- survive. A TRUE >=180deg down-track hairpin is INCOMPATIBLE with a single-axis monotone guarantee (cos<=0 there) and is deliberately NOT offered. CHANGE 2: the adjacent-skip is now DERIVED at build time (tg_adjacent_skip) from the LARGER of the two budgets and the widest road the generator can emit (12 lanes): skip = ceil((w_max + lane_width*0.25)/(span_len*cos(limit_max))). A hardcoded 25 would silently under-exempt once the budget rose past 80deg and could false-reject a legal tight turn; the derived value keeps the guarantee sound for any budget. INVARIANT: any two centerline nodes >= skip apart have axis-coordinate separation >= skip*span_len*cos(limit_max) >= worst-case too-close need, so they provably cannot overlap; nodes within skip are the legitimately-close turn interior and are exempt. tg_too_close became the derived-skip backstop that should never fire. MINOR: at an acute's sharpest LEFT-hand apex the route heading byte reaches toward the <4 junction sentinel; tg_emit_routes already clamps to >=4, a small heading-fidelity loss on a few apex spans, not a sentinel collision. CONFIRM: launch the AUTO-GENERATED track with a pinned seed (TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_SEED=123456789) and look for visibly tighter switchbacks vs before; drive it and confirm the car localises to the correct span throughout (no airborne spawn, no teleport, spawn on the start line). A/B the acute budget with TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_ACUTE_DEG=80 (old behaviour) vs 88 (new). Check log/race.log for the one-line 'heading budget spine=80deg acute=88deg -> adjacent_skip=N' at generation. Regression: generation must still deliver the full requested span count (no 'boxed in ... ending track early' warning) on several seeds.

summary: Top-gear fix: 8 cars can finally reach their own top speed (cops excluded)
detail: [TOPGEAR REACHABILITY FIX 2026-08-20] Separate bug fix carved out of the gearbox rework at the user's request -- NOT part of the manual-only reward; it applies to every driver and every AI, EXCEPT police cars (see exclusion below). SYMPTOM: 10 of the 77 shipped cars are geared so that TOP gear hits the rev limiter BELOW their own authored top-speed rating (carparam+0x74), so the car could never reach the top speed its own stats claim, regardless of who drove it or how well. Drive torque is hard-zeroed above redline-50, so the limiter wins. MEASURED ceiling/rating: chr 0.90, cp2 0.90, lit 0.90, flx 0.91, nis 0.91, pwr 0.92, cp3 0.96, mgt 0.96, cob 0.98, mcj 0.98 -- i.e. the Dodge Charger, Shelby Cobra 427SC, Mustang LX 5.0, Mustang 428CJ, Mustang Saleen S351, F150 Lightning, Plymouth Prowler, Hot Dog, and BOTH cop cars (cp2 = Charger cop car, cp3 = Mustang cop car). POLICE EXCLUDED (user decision): cp2/cp3 (roster 47/48) are TD6 police cars, and giving a pursuing cop +11.7%/+4.1% top speed would silently re-balance Cop Chase on top of the existing TD5RE_COPCHASE_AI_SPEED_PCT 70% suspect debuff -- a correctness fix must not move a mode's difficulty. So 8 of the 10 are fixed and the 2 police cars keep their authored (unreachable) rating. Excluded by CAR IDENTITY, not cop ROLE, so a police car behaves consistently instead of changing gearing when a chase starts. Exclusion uses the NEW shared query td5_game_car_index_is_cop_car() (roster 33-36 TD5 + 46-49 TD6), hoisted in td5_game.c because the ranges were previously spelled out inline in the Cop Chase car-forcing loop AND again as frontend_car_is_cop() in td5_frontend.c (frontend-private, unreachable from leaf modules); the game.c inline copy was refactored to call it, the frontend copy was left alone to keep scope tight but MUST stay in agreement. Per-slot car identity via the new td5_game_get_slot_car_index(). Both declared in td5_game.h and mirrored into td5_race_state.h per that header's subset rule. FIX (td5_physics_effective_gear_ratio, knob TD5RE_TOPGEAR_FIX default 1): in TOP gear only, clamp the ratio to the tallest value that still reaches the authored rating -- ratio <= (redline-400)*4096/(rating*45). Ratio drops at most 10.4%; top speed rises 2.0%..11.7%, which is exactly the figure the carparam always advertised. SCOPE: no-op for the other 67 cars and for the 2 police cars (the clamp does not trigger), so their pacing and every AI assumption built on them is bit-unchanged. Runs BEFORE the manual top-gear stretch so the two compose: reachability first, earned bonus on top. DESIGN NOTE worth keeping: uses the RAW authored rating via PHYS_S(0x74), deliberately NOT phys_top_speed_rating(), because that returns 0x7FFF for a CHASING COP and also folds in MP catch-up and arcade-nitro multipliers -- using it would make the gearing situational, unstable, and would have blown up the division for cop cars. Since two of the ten affected cars ARE cop cars, this mattered in practice, not just in theory. CONFIRM: drive each of the 8 fixed cars (roster indices 12 Cobra, 28 Hot Dog, 45 Charger, 53 Mustang LX, 58 Lightning, 61 Mustang 428CJ, 63 Saleen S351, 66 Prowler; e.g. --DefaultCar=45 is the clearest at +11.7%) on a long straight in AUTOMATIC and check the speedo now reaches the top speed shown on the car's stats screen, where before it plateaued 2-12% short. Regression: run a Cop Chase and confirm it is exactly as hard to escape as before (police gearing untouched); and pick any of the other 67 cars and confirm top speed and acceleration feel identical to before, and that AI pace in a normal race is unchanged.

summary: Gearbox rework + earned manual bonus up to +50%
detail: [GEARBOX REWORK 2026-08-20] TD5RE-only rework of gear behaviour plus a skill-based manual reward. (1) PER-GEAR SPEED CEILING: faithfully gear only scaled TORQUE (compute_drive_torque * ratio at carparam+0x2E) with no per-gear speed limit, so 2nd gear would pull to the car's absolute top speed given road -- the box never felt like a gearbox. Now every gear BELOW top gear tops out at the speed where that ratio hits the limiter, derived by inverting the RPM model (|spd>>8| at redline = (redline-400)*4096/(ratio*45)); the same inversion the over-limiter engine-brake path already used, now shared via td5_physics_gear_ceiling_speed so they cannot drift. TOP gear is deliberately EXEMPT so no car's real top speed is ever reduced. Knob TD5RE_GEAR_CEILING (default 1). (2) EARNED MANUAL BONUS: manual paid a flat +20% accel and top speed; it now pays +20% as a floor and up to TD5RE_MANUAL_MAX_PCT (default 50) EARNED by clean shifts. A green-band upshift adds 1 to a 0..5 streak (TD5RE_SHIFT_STREAK_LEN); a short-shift costs 2 and an over-rev money shift costs 3, so the ceiling must be maintained, not just reached once. Interpolates base..max and flows through the existing td5_physics_actor_manual_boost_q8 chokepoint, so BOTH drive torque and all three speed gates inherit it with no new call sites. Verdicts come from the pre-existing shift-timing band check in td5_input.c (same bands as the HUD arrow colours). Streak resets every race. (3) TOP-GEAR STRETCH -- the load-bearing finding: MEASURED all 77 shipped carparam.json files and the speed at which TOP gear hits the limiter is only a MEDIAN 1.10x the car's authored top-speed rating (min 0.90x, max 1.86x). Because drive is hard-zeroed above redline-50, that limiter -- not the cap -- is what actually stops the car. So 71/77 cars could not reach rating*1.5 and 53/77 could not even reach rating*1.2, meaning the PRE-EXISTING flat +20% manual boost was already inert on most of the roster, and 10/77 cars are limiter-bound BELOW their own authored top speed. Fix: in TOP gear only, a manual car's effective ratio is made TALLER by the bonus factor (td5_physics_effective_gear_ratio), exactly like a taller final drive -- lower revs at a given road speed, so the raised cap becomes reachable. Torque keeps the RAW ratio deliberately (the reward must not cost power). (4) CLUTCH BEAT: every manual shift, up or down and regardless of quality, now costs ~0.1s at 78% throttle (s_shift_dip_ticks) so shifts have weight; separate from and composing with the longer mistimed-shift bog. (5) AUTO-SHIFT HYSTERESIS: the faithful auto FSM re-decided every tick with no dwell and hunted between two gears on crests/part throttle. Added a 12-tick minimum dwell (TD5RE_AUTO_SHIFT_DWELL), scoped to the HUMAN-in-automatic slot ONLY -- AI and traffic keep the byte-faithful every-tick FSM on purpose, because the DRIVER AI model's pace was tuned against it (2026-08-18) and adding dwell there would silently re-tune every opponent. (6) HUD: live '+NN% ***--' readout under the rev counter showing the current bonus and streak pips, via td5_physics_shift_quality_hud_pct (-1 = nothing to show), so the reward is visible. NETPLAY CAVEAT: the streak is driven from the LOCAL input path but feeds physics every peer recomputes, which would desync -- so the EARNED half is gated on !td5_net_is_active() and a net race falls back to the flat base bonus (pure launch config, identical on every client). GOLDEN TRACES: gear/RPM live in the controls trace module and are golden-pinned for Moscow/Pelton/drag; this change moves controls + motion + pose hashes BY DESIGN and the goldens were re-recorded with it. CONFIRM BY DRIVING (this is feel work, it cannot be verified from a log): pick MANUAL in car select. (a) intermediate gears should now run out of puff and demand an upshift instead of pulling forever; (b) each shift should cost a perceptible beat; (c) shifting in the green band should walk the HUD bonus up from +20% toward +50% and make the car both pull and run noticeably harder in top gear; short-shifting or bouncing off the limiter should visibly give it back; (d) in AUTOMATIC, crest a hill at part throttle -- the box should no longer flip between two gears; (e) regression: an AUTOMATIC car's pace and the AI field's pace should feel unchanged.

summary: AUDI TT / MUSTANG COBRA / XJR-15 got real physics (were CERBERA clones)
detail: [DONOR-PARAM CARS 2026-08-20] TD6's param.zip ships NO <code>param.dat for aud, pro and xjr, so convert_td6_cars.py:379-395 fell back to the donor car's carparam wholesale (documented there as 'approximate physics', stamped [param=DONOR]; donor was tvr CERBERA). Result: FOUR roster slots -- tvr, aud, pro, xjr -- all drove as a CERBERA. pro was byte-identical to tvr in EVERY field; aud and xjr differed only in wheel_pos (0x40, which is 'live' so those two at least sat on their own wheelbase). VISIBLE SYMPTOM: the SELECT CAR spec sheets are authored from a separate table (convert_td6_cars.py TD6_STATS) and claimed a 40 mph / 2.5 s spread across these cars while the actual spread was ZERO -- an AUDI TT advertising 151mph/6.4s and a JAGUAR XJR-15 advertising 191mph/3.9s were the same car underneath. They also occupied four consecutive ranking rows sharing the identical tier score 0.31. FIX: 15 new rows in td5_carbalance.c k_overrides[] setting top_speed_limit, drive_torque_multiplier, collision_mass, brake_force and drag_coefficient per car. There is no value to RESTORE (the source data does not exist), so these are DERIVED from the only per-car intent that does exist: the config.nfo spec sheet (top speed mph, 0-60 s). Method = nearest neighbour in normalised (mph, 0-60) space over the 65 roster cars with genuine params, the three donor cars excluded so they cannot poison it. aud is an EXACT twin (distance 0.000) of att '1999_AUDI_TT_COUPE' -- literally the same car already on the roster with real TD6 params -- so aud's values are COPIED from att, which is correct. pro and xjr use an inverse-distance-weighted mean of their 5 nearest neighbours rather than copying the single closest car, so they get distinct values instead of becoming a fresh clone (which would just relocate the bug). A global least-squares fit was tried FIRST and REJECTED for two fields: lateral-G vs drag_coefficient came out R2=0.006 (no relationship; the lateral column has junk in it, e.g. sp4 claims an impossible 3.0G) and 60-0ft vs brake_force only reached R2=0.36. MEASURED RESULT: the four cars now score 0.376/0.148/0.146/0.563 instead of four identical 0.31; cars sharing a score with another car fell 11 -> 6. All 15 overrides verified firing in log/engine.log on the CAR SELECT screen. CONFIDENCE: top speed and torque well supported; brake_force is the noisiest field (R2=0.36) and is the first thing to revisit if these three brake oddly. All three moved off CERBERA's invmass 18 to the roster-typical 16, which via td5_physics_assists.c also shifts their hill-climbing and crash fly-away slightly. Confirm by DRIVING each: AUDI TT should feel clearly the slowest of the four and match att; MUSTANG COBRA modest; XJR-15 a genuine supercar. Regression check: CERBERA (tvr) itself must be UNCHANGED -- it is not in the override table.

summary: PITBULL mass fixed (had the traffic-vehicle value); tracked override layer
detail: [CAR BALANCE OVERRIDE LAYER 2026-08-20] NEW MODULE td5_carbalance.c/.h. PROBLEM 1 (infrastructure): per-car performance data lives in re/assets/cars/<code>/carparam.json, and NONE of it is tracked by git (0 of 77 car dirs are in the index), so any balance edit there is local-only -- unversioned, not LAN-deployed, lost on a fresh clone. This module is the tracked home for such corrections: a small k_overrides[] table applied to the 268-byte carparam image at load. HOOK POINT: td5_asset_open_and_read() was split into a static asset_open_and_read_raw() plus a thin wrapper that applies the table, because that function is the ONE choke point every carparam consumer shares (physics load, frontend MORE STATS, handling bar, AI speed pool, traffic top-speed lookup). That matters: td5_carparam.h's contract is that the display bars and the weight mechanics agree BY CONSTRUCTION, which only holds if every reader sees the same bytes. PROBLEM 2 (the data bug): sp8 PITBULL shipped collision_mass=32, which is the documented TRAFFIC inverse-mass override and is off the player/AI scale entirely (3..20, median 16). collision_mass is INVERSE mass (higher = lighter), and the accel proxy is torque*inv_mass, so 32 with the roster's max torque (180) gave an accel score of 5760 vs a roster median of 1248 -- 4.6x the median, 2x the next car, and the sole reason the roster's accel spread was 17.45x. Corrected to TD5CP_INVMASS_MAX (20), the lightest value any other player car legitimately uses (COBRA). MEASURED: accel 5760 -> 3600, spread 17.45x -> 10.91x, Pitbull still leads the next cluster (3 cars at 2880) by 25% so it remains the reward car. KNOB TD5RE_CAR_BALANCE, default ON, set 0 for raw asset values. Both paths verified in-game via log/engine.log: ON logs 'carbalance: sp8 off=0x88 32 -> 20', OFF logs nothing. NOT corrected (judged authored character, not data errors): nis HOT DOG invmass 3, sp2 WAGON 8, day DAYTONA 11 -- the rest of the roster is coherent (16 typical, 12 muscle, 18..20 light sports). IMPORTANT SIDE EFFECT TO WATCH: mass no longer feeds only the V2V impulse -- td5_physics_assists.c wired it into uphill decel, accel power-to-weight and crash fly-away, so Pitbull's hill-climbing and crash behaviour change too, not just its acceleration. Confirm by DRIVING Pitbull: it should still feel clearly the quickest car but no longer cartoonishly so; check it climbs hills sanely and does not get launched unusually far in a crash. Regression check: any other car must be bit-identical (only sp8 is in the table).

summary: Every car gets a SLOW/NORMAL/FAST class (was 56% unclassified)
detail: [CAR SPEED TIER PARTITION 2026-08-20] frontend_build_speed_tiers() (td5_fe_carstats.c) assigned classes by three NARROW rank windows with the two extremes dropped: SLOW = next K slowest, FAST = next K fastest, AVG = K around the median, K = max(9, 15% of roster). MEASURED on the live roster: 68 scored non-cop cars, K=10, so only 30 cars got a class and 38 (56%) stayed at tier -1. The sole consumer, the MP simultaneous car-select deal (td5_fe_race.c:1758), therefore missed most of the roster and fell through to its nearest-to-class-centre fallback, which kept dealing the same handful of cars. FIX: the DEFAULT is now a full three-way PARTITION by rank (b1=n/3, b2=2n/3) so every scored car gets exactly one class; live roster splits 22/23/23. The legacy narrow windows are preserved and still reachable by setting TD5RE_HOST_TIER_CARS explicitly. Verified offline for every roster size n=5..76: no unclassified car, no empty class, no overlap, and each class holds >=9 cars from n=27 up (the 2026-06-29 floor). Cop cars stay excluded. NOT changed: frontend_speed_band_for_tier / s_speed_pool_ids (a separate top-speed thirds split used by MP setup) and the per-car carparam values themselves. Confirm in game: MP simultaneous car-select, deal several SLOW/NORMAL/FAST picks -> the variety of cars offered per class should be visibly wider than before, and no class should ever come up empty. Regression check: single-player car select and its stat bars must look unchanged.

summary: Net cop chase activates all N players (was capped at 2)
detail: [NET COP CHASE FIELD 2026-08-20] Cop Chase over the network shipped in Phase 2b (72f8713a, 2026-07-04) and works for 2 players, but a 3+ player online cop chase silently activated only TWO cars. ROOT CAUSE: td5_game_mp_cop_chase_field() bailed with `|| g_td5.network_active -> return 0`; that 0 fed two places -- slot activation (td5_game.c:2801: keep=field, if<=0 keep=2 -> slots 2..5 forced DISABLED) and racer count (:2982: g_racer_count = field>0?field:2). So every net cop chase collapsed to the faithful 2-slot wanted field regardless of how many players joined. FIX (td5_game.c:11281, port-only, TD5RE-only): drop the network_active clause; for net return td5_net_get_player_count() (all racers are human net players -- num_human_players is forced to 1 locally -- and cops are drawn from them since net forces cop_is_ai=0). DETERMINISM: net_get_player_count() is replicated roster state, identical on every peer, so slot activation stays in lockstep; the random-cop draw was already net-safe (private xorshift on the replicated rng_seed, not shared CRT rand). Audit found NO non-deterministic sim input in the cop-chase path (arrest/damage are pure physics; the only rand()&7 is a cosmetic HUD 'wanted message' index). NOT in scope (deliberate deferrals from Phase 2b, still local-only): INFECT over net, manual host-chosen cop roles (net forces random cop), and the COPS/SUSPECTS results-screen layout. Confirm with TWO+ instances/machines: host a net COP CHASE with 3-4 players -> ALL of them spawn and race (before this, only 2 cars appeared); one is the cop (random), rest are suspects; arrests/HUD/minimap cop markers work for every active slot. Regression check: a 2-player net cop chase, and LOCAL split-screen cop chase, must behave exactly as before.

summary: Net play protocol version gate + custom-track identity check
detail: [NET PROTO PHASE 0 2026-08-19] Groundwork so netplay feature work can change the wire format safely, plus a real fix for a silent custom-track desync. (1) NEW TD5_NET_PROTO_VERSION (=1) in td5_net.h, stamped into DiscoveryMsg.proto_version (appended LAST so a pre-versioning v0 peer's shorter packet still parses and gets a real JOIN_NAK instead of being dropped on a size check and spinning until timeout) and into TD5_NetRaceConfig.proto_version. Host checks it in ws2_accept_join BEFORE the password/capacity gates and replies JOIN_NAK reason 3 (WS2_NAK_VERSION); the joiner's screen now reads COULD NOT CONNECT: DIFFERENT GAME VERSION instead of a generic timeout. TD5_NetRaceConfig grew 428 -> 436 bytes, static assert bumped in step. (2) NEW TD5_NetRaceConfig.track_fingerprint + td5_net_track_fingerprint(): custom track slots (37+) are per-machine (each peer has its own custom_tracks.json), so the same track_index could load a DIFFERENT track on each side and desync instantly with no error. Host stamps the fingerprint of the track it picked; clients recompute from their own registry on DXPSTART and REFUSE to start (td5_net_get_start_reject_reason) rather than run a guaranteed-desync race, showing 'The host is racing a track you do not have'. Native/cup/TD6 slots hash the index alone (compiled-in tables, so index == identity). SCOPE LIMIT: the fingerprint covers the manifest ENTRY (level/name/circuit/start+finish span), NOT the level file contents -- two peers with matching manifests but differently-edited geometry are still NOT caught. KNOWN GAP: if a client refuses the start, the host is not told and sits in the lockstep barrier until its own timeout; wiring a refusal message back is follow-up work. Confirm with TWO machines/instances: (a) same build, native track -> joins and races exactly as before (no regression); (b) same build, a custom track present on host only -> client refuses with the track message instead of desyncing; (c) mismatched builds (bump TD5_NET_PROTO_VERSION on one) -> join is refused at the lobby with DIFFERENT GAME VERSION.

summary: Car horn: smooth distance falloff + no longer detunes a nearby car's engine
detail: [HORN AUDIO 2026-08-20] Two confirmed defects in the horn playback block (td5_sound.c td5_sound_update_audio_mix): it referenced horn_slot+1 for both the finished-poll and the per-frame slot_modify. Slots are 3 per vehicle (Drive, Rev, Horn) so horn_slot+1 is the NEXT vehicle's LOOPING Drive.wav (or the Rain ambient loop for the last car): (a) that neighbour loop is always playing, so the horn state never reset to 0 and re-armed cleanly; (b) once running, every frame it wrote the horn's volume/pan/22050Hz onto that neighbour car's engine loop, audibly detuning it. FIX: poll and modify the horn's OWN slot (drop the +1). Also replaced the inline volume formula (scaled by 0x1000 then clamped >=0x80 to 0x7F -- effectively full until ~15872 units then a cliff to 0) with sound_attenuate_volume(0x7F, dist), the same linear falloff the engine and siren use. RUNTIME-VERIFIED via control-socket hold_action horn on Moscow: horn arms, buffer loads (Horn.wav 19288 bytes), slot_play fires at full vol, DirectSound plays it (channel play, steal=0 fail=0) -- the audio chain was already sound; these were the real latent bugs. NOT confirmed: whether the user's own keypress reaches the horn (headless key-inject can't test focus-gated input). Confirm by DRIVING: press horn (P1 = Right Ctrl, or L3 on a pad), it should sound and fade with distance; honk near another car and that car's engine pitch must NOT shift.

summary: Menu mouse double-click: no timeout + whole-button hit area
detail: [FRONTEND DBLCLICK 2026-08-19] Two reported inconsistencies in the default double-click-to-activate menu path (td5_frontend.c, PORT-ONLY, added 2026-06-15), both fixed. (1) TIMEOUT: the confirming click had to land within GetDoubleClickTime() (500ms system default) or it silently re-armed instead of activating -- if i take too long to press the second click it wont trigger menu change. The window is now UNBOUNDED by default (new knob TD5RE_MOUSE_DBLCLICK_MS: 0/unset=no timeout, N=N ms, negative=restore the Windows system interval); a stale arm cannot leak because activation also requires the button to still be the selected one AND frontend_reset_buttons() now clears s_dbl_last_button on every screen transition. (2) HIT AREA: the arrow-zone check (20px left/right edge strip of the ALREADY-SELECTED button, used for left/right value cycling) was evaluated BEFORE the double-click check, and that strip is exactly the region outside the green highlight box (drawn with insets inL=20/inR=22) -- so a second click anywhere but the green box was consumed as an arrow-cycle and the menu never changed (if i click outside the green square area it wont trigger either). The confirming click is now tested first and wins anywhere inside the button rect; repeated arrow cycling is unaffected because the arrow branch never arms the double-click. Confirm by MOUSE-DRIVING the frontend: (a) click a menu button once, wait 3+ seconds, click it again -- it must activate; (b) click once then click again on the far left/right edge of the button (outside the green box) -- it must activate, not cycle; (c) on an options row with left/right arrows, repeatedly clicking the edges of the already-selected row must still cycle the value as before.

summary: AUTO-GENERATED track: procedural road, walls CONFIRMED working
detail: [AUTOTRACK 2026-08-20 PHASE 1] New AUTO-GENERATED entry in the track selector (registry slot 60, level090, rebuilt with a fresh seed on EVERY race launch so no two races share a road). New module td5_trackgen.c ports the geometry+emitter half of re/tools/td5_trackgen.py to C: seeded section picker (straight / sweeping curve / sharp bend / widened multi-lane) -> centerline -> STRIP.DAT spans+shared vertex rows, LEFT/RIGHT.TRK routes, LEVELINF.DAT. No Python, no runtime deps. Knobs: TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_SEED (pin the seed to reproduce a track), _SPANS, _LANES, _ELEVATION, _BLOCK, _PCT_STRAIGHT/_CURVE/_ACUTE/_DUAL. VERIFIED: walls contain the car (user-confirmed 2026-08-20); walls need no extra data, td5_track_resolve_wall_contacts builds rails from the span vertex indices the generator already writes. Measured on pinned seed 123456789: wall_clear sane 100% of ticks, span walk monotonic with zero jumps, wheels grounded 90% at rest / 94% driving. IMPORTANT LESSON RECORDED IN THE COMMITS: the race-trace column formerly called wheel_mask is actor+0x37C, an AIRBORNE mask (bit set = wheel OFF the ground) reached via the misnamed actor->damage_lockout; it is now emitted as airborne_mask. Reading it as a contact mask caused a vertex-row winding flip and a grade cut that together produced an oscillating span walker, negative wall_clear and the car falling into void. Both were reverted; the generator was substantially correct as first written. Confirm: (a) AUTO-GENERATED appears in the selector for every non-drag game type and not in drag; (b) each race is a different road (race.log trackgen seed= differs per launch); (c) car spawns on the road, level, facing down-track; (d) you cannot drive off the sides. VERIFIED 2026-08-20: the P2P FINISH FIRES correctly (log 'Actor finish: slot=0 mode=td6-p2p raw=1796 norm=1796 finish=1796', player placed 2nd behind an AI) - the registry finish_span feeds td5_asset_td6_finish_span_for_level, no code change was needed; earlier claims that it did not fire were untested, the car had only ever reached span ~46 of 1800. Opt-in scenery via TD5RE_AUTOTRACK_SCENERY=1 gives a TEXTURED asphalt road with dashed lane markings (MODELS.DAT road mesh + 1-page TEXTURES.DAT), default OFF. KNOWN GAPS: no buildings/tunnels/bridges/biomes yet, no sky texture, and the hill profile (TD5_TG_MAX_GRADE 0.12) has never been validated with a correct airborne metric.

summary: CONTROL OPTIONS: standard row spacing + PLAYER limited to connected controllers
detail: [CONTROL OPTIONS 2026-08-19] Two user-reported issues on the CONTROL OPTIONS screen (14). (1) SPACING: the rows sat on an 80px pitch (y=97/177/257), double every other options screen; the shared standard is base y=97 step 40 (OPTIONS hub, GRAPHICS OPTIONS, SOUND OPTIONS, RACE MENU all use it) with OK on the y=377 footer. Rows are now 97/137/177 (td5_fe_menu.c Screen_ControlOptions); the overlay's CONTROLLER row moved 177->137 to match (td5_frontend.c frontend_render_control_options_overlay: icon quad y and the wrapped device-name block first_y 185->145). The arrows are drawn by button INDEX (fe_draw_option_arrows) so they follow the rects automatically. (2) PLAYER GATING: the selector ranged 1..9 regardless of what was plugged in, so you could configure a PLAYER 5 with no device. It is now capped by the CONNECTED device count. IMPORTANT this is NOT a revert of the earlier fix that removed a cap at the JOYSTICK count -- that cap was wrong because with N pads you could only reach PLAYER N, breaking keyboard+pads setups. The cap here counts the keyboard as the device it is (device 0, player 1 only) plus each non-lost pad, so N pads reach PLAYER N+1; unplugged-but-still-enumerated pads are excluded with td5_plat_input_device_is_lost (the same predicate the MP lobby panes use). s_num_human_players is kept as a FLOOR so a player already in the race stays configurable if their pad drops mid-session. Recomputed on every screen entry (existing hot-swap path). Confirm: (a) CONTROL OPTIONS rows look evenly spaced like SOUND/GRAPHICS OPTIONS, arrows + device icon + device name all line up with their rows; (b) with NO pad plugged in the PLAYER selector will not move off 1; (c) with 1 pad it reaches PLAYER 2; with 2 pads PLAYER 3; (d) unplug a pad, re-enter the screen, and the range shrinks. Log line to check: frontend.log 'ControlOptions: devices=N connected=N humans=N range=1..N'.

summary: LIGHTING OPTIONS: CAR LIGHTS row turns off car-emitted light (LOW + HIGH)
detail: [GFXOPT 2026-08-19] New [Lighting]CarLights (default 1, --CarLights=N) plus LIGHTING OPTIONS row 8 CAR LIGHTS. OFF makes vehicle headlight spots never enter the dynamic light registry (gated per-slot in td5_light_headlights_active_for_slot, td5_light.c), so it strips car lighting cost in BOTH the LOW screen-space light pass and the HIGH RT light path. Street lamps and brake-light billboards are deliberately unaffected. Applies live via td5_light_set_car_lights and persists through td5_ini_persist_options. Confirm: race at night or in a tunnel with CAR LIGHTS ON - the road ahead of each car is lit; set OFF - no light pool from any car, street lamps still lit, brake lights still red; the setting survives a restart.

summary: SP cop chase suspect count follows OPPONENTS (1-5), was hardcoded 1
detail: [SP COP CHASE FIELD 2026-08-20, PORT ENHANCEMENT] User: ''I have not seen more than 1 opponent''. Confirmed NOT a bug: SP cop chase hardcoded a 2-car field (1 player-cop + 1 AI suspect) and ignored the OPPONENTS row entirely -- faithful to the original [CONFIRMED @ InitializeRaceActorRuntime 0x00432E60: if (g_selectedGameType != 0) g_racerCount = 2; slots 2..5 disabled @ InitializeRaceSession 0x0042AB91]. User chose to make it configurable. NEW shared helper td5_game_cop_chase_field() (td5_game.c, declared in td5_game.h) is now the single source of truth for the cop-chase field: MP cop chase returns exactly what td5_game_mp_cop_chase_field() did (UNCHANGED), SP returns 1 + clamp(num_ai_opponents, 1, 5). Both the game-side s_slot_state disable loop AND the AI-side g_slot_state mirror in td5_ai_init_race_state now call it, so the two slot tables can no longer drift (they were duplicated literals before). Bounds rationale: minimum 1 suspect because OPPONENTS=0 would leave the cop alone on the track; maximum 5 (field 6) because the cap is load-bearing -- g_traffic_slot_base only stays 6 while g_racer_count <= 6, and a >6-racer field pushes traffic to slot 16 and force-disables traffic/cops since the cop subsystem is hardwired to the 6+6 layout. So OPPONENTS=5 gives a full 6-car chase, which is also the original maximum grid. Default behaviour with OPPONENTS=0 or 1 is byte-identical to before (field=2). VERIFIED: --DefaultGameType=8 --DefaultOpponents=5 logs ''Cop Chase: active field=6 (1 cop + 5 suspect(s))'' with the AI mirror agreeing (g_slot_state[6..]=3), and actors_rendered rose from 2 to 6-7. Confirm by DRIVING: set OPPONENTS to 3-5 on the race-setup screen, start a police chase, and check that many suspect cars spawn, all drive, each can be rammed/arrested independently, POINTS/arrest tallies are per-suspect, and the results screen lists them all.

summary: Police chase: traffic is no longer treated as a suspect (chase arrow/points)
detail: [COP CHASE TRAFFIC GATE DRIFT 2026-08-20] User report: ''when I crash into traffic I see the chase indicator, traffic should not be changed''. CONFIRMED from the user run log: wanted_first_hit fired for suspect=7, 8 and 10 in an SP cop chase whose field was only 2 (slot 0 cop + slot 1 suspect, slots 2..5 disabled) -- i.e. TRAFFIC actors. ROOT CAUSE: td5_game_cop_chase_is_suspect()/is_cop() bounded the slot by TD5_MAX_RACER_SLOTS, which was 6 when those gates were written but the N-way racer work raised it to 16, while the runtime racer/traffic boundary g_traffic_slot_base stays 6 for a legacy <=6-racer field. Traffic actors live at slot_index 6..69 and 6..15 alias into every racer-sized array (g_wanted_damage_state[16], g_wanted_hit_tick[16]), so is_suspect() (which returns !is_cop) said YES for civilian cars. The V2V hook in td5_physics_collision.c passes raw actor slot_index values, so ramming traffic ran the whole wanted chain: hit-tick stamp -> chase arrow + random WANTED banner, damage-bar drain, +10/20 pts and even a bogus arrest (+50) credited to the player. Exact same drift class as the documented 2026-06-12 traffic-WHEEL gate fix in td5_render_mesh.c. FIX at 4 sites, all switching the stale constant to the runtime boundary: (1) td5_game_cop_chase_is_suspect + is_cop -> slot >= g_traffic_slot_base rejected (root cause); (2) td5_ai_wanted_cop_hit validates both its cop and suspect indices the same way (defense in depth -- it is the only place that mutates wanted damage/score); (3) td5_render_mesh.c wanted damage-indicator call + wanted-smoke gate now use the is_racer local that already existed in that loop (a traffic car could also emit the wanted-target smoke trail); (4) td5_hud_update_wanted_damage_indicator internal gate. Confirm: SP cop chase (--DefaultGameType=8 --Cops=1) -- ram several TRAFFIC cars: NO cyan arrow / bust bar / WANTED banner over them, POINTS must not increase, no arrest; then ram the real suspect (slot 1) and the arrow, bar drain, points and arrest must all still work exactly as before. Also check MP cop chase multi-cop still credits each cop.

summary: Police chase: siren starts AFTER the countdown (with the lights)
detail: [COP CHASE SIREN COUNTDOWN GATE 2026-08-19] User report: in police chase the siren was audible on the start grid but no flashing lights were visible. Root cause found by reading both paths: the strobe is drawn every frame but its brightness IS its phase counter (td5_render_effects.c render_tracked_actor_marker: alpha = sin(phase*-4), submitted ADDITIVE, so phase 0 = additive black = invisible), and the phase only advances on a NON-paused sim tick (td5_game.c per-non-paused-tick block, td5_vfx_advance_tracked_marker_phases) -- the whole countdown runs in the paused branch. The siren SOUND, by contrast, runs from frame_audio_tick() on every rendered frame including the countdown. So sound and lights were decoupled. FIX (both siren drivers): (1) the cop-chase horn siren in td5_sound_update_vehicle_looping_state() now also requires !td5_game_is_countdown_active(); (2) the PORT-ONLY POLICE-option traffic-cop siren call in frame_audio_tick() treats countdown like pause (explicit td5_sound_stop_tracked_vehicle_audio) -- needed because td5_ai_tick() runs during the countdown so a cop can already be COP_CHASING before the green light. Covers SP and MP (incl. MP cop chase where the cop siren defaults ON) since both drivers are shared. Confirm: start a police chase race (Cops on / MP COP CHASE) -- grid + countdown must be SILENT with no cop lights, then on the green light the siren and the red/blue strobe must start TOGETHER; horn still toggles both mid-race; pause still silences it.

summary: Drag traffic dry-up ROOT CAUSE fixed: wrecks now retired (SP + MP)
detail: [DRAG TRAFFIC DRY-UP 2026-08-19] Tester localised it as TEMPORAL (''dries up after a fixed time, anywhere on the strip''), which ruled out the finite-strip theory. A new periodic traffic census showed the mechanism: pool pinned at the cap while the BROKEN-DOWN count climbed monotonically (tick 900 active=16 broken=5, tick 1050 active=16 broken=6) -- ~1 permanent wreck every 5s. Drag traffic is oncoming and gets destroyed constantly; broken-down cars stay ACTIVE forever and eat the pool until nothing can spawn. Constant rate = death after a fixed TIME regardless of position. No distance despawn arm can help (wrecks sit where they died). ROOT CAUSE: the wreck-retirement arm was gated on td5_game_battle_mode_active(), though its own comment says it is what frees slots so fresh traffic keeps coming. SAME bug shape as the earlier battle-gated rear-despawn fix -- one was fixed and its sibling missed. FIX: (battle || g_td5.drag_race_enabled), inheriting the existing 300-tick/~10s default and the TD5RE_BATTLE_WRECK_DESPAWN(_TICKS) knobs. MEASURED before->after (same 2-min SP drag): peak broken climbing monotonically -> 4 then recovering to 0; active at tick 1650 pinned 16 -> 15 with fadeout=1; spawns 66 -> 79. Confirm by driving a LONG drag race (and an MP drag): oncoming traffic must keep arriving for the entire race, with no point where it permanently stops. Watch also for wrecked cars vanishing ~10s after they break (that is the new retirement, not a bug).

summary: Drag traffic no longer starves after the first wave (SP + MP)
detail: [DRAG TRAFFIC STARVATION 2026-08-19] Tester: traffic spawns one wave in a drag race then STOPS forever; suspected in MP drag too - CONFIRMED, the defect is mode-wide and pre-existing for MP. ROOT CAUSE: drag traffic is ONCOMING, so it sweeps past the player in seconds and parks behind them, but NO despawn arm could retire it, so every slot stayed ACTIVE and the spawn cap gate never reopened. Each arm verified individually: (a) the legacy rear rule (behind < -traffic_dyn_despawn) is gated on !trf_perplayer_cap_enabled(), and td5_env_flag_on returns 1 unless the var is literally ''0'' -- so it is DEAD in every default run; (b) `ahead > front_keep` can never fire because oncoming cars move DOWN the span axis, so ahead only grows more negative; (c) the two remaining arms need separation > front_keep, whose default floor is ~228 spans (128*1.6+24); (d) circuit/ring-wrap paths are inert on a point-to-point strip; (e) the 50-span passed-traffic despawn that WOULD fix it was gated on td5_game_battle_mode_active(). FIX: that arm is now (battle || g_td5.drag_race_enabled) -- one condition, covers SP and MP drag. `behind` is sp - trailing-player span, so a passed oncoming car goes increasingly negative and the arm fires. MEASURED A/B (90 s SP drag, 5 opponents, traffic on; pre-fix emulated via TD5RE_BATTLE_DESPAWN_BEHIND=100000): WITH fix = 8 recycle/fade-out events, 0 starvation warnings, spawns continuing into the last decile of the run; WITHOUT = 1 recycle event, 2 ''traffic_dyn_starved: 30 consecutive spawn failures'' warnings, zero spawns after decile 6. Confirm by DRIVING a drag race for a while (and an MP drag): oncoming traffic should keep arriving for the whole run instead of drying up after the opening wave.

detail: [SP DRAG OPPONENTS/TRAFFIC 2026-08-19] SP drag had no opponent, lane or traffic control anywhere (field was pinned at 2; g_td5.ini.drag_traffic was read by nothing). Added: (a) RO_OPPONENTS is now shown for SP drag (still hidden for MP drag, which has no AI) and the count DEFINES THE LANE COUNT -- td5_game_drag_field_size() sizes the SP field as 1 human + num_ai_opponents, and that same value drives the road widener AND the per-lane car fill, so lanes and cars cannot disagree.
