summary: DRIVER AI experimental racing line (opt-in, TD5RE_AI_DRIVER_LINE=1): +27-29%% twisty pace
detail: [AI DRIVER MODEL C2+C3 2026-08-19] New OPT-IN out-in-out racing line for the DRIVER AI, DEFAULT OFF (LINE=0 is byte-identical to the shipped centre-line behavior; zero regression). td5_ai_driver.c: (C2) a per-span lateral line computed by minimum-curvature elastic-band relaxation between the rails (projected Gauss-Seidel, clamped LINE_MARGIN off each rail), fed into BOTH the steering aim point AND the corner-speed curvature; (C3) the corner cap is now the physically-grounded v~sqrt(R): cap=sqrt(R_line/RREF) using the actual line radius, which matches a holdable speed instead of the old 1-loss*sharp over-estimate; plus a tight-corner blend (LINE_RLO) that ramps the apex back to centre on hairpins. Knobs: TD5RE_AI_DRIVER_LINE (0/1), _RREF (34000), _LINE_MARGIN (14), _LINE_RLO (10000), + a per-race STATS diag (TD5RE_AI_DRIVER_STATS: sat%%/wall%%/meanv). MEASURED (fixed-seed lone-car A/B, mean lspd vs CLASSIC, LINE=1 RREF=34000): Tokyo 0.59->0.76x (+29%%), Kyoto 0.64->0.81x (+27%%), Newcastle 0.87->0.94x, Sydney 0.84->0.90x, Moscow 0.78->0.83x, BlueRidge 0.57->0.58x -- all clean at RREF=34000. WHY OPT-IN not default: RREF=34000 is a KNIFE-EDGE for one Newcastle corner (span 744 spins/stalls at RREF 30000 AND 38000 but is clean at 34000), so it is not robust enough to default-on; making it robust needs targeted work on that corner (per-corner speed/line, not a global knob). GOTCHA fixed mid-build: the LINE flag was inverted (used !td5_env_flag_off which returns 1 for '1'), so early A/B ran with the line OFF -- caught by the 'path table built line=N' log. Confirm (opt-in): race with TD5RE_AI_DRIVER_LINE=1 on Tokyo/Kyoto -- opponents carry noticeably more corner speed, stay on the road; and with LINE unset (default) behavior is unchanged. Full --SelfTestSuite=1 green at the default.

summary: Selftest 'peak jump>8000' WARNs eliminated (were a spawn artifact, not AI crest launches)
detail: [AI DRIVER MODEL followup-b 2026-08-19] Investigated the ~6 selftest 'peak jump>8000' soft WARNs, believed to be DRIVER cars catching air over crests. MEASUREMENT DISPROVED that: the invariant sampler's peak_jump is the running max per-sample |world_pos delta|, and the big jump is at t=0 / span=110 / longitudinal_speed=0 -- i.e. the car STATIONARY on the start grid. The first sample catches world_pos.y ~= 0 (actor not yet positioned), the next catches the real spawn elevation, so the 'jump' is just the SEED->spawn transition and its magnitude is the track's spawn elevation (Newcastle ~21846, Moscow ~3174 render units); every genuine in-race vertical delta is <=126. So it was a selftest measurement artifact, NOT a launch -- a prototype anticipatory crest-easing speed cap left Newcastle's 21846 completely unchanged, confirming no speed change is involved. FIX (td5_selftest.c only, dev/QA harness -- compiled out of RELEASE, zero gameplay/sim/determinism impact): gate the peak_jump accumulation (and teleport FAIL) on the slot actually MOVING (longitudinal_speed > 0x800), so the one-off stationary spawn-placement delta is not counted while genuine at-speed launches and mid-race teleports still are. VERIFIED: full --SelfTestSuite=1 now reports 0 'peak jump' WARNs (was 6), no new FAILs, exit 0 (one run hit the pre-existing flaky nvwgf2um teardown Present crash exit 139; a clean re-run confirmed it is environmental, not this change). Confirm: run pwsh scripts/selftest.ps1 -Suite full and check the report shows no 'peak jump' WARN rows and still PASSes.

summary: DRIVER AI twisty-track pace: less conservative on Blue Ridge/Tokyo/Kyoto
detail: [AI DRIVER MODEL followup-a 2026-08-19] The P6 authored-speed feed used LEFT.TRK byte[2] as a fraction of top speed (hint/255). But byte[2] is NOT a speed -- in the faithful path it is a forward-track-component (fwd_comp) brake-onset THRESHOLD (rescaled threshold*0x400/0xFF, compared to g_actor_forward_track_component, never to longitudinal_speed). So hint/255 systematically UNDER-read corner speed, and the hard min(authored,curvature) dragged whole twisty laps: fixed-seed lone-car A/B measured DRIVER at 0.53-0.63x CLASSIC mean speed on Blue Ridge/Tokyo/Kyoto, coasting/braking 47-70%% of the lap. Pure curvature (TD5RE_AI_DRIVER_NOROUTE=1) is faster but UNSTABLE (selftest crash exit 139; stalls the car on Blue Ridge) -- authored is still needed for stability. The under-read is roughly uniform across corners (per-span dump: ~45%% of spans have authored<geometry, spread widely), so the fix lifts every authored cap a fixed fraction TOWARD the geometry estimate: cap = geo - (geo-authored)*ROUTE_PULL, new knob TD5RE_AI_DRIVER_ROUTE_PULL (1.0=old hard min, 0.0=geometry-only). Default 0.70, tuned by A/B sweep + full selftest: pulls <=0.6 stall Blue Ridge / crash the selftest, 0.70 is the safe floor. RESULT (fixed-seed A/B, mean lspd vs CLASSIC): Blue Ridge 0.56->0.62x, Tokyo 0.53->0.62x, Kyoto 0.63->0.68x (+11-17%% relative); guard tracks Moscow -2%%, Sydney/Newcastle unchanged; full --SelfTestSuite=1 still green (exit 0). Confirm by DRIVING Blue Ridge/Tokyo/Kyoto: opponents should carry more speed through the corners (less coasting) yet still stay on the road, not spin/stall; and Moscow/Sydney/Newcastle should feel the same as before. NOTE still slower than CLASSIC on the twistiest tracks -- closing that fully needs a controller/line rework, not just this speed-cap knob.

summary: Billboard trees render SOLID over houses behind them + no black top-edge line
detail: [FOLIAGE OCCLUSION 2026-08-17] Two user-reported bugs on billboard trees: (1) trees did not occlude houses/scenery BEHIND them -- the background blended through the canopy and houses drawn later painted over the tree; (2) a dark/black line along the top edge of the 2D tree textures. Root cause of (1): the foliage-AA feature promoted type-1 tree billboards to TRANSLUCENT_ANISO = alpha BLEND with z-write OFF, so they wrote no depth and were unsorted. Fix: new TD5_PRESET_FOLIAGE_CUTOUT (td5_types.h/td5_platform_win32.c) = alpha-TESTED OPAQUE, blend OFF, z-write ON, alpha_ref 0x80; td5_render_mesh.c routes billboard type-1 to it; the wrapper foliage-AA gate (d3d12_backend.c) gains a !blend&&z_write clause so the sampler still runs (type-2 clause byte-identical, unchanged). Shader (ps_common.hlsli): SampleFoliageAA keeps LOD-footprint dither-merge + alpha-weighted RGB (kills the black top-edge fringe); ApplyFogAndAlphaTest tests foliage HARD at 0.25 (merged-dither fills solid, stable, writes depth) instead of the old soft 1/255 blend threshold. Gated by TD5RE_FOLIAGE_AA (=0 = old hard cutout). Shared preset -> affects EVERY track billboard (trees/signs/banners). Confirm: (1) Blue Ridge (--DefaultTrack=3) idle at grid -> both corner trees are SOLID, occlude the houses/hills behind, no see-through canopy, no black top line; (2) SF (11) hillside trees occlude the city behind; (3) START banners/signs still render solid and legible; (4) thin fences (SF/Keswick) not dissolved; (5) selftest --SelfTest=1 passes.

summary: DRIVER AI multi-track robustness rework: authored corner speeds + traffic + wall escape
detail: [AI DRIVER MODEL P6 2026-08-18] Drive-test + A/B across many tracks exposed that the curvature-only speed heuristic overfit (great on Newcastle, but on twisty/hilly tracks the car entered corners too fast, SPUN and lost ~10-30%% of the race to recovery, and on Blue Ridge launched off crests). Root fix: DRIVER now seeds its per-corner speed profile from the AUTHORED route data (new td5_ai_route_speed_hint() in td5_ai.c reads LEFT.TRK byte[2], the same designer-tuned speeds the faithful AI uses to drive every track well), capped by the geometry estimate -- min(authored, curvature) -- so whichever is more conservative wins (authored catches corners geometry misjudges e.g. Blue Ridge; geometry catches corners where authored is too hot for the driver's line e.g. Newcastle). Also this session: aim at the ROAD CENTRE not the grid sub-lane (fixed Sydney outer-lane wall-grind 72%%->0), lateral line offset halved + hard-clamped inside the rails (fixed wall-leaning), METRIC forward-distance proximity replacing span-based (fixed 'not reactive to traffic' + won't crawl behind slow cars), fork_diverge=0 (stop clipping tight branch dividers), a wall-grind escape, and the steering-saturation brake DEFAULT-OFF (it crawled twisty tracks). New TD5RE_AI_DRIVER_NOROUTE=1 knob A/Bs the authored-speed feed off. New wall_clear column in the track trace + an A/B harness (scripts in scratchpad). VERIFIED (fixed seed, 6 tracks Moscow/Sydney/Newcastle/Tokyo/Kyoto/BlueRidge): ALL clean -- 0%% spins/stucks, wall <=1.3%%. Selftest --SelfTestSuite=1 = 52 PASS / 6 WARN / 0 FAIL (6 'peak jump>8000' soft warnings = cars catch a little air over crests; non-failing). KNOWN FOLLOW-UPS (not done): (a) DRIVER is conservative -- clean but slower than CLASSIC on the twistiest tracks; (b) the crest/airborne jump-WARNs need crest speed-easing to clear. Confirm by DRIVING several varied tracks incl. Blue Ridge/Tokyo: opponents should stay controlled through corners, not spin off or grind walls, and react to traffic.

summary: DRIVER AI cross-track sweep: two real bugs fixed (pace bootstrap + corner line-clip)
detail: [AI DRIVER MODEL P5 2026-08-17] Cross-track tuning sweep (Moscow/BlueRidge/Newcastle/SanFrancisco/Munich + TD6 circuit index 26 + TD6 index 32) surfaced two bugs introduced in P4 that the completion-based selftest missed: (1) PACE BOOTSTRAP: the P4 pace multiplier pushed eff_frac below the 0.97 straight-floor threshold, so the car stopped flooring before vmax reached true top speed -> vmax froze early (~56k vs ~200k) and every target capped to ~0.95*56k -> cars crawled (avg throttle 52/256, coasting 71%). This had regressed the P1 'beats Classic' result to SLOWER-than-Classic. FIX: the straight-floor now keys on the PROFILE fraction (min with the follow cap), not the persona-shaped value, so a clear straight is always flat-out and vmax always converges to true top; personality pace now shapes only the LIMITED (corner/following) target, which is more realistic (drivers differ in corner commitment, not top speed). (2) CORNER LINE-CLIP: the P3/P4 lateral line offset (line_bias) made a car run an off-centre line even through tight corners, clipping walls -- Newcastle 10.9%% wall / 4.9%% stuck / 49 spins, BlueRidge 4.7%%. FIX: the lateral offset (baseline + overtake) is now scaled by 'straightness' (from the profile frac) so cars run their preferred line on straights but converge to the racing line in tight corners. AFTER FIX (lone car): Newcastle 0.8%% wall / 0 stuck / 0 spins; BlueRidge 3.4%% (no spins/stuck); all other tracks <=1.6%%; Newcastle driver vs classic pace restored to +27%% (435 vs 343 dist/tick). Full selftest --SelfTest=1 --SelfTestSuite=1 = 58/58 PASS. Confirm by DRIVING across a spread of tracks incl. a tight one (Newcastle) and a TD6 track: opponents fast, on the racing line through corners, no wall-scraping.

summary: DRIVER AI personalities: per-driver pace/aggression/line/consistency + hidden catch-up
detail: [AI DRIVER MODEL P4 2026-08-17] Per-driver persona in td5_ai_driver.c, seeded DETERMINISTICALLY from (slot, difficulty_tier) via a hash -- NO CRT rand and NO race seed, so it is identical on every lockstep peer and replay by construction (slot+tier are replicated). skill scales pace (0.92..1.0) + corner speed; aggression sets how small a speed deficit triggers an overtake; consistency gates a small deterministic per-corner speed error (bucketed by span, hashed) so less-consistent drivers occasionally run wide / lock up; line_bias [-1,1] is the driver's preferred lane (replaces P3's static third-bias -> route variety). HIDDEN LEASH: a subtle catch-up boost (default max 3%%, TD5RE_AI_DRIVER_LEASH) applied to the TARGET speed of cars running behind (by race_position), never a raw throttle override -- replaces the old visible rubber-band for DRIVER cars (Classic CatchupAssist/SmartAILeash untouched). Pace shaping only applies AFTER vmax is established during the launch floor, so it can't stall the bootstrap. MEASURED: per-slot avg speed spreads widely (e.g. Moscow slot1 ~10.8k .. slot3 ~45k over the opening laps) and steering activity differs -> drivers visibly distinct. DETERMINISM VERIFIED: two identical Moscow runs produced byte-identical driver traces across all 2401 rows once the (inherently nondeterministic) render-frame index column is excluded. NOTE: MP-cup per-opponent difficulty override is NOT wired (needs td5_game.h, which the structure lint forbids the driver module to include); DRIVER uses the global tier. Branch variety is emergent from line_bias placing cars in different lanes at forks (not separately measured). Confirm by WATCHING a full DRIVER field: do cars have distinct pace/lines, make occasional believable mistakes, and do close races stay close without an obvious elastic-band?

summary: DRIVER AI racecraft: follow without rear-ending, overtake slower cars, spread the field
detail: [AI DRIVER MODEL P3 2026-08-17] Racecraft in td5_ai_driver.c (driver_racecraft): HYBRID proximity -- span ordering for reliable ahead/behind + a metric lateral projection (world velocity onto the car's right vector) for lane overlap the classic span-only search cannot see (a car one lane over). FOLLOWING: caps target speed to a slower car ahead scaled by the span gap so cars tuck in a length back instead of rear-ending. OVERTAKING: when faster with a clear side, commits a lateral aim-point offset to that side for a dwell (TD5RE_AI_DRIVER_OVERTAKE_TICKS) and keeps the speed -- real passes. HAZARD: a stopped/spun car ahead with no room -> hard slow (cap 0.25). FIELD SPREAD: a per-slot baseline lane bias (left/centre/right thirds) so six cars don't converge on one line and bunch/shove -- also the P3 stopgap for route variety (P4 replaces it with per-driver lines). STUCK recovery reworked to try steer-to-track + FORWARD first, reverse only if that fails (frees shove-offs faster). Knobs: TD5RE_AI_DRIVER_AHEAD_SPANS/PASS_FRAC/OFFSET_CLAMP/OVERTAKE_TICKS. MEASURED (5 AI opponents, Newcastle): position changes 2-6 per car (overtakes happen); STUCK dropped from 2 cars at 21-25%% to one at 6%%; every car ends NORMAL + moving (no permanent stick / pile-up); a real 178-degree spin was caught and recovered in ~1s (SPUN->NORMAL 27 ticks). Full selftest --SelfTestSuite=1 = 58/58 PASS with the whole field on DRIVER. KNOWN ROUGH EDGE: the static third-bias can push an outer-lane car wide on very tight corners (one car lost ground on Newcastle); P4 per-driver lines will refine this. Confirm by WATCHING a 5-6 car DRIVER race: do they race side-by-side and overtake cleanly without stacking into each other or getting stuck?

summary: DRIVER AI traction cap + spin/stuck recovery -- no opponents wedged for a whole race
detail: [AI DRIVER MODEL P2 2026-08-17] Added to td5_ai_driver.c: (1) TRACTION CAP -- backs off throttle when rear_axle_slip_excess exceeds a threshold so a power-on corner exit does not snap into a spin (knobs TD5RE_AI_DRIVER_SLIP_THRESH/SLIP_RANGE); (2) RECOVERY FSM (SPUN/STUCK) replacing racer_collision_escape for driver-owned cars -- SPUN = travelling backwards vs heading (coast + re-align with strong yaw damping, scrub a fast spin), STUCK = not moving after having launched (rock free: brief reverse toward the track aim, then full forward). summary: Thin alpha-tested fences (Keswick) draw at full distance again - no fade-out / near pop-in
detail: [KESWICK MIP REGRESSION 2026-08-10] The track-mipmap fix (see SF fence item) made thin alpha-keyed fences on Keswick (--DefaultTrack=10, level001 type-1 pages e.g. 356/316/323, 6-34%% opaque) FADE OUT at distance and only pop in when very close; TD5RE_TRACK_MIPS=0 drew them at full distance. Root cause: the per-mip coverage-preservation rescale allowed the alpha scale to drop BELOW 1.0. For type-1 pages (draw alpha_ref=1) box-filtering naturally GROWS coverage with distance (a thin wire's alpha blurs across more texels), so the rescale tried to SHRINK coverage back to the level-0 value -- and on discrete 0/255 alpha the coverage-vs-scale curve is a step function, so the binary search overshot and landed on a scale that zeroed the fence (coverage 0.06->0.00 by mip level 2, verified offline from indices.bin). Fix: clamp the coverage scale to >=1.0 (boost-only, Castano's actual formulation -- preservation may only ADD coverage to counter a coarser mip losing it, never remove it) and widen the boost cap to 32. Type-1 becomes a no-op (plain box keeps the fence visible, coverage 0.06->1.0 across mips); type-2 (SF page 518, ref=0x80) still boosts and stays solid so the SF checkerboard fix is preserved. Confirm: Keswick (--DefaultTrack=10) fences draw at FULL distance with no near pop-in (A/B vs TD5RE_TRACK_MIPS=0); San Francisco (--DefaultTrack=11) fence still see-through with no checkerboard/jagged edge; foliage on 1-2 other tracks unregressed. Render-only, TD5RE-only.

summary: Track chain-link fences / alpha-cutout signs no longer checkerboard at distance (SF fence)
detail: [SF FENCE MIPS 2026-08-10] San Francisco (level002) has a chain-link fence wall (texture page 518, transparency type 2) that rendered as an opaque grey checkerboard/moire with a jagged blocky top edge: the 64x64 alpha-keyed mesh tiles across a large wall and was minified with NO mipmaps (every track texture uploaded MipLevels=1) while the sampler asked for trilinear -> severe minification aliasing on both RGB and the 1-bit alpha coverage. Fix (scoped, ddraw_wrapper/src/d3d12_backend.c + td5_platform_win32.c): build a coverage-preserving mip chain ONLY for track race pages (page index < 700 static-atlas base) whose transparency type is 1 (alpha-keyed) or 2 (color-key) -- fences/foliage/signs. Alpha-weighted box-filter RGB (so black type-2 hole texels don't bleed the wire dark), plain-averaged alpha, then alpha rescaled per-mip to hold the draw-time alpha_ref coverage (0x80 for type 2, 1 for type 1) so the fence neither dissolves nor thickens with distance. Font atlas (700+), car (800+), traffic (820+) and opaque road/building pages are NEVER mipped. Gated by env TD5RE_TRACK_MIPS (default ON; =0 restores single-mip). In-place-refresh and device-lost re-flush paths stay mip-consistent (both funnel through Backend_TextureUpload, which regenerates the chain when bt->want_mips). Confirm: race San Francisco (--DefaultTrack=11) -> the roadside chain-link fence reads as a smooth see-through grey mesh with a clean top edge, no shimmering checkerboard; spot-check 1-2 other tracks that alpha-keyed foliage/signs still look right and opaque road textures are unchanged. summary: Trees: no black borders around foliage sprite edges (Keswick)
detail: [FOLIAGE EDGE AA 2026-08-10] Roadside trees (reported on Keswick, the big central tree) rendered with blocky BLACK borders around the alpha-cutout silhouette. Investigation: the trees are NOT a black-bleed/alpha problem -- the canopy interior itself is near-black (measured ~RGB 6,7,4 under a bright overcast sky; the source tree pages are genuinely very dark green ~3,16,2). Under a hard alphaRef=0x80 discard, RGB alpha-bleed is a no-op (surviving edge texels never blend the transparent RGB). The visible 'black border' is the blocky HARD-CUT alpha-test silhouette of an already-dark tree against bright sky, because the 2D foliage edge-AA path (SampleFoliageAA in ps_common.hlsli) shipped on the retired D3D11 backend (@91e51a6f) but was left DORMANT on D3D12 -- the FogCB.foliageAA flag was never written (comment claimed 'set per-draw by the foliage path' but no writer existed). Fix (TD5RE-only, D3D12 render path): re-enable it -- Backend_CreateDevice sets g_backend.foliage_aa_enabled (TD5RE_FOLIAGE_AA env, default 1) and Backend_UpdateFogCB sets fog.foliageAA=1 for exactly the colour-key cutout draws (foliage_aa_enabled && alpha_test_enable && current_tex_has_alpha), the same gate as the old Backend_IsFoliageAA. Those draws now sample via SampleFoliageAA (alpha-weighted manual bilinear reconstruction -> smooth 0..1 alpha edge ramp), anti-aliasing the silhouette. Opaque sky/road/car-body draws (no alpha test / no alpha) keep foliageAA=0 and are byte-identical. UPDATE 2026-08-10 (increment 2): the first attempt only covered type-2 (alpha-blended) pages, but Keswick's big near-field trees are type-1 (color-key, drawn OPAQUE_LINEAR = hard cut) so they were untouched (user confirmed still blocky). Increment 2 extends the edge-AA to type-1 pages ONLY when drawn as a BILLBOARD (tree/sign camera-facing quad, td5_render_mesh.c billboard_tag 1/2): such draws set s_bb_foliage_aa, which promotes their type-1 page from OPAQUE_LINEAR to TRANSLUCENT_ANISO (blend + alpha_ref 0x80) so the wrapper foliageAA gate anti-aliases the edge. The bit is carried through the rcmd RC_BIND_PAGE command (c->b) so it survives split-screen pane record/replay, and is __thread so parallel pane recording never races. CRITICAL scoping: ordinary type-1 WORLD geometry (walls, chain-link track-mesh fences, ground detail) is NOT a billboard, so s_bb_foliage_aa stays 0 and it keeps its faithful hard cutout. Knob TD5RE_FOLIAGE_AA_BILLBOARD=0 restores type-1 hard cutout; TD5RE_FOLIAGE_AA=0 (wrapper) disables all foliage AA. Confirm by DRIVING/looking: race Keswick (--DefaultTrack=10) -> the big near-field trees now have a soft anti-aliased outline (NOT crisp/HD -- a 64x64 mask at ~16x is inherently soft; crispness is the separate AI-upscale path, out of scope) instead of hard blocky black borders; spot-check that WALLS / chain-link fences / road / ground on Sydney+Keswick are UNCHANGED (still hard-edged, no new translucency/z-fighting); split-screen (2-4 panes) trees look identical to single-pane (proves record/replay path). Render-only, sim untouched (goldens unaffected). NOTE: overall tree DARKNESS is separate (likely faithful to the dark source art on rainy Keswick) -- this only fixes the blocky EDGE.

summary: RT: no first-frame freeze on slower GPUs (warms up on loading screen)
detail: [RT WARMUP 2026-08-08] On a slower DXR card (reported on an RTX 3070) enabling RT lighting rendered ONE non-RT frame and then froze the renderer while race audio kept playing -- a classic GPU TDR: race frame 1 stacked the full ray-tracing first-frame cost (the ~1600-mesh MODELS.DAT scenery feed that td5_rt_frame defers to frame 1, the resulting BLAS build wave, the shadow/light/reflection + denoise PSO creates, and the first-DispatchRays driver pipeline compile) and blew the 2s watchdog on hardware slower than the dev card. Fix: a new loading-screen RT warmup (td5_rt_warmup_prepare + Backend_RTWarmup{Begin,Step,Pending}, driven by rt_warmup_loading_pump at the end of InitRace) does the scenery feed early, force-creates every RT pipeline object, forces RT-pipeline driver residency with one throwaway DispatchRays, and drains the whole BLAS wave in bounded per-frame chunks WHILE the loading splash is shown -- so the first race frame is cheap. No-op in LOW / when RT is unavailable. MUST be confirmed on the RTX 3070 downstairs: enable [Lighting] Enabled=1 + HIGH quality, start a race (Moscow/Sydney) -> the loading image should hold a touch longer, then the race renders with RT and NO freeze; drive a full lap. Also sanity-check a fast card still races fine with RT on. TD5RE-only (RT enhancement); LOW path unchanged so goldens unaffected.

summary: Minimap draws the whole lap on big circuits (no abrupt road cut-off)
detail: [MINIMAP 2026-08-09] On large circuits the in-race vector minimap walked only a fixed 48/72-quad window (~432 spans). The per-quad AABB cull inside minimap_emit_road_quad already drops everything outside the minimap rectangle, so covering the full ring shows exactly what is visible and nothing more. P2P tracks are unchanged (their strip does not loop; widening risks redrawing the disconnected post-finish tail). Knob TD5RE_MINIMAP_FULLRING=0 restores the old fixed window. Confirm: race Newcastle (--DefaultTrack=5) and idle at the grid -> the road under the start bridge and other on-screen loop sections draw continuously to the minimap edge instead of stopping mid-map; race Moscow/Edinburgh (P2P) -> minimap unchanged. summary: RT: car shadows smooth in all lighting (no double/lag/missing-wheels)
detail: [CAR SHADOW 2026-08-06] Under RT lighting the car's grounding shadow was the RT sun shadow CAST by the car body BLAS (td5_rt.c fed actors InstanceMask 0 -> wrapper 0xFF -> shadow-ray castable), and render_vehicle_shadow_quad dropped the legacy soft blob whenever RT was active. On hardware that RT car cast (a) lagged the car at speed / glitched, (b) DOUBLED with the blob in sunlit scenes, (c) never included the WHEELS (body mesh only), and (d) vanished entirely in dark scenes (the sun-shadow pass bails with no/weak sun). Fix: cars no longer cast the RT sun shadow -- td5_rt.c feeds actors InstanceMask 0xFE (sun-shadow caster bit 0x01 cleared; reflection/GI/primary rays 0xFF still hit them so cars still reflect + occlude GI) -- and the soft terrain-conforming blob (render_vehicle_shadow_conforming) is now the car's grounding shadow in ALL lighting. The blob tracks the car exactly via the wheel-probe footprint, covers the whole contact patch incl. wheels, and works in dark/night/tunnel and bright sun alike. World/scenery objects still cast crisp RT sun shadows on the road (unchanged). TD5RE_RT_CAR_CAST=1 restores the old RT car cast (drops the blob) for A/B. Confirm by DRIVING with RT LIGHTING on: (1) sunny track -> ONE soft shadow under each car, no doubling; (2) at speed -> the shadow stays glued to the car, no lag/glitch; (3) the shadow spans the whole car incl. under the wheels; (4) overcast/evening/tunnel -> cars still have a grounding shadow. TD5RE-only (RT enhancement); goldens unaffected (render-only).

summary: RT: fixed blocky/pixelated shading on the back of cars
detail: [CAR PIXELATION 2026-08-05] The rear panels of cars showed a coarse blocky/pixelated grey pattern under RT lighting. Cause: the RT per-pixel ray jitter (rt_hash_world, rt_common.hlsli) is world-locked and quantized into 16-unit cells for motion stability; on a small curved car body those cells project to big blocks. Two RT passes composite onto the car with that coarse jitter: the sun-shadow cone (rgen_shadow) AND -- the dominant contributor with [Lighting] Reflections off -- the sky-visibility GI/AO (rgen_ao), which under the TDR-safe default runs only ~2 hemisphere rays, so the AO is very noisy and the a-trous denoiser can't smooth the big blocks -> grey blotches. Fix (rt_pipeline.hlsl): in BOTH rgen_shadow and rgen_ao, detect car pixels via the G-buffer alpha isCar tag (bit 0x40, from ps_modulate_g.hlsl) and give them a FINER jitter cell (RT_CAR_NOISE_CELL=2.0) + more samples (>=6 rays) so the signal is fine grain the denoiser resolves into a clean gradient. Road/world keep the coarse, cheap, distance-stable path. Verified in a headless framedump on Newcastle (RT active): rear bodywork clean, no blotches. NEEDS DRIVE-TEST for motion: watch a car up close (esp. overcast) while moving -> shading stays smooth, no new shimmer/crawl; road shadows unchanged. Requires a ddraw_wrapper shader rebuild. TD5RE-only (RT enhancement); goldens unaffected (render-only).

summary: Split-screen pause: PLAYER N PAUSED label + quick 3-2-1 resume countdown
detail: [PAUSE UX 2026-08-05] Two local split-screen MP additions (num_human_players>1, non-network). (1) PAUSED-BY LABEL: a green 'PLAYER N PAUSED' line sits above the shared, screen-centred pause panel naming the pad that opened the menu. Capture is in td5_game.c: the per-player TD5_INPUT_PAUSE scan records which slot fired (keyboard ESC = pane 0); td5_game_pause_local_slot() surfaces it and td5_hud_draw_pause_paused_by() renders it (hud_screen_center + hud_pause_scale so it tracks the panel at any window size). (2) RESUME COUNTDOWN: any genuine resume (CONTINUE / ESC / pad-B, NOT restart/quit/exit/freecam) arms a brief 3-2-1 (TD5_RESUME_COUNTDOWN_TICKS = 45 = 15 ticks/digit @30Hz = 0.5s/digit, ~1.5s total -- deliberately quicker than the ~1.3s/digit race start). A new freeze branch in the sim loop (s_resume_countdown_ticks>0, alongside disconnect/freecam) holds the field fully frozen while tick_resume_countdown() drives the SAME per-pane HUD digit as the start countdown (set_countdown_indicator_state), then unfreezes at GO; g_td5.paused stays 0 so the start-countdown path is never entered. Re-pausing during the 3-2-1 cancels it. Single-player and network pause are unchanged (net keeps its lockstep PAUSED BY overlay). Confirm: 2+ joystick split-screen race, player 2 presses pause -> panel shows 'PLAYER 2 PAUSED'; pick CONTINUE (or press ESC/pad-B) -> a quick 3-2-1 counts down in every pane, cars stay frozen, then GO and control returns; single-player pause still resumes instantly. TD5RE-only; recovery/resume are manual-press only so goldens unaffected.

summary: Manual over-rev: red warning border corners no longer double-bright
detail: [SHIFT 2026-08-05] The pulsating red over-rev border (shown after holding the engine over the limiter in a manual gear for TD5RE_OVERREV_WARN_MS) drew four full-length edge bars whose corners OVERLAPPED; with alpha blending the four corners composited at ~2x alpha and pulsed brighter than the edges ("shown double"). Fixed by insetting the left/right bars to the interior height [T+th,B-th] so each corner is covered by exactly one bar (td5_hud.c). Confirm in a DRAG or Manual race: bounce off the limiter until the red border appears -> all four corners pulse at the SAME brightness as the edges, no bright double-corners. Render-only, TD5RE-only; goldens unaffected.

summary: Manual shift arrows + timing use each car's per-gear shift point (low gears)
detail: [SHIFT 2026-08-05] The manual shift-up arrow bands AND the shift-timing reward/penalty were a flat % of redline for every gear, so fast-revving low gears blew past the green window almost instantly -- "first gears feel too short". The GREEN ideal-shift band now tracks the car's OWN tuned per-gear upshift RPM (carparam phys+0x3E+gear*2, the same value the auto box uses); BLUE (approaching) and RED (over-rev) keep their proportional offset via the *_PCT knobs; DOWN uses the tuned downshift RPM. Falls back to the flat %-of-redline when a car's per-gear value is missing. td5_hud.c (arrow) + td5_input.c (bog / money-shift penalty) share the point so they agree. Confirm in a DRAG or Manual race across several cars: the green shift-up window appears at a sensible per-gear point in EVERY gear (1st/2nd no longer flick green->red instantly) and the bog / money-shift penalties line up with the arrow colour. TD5RE-only, manual path only; goldens (auto slot 0) byte-identical.

summary: Manual: engine braking on wrong gear; N coasts, reverse-while-forward brakes
detail: [SHIFT 2026-08-05] New MANUAL-only engine-braking layer on the drive-torque chokepoint (td5_physics_compute_drive_torque): (1) holding a too-low forward gear over the limiter and LIFTING off throttle now actively SLOWS the car instead of coasting -- under throttle it stays just the rev limiter (no accel); (2) selecting REVERSE while still rolling FORWARD brakes hard until forward motion stops, then normal reverse drive resumes; (3) NEUTRAL is pure coast (no drive, no brake). Gated on manual gearbox so automatic/AI cars and the auto slot-0 golden races never engine-brake (byte-identical). Knobs: TD5RE_ENGINE_BRAKING (1=on default), TD5RE_ENGINE_BRAKE_PCT (over-rev coast brake %/tick, def 6), TD5RE_WRONGGEAR_BRAKE_PCT (reverse-while-forward %/tick, def 20). Confirm in a Manual race: (a) rev a low gear then lift without upshifting -> car slows noticeably vs auto; (b) at speed drop into Reverse -> brakes hard to a stop then reverses; (c) shift to Neutral -> pure coast. TD5RE-only, manual path only; goldens byte-identical. Two _PCT magnitudes need a manual drive-test to tune.

summary: Restore car (SELECT/R) resets IN PLACE, no teleport to track start (MP)
detail: [BREAKDOWN IN-PLACE 2026-08-05] In 6-player MP, restoring a car with SELECT sometimes teleported it back near the START of the track instead of a few spans. Root cause (td5_physics_assists.c): a KNOCKED-OUT car took the breakdown 'force-recovery' path (TD5_BREAKDOWN_SPANS_BACK, default 30) which stepped back 30 spans via td5_track_get_recovery_pose(); near the start (point-to-point clamp) or the start/finish (circuit wrap) that resolved to ~span 0. Frequent in 6-player races because knockouts are common, so the same SELECT press silently did the punishing step-back instead of the gentle in-place reset. Fix: breakdown step-back default 30 -> 0, so restore ALWAYS resets the car in place (a few spans at most) like the ordinary-stuck flavour; the breakdown path still grants full repair + the ghost window. Old behaviour opt-in via TD5RE_BREAKDOWN_SPANS_BACK=30. Confirm: 6-joystick MP with car damage on, get a car knocked out (PRESS TO CONTINUE), press SELECT -> car recovers roughly where it broke down, NOT back near the start; ordinary stuck recovery unchanged. TD5RE-only; recovery only fires on manual press so goldens unaffected.

summary: TRAFFIC BATTLE: reversing auto-returns you to your furthest point
detail: [BATTLE ANTIREVERSE 2026-08-05] Follow-up to the HWM spawn anchor: a human who drives BACKWARD for a sustained ~5s (TD5RE_BATTLE_ANTIREVERSE_SECS, default 5) — i.e. stays >TD5RE_BATTLE_ANTIREVERSE_SLACK spans (default 4) below their furthest mark from td5_ai_traffic_battle_hwm without making forward progress that whole time — is restored forward onto the track at that high-water span with all velocity zeroed and heading realigned. The timer RESETS the instant they get back to their mark or drive forward, so ordinary reversing / U-turns / dodging (and legitimate forward recovery) are left alone; only a persistent wrong-way run trips it. Reuses the byte-faithful spawn placement primitive (td5_track_init_actor_segment_placement -> on-road lane point) so it never drops into wall geometry, + td5_physics_reset_actor_state + td5_track_compute_heading. Runs in td5_physics_battle_antireverse_tick (td5_physics_assists.c) from td5_physics_tick. Humans only (g_race_slot_state==1), skips broken-down/finished cars, deterministic/lockstep-safe. Confirm by DRIVING a TRAFFIC BATTLE: try to reverse / U-turn and drive back down the track -> the car is pulled back to the furthest point you'd reached (not a teleport to start; lands on-road, stopped, facing forward). Test on a CIRCUIT (e.g. Newcastle) too, incl. across the start/finish line, to confirm no false snap on a legit lap. TD5RE_BATTLE_ANTIREVERSE=0 disables. TD5RE-only; goldens unaffected (battle only).

summary: TRAFFIC BATTLE: passed traffic despawns ~50 spans behind
detail: [BATTLE DESPAWN 2026-08-05] In TRAFFIC BATTLE a car that has fallen more than TD5RE_BATTLE_DESPAWN_BEHIND spans (default 50) behind the trailing-most player now retires promptly, freeing its slot to respawn fresh ahead of the field. Added as a battle-only term in the dynamic despawn corridor (td5_ai_traffic.c TRF_DYN_ACTIVE case) that fires even with the per-player cap on (whose union-of-bubbles rear bound is otherwise ~115+ spans). Confirm by DRIVING a TRAFFIC BATTLE: drive past oncoming traffic and watch behind you -> passed cars fade out ~50 spans back rather than lingering far behind; density stays concentrated around the players. Split-screen: uses the trailing-most player, so a car another pane is still approaching is NOT despawned early. TD5RE-only; goldens unaffected (battle only).

summary: TRAFFIC BATTLE: reversing no longer farms traffic spawns
detail: [BATTLE HWM 2026-08-05] In TRAFFIC BATTLE, live traffic used to anchor spawns on each racer's CURRENT track span, so a player could drive BACKWARDS to keep sliding their spawn window into road they re-approach = endless fresh targets (6-joystick MP farm). Now spawns anchor on each racer's FURTHEST-reached point (high-water mark s_trf_battle_hwm, cumulative lap*ring+span via td5_game_get_slot_progress so it survives circuit lap-wrap, in td5_ai_traffic.c). A player who drops more than TD5RE_BATTLE_HWM_SLACK spans (default 6) below their mark is skipped as a spawn anchor AND their per-viewport pane places no traffic, until they climb back past the mark. Forward driving is unchanged (current==mark). Confirm by DRIVING a TRAFFIC BATTLE (MP or solo via TD5RE_BATTLE=1): drive forward -> traffic streams normally; stop and REVERSE -> traffic stops appearing near you and does NOT refill until you drive forward past where you'd already been. Split-screen: each pane independent (one player reversing doesn't starve the others). TD5RE-only; goldens unaffected (battle mode only).

summary: TRAFFIC BATTLE: first-finisher 60s countdown ends the race
detail: [BATTLE FINISH TIMER 2026-08-05] TRAFFIC BATTLE (MOST WRECKS) had no early end, so players could crawl/idle to farm wrecks indefinitely. Now the moment the FIRST racer finishes the race, a countdown arms (TD5RE_BATTLE_FINISH_SECS, default 60s, sim-tick based so it stays lockstep-deterministic in netplay); when it elapses every still-racing slot is force-finished so the normal completion latch fires and standings lock (most wrecks wins). HUD shows an 'ENDS m:ss' clock under the WRECKS count (red in the last 10s). td5_game.c battle_finish_timer_tick + td5_game_battle_finish_secs_left; HUD in td5_hud_draw_battle_wrecks. Confirm: run a TRAFFIC BATTLE with 2+ racers, let one finish the race -> the ENDS m:ss clock appears for everyone and counts down from 1:00; when it hits 0:00 the race ends and results show (winner = most wrecks) even if others were still driving. Set TD5RE_BATTLE_FINISH_SECS=0 to disable. TD5RE-only; goldens unaffected.

summary: No crash pop-up on exit (harmless MF/D3D12 teardown race silenced)
detail: [EXIT-CRASH DIALOG 2026-08-05] Quitting the game (Alt+F4 / EXIT) sometimes flashed a 'TD5RE Crash' modal. Root cause: as the process exits, Windows system DLLs fault on their OWN background/work-queue threads while their platform is torn down -- RTWorkQ.DLL from the internet-radio/FMV Media Foundation MFShutdown, or D3D12Core.dll from the device release. Our SetUnhandledExceptionFilter caught the background-thread fault and popped MessageBoxA (the 'brief crash message'); the main thread meanwhile finished its orderly shutdown, so the process still exited cleanly. Fix (main.c): a shutting-down flag is set at the start of Step 7; while set, the filter still writes crash.log (diagnostics preserved) but suppresses the modal -- a faulting BACKGROUND thread is parked (SleepEx INFINITE) so the main thread completes shutdown and ExitProcess reaps it, and a main-thread teardown fault terminates quietly. In-game (non-shutdown) crashes still log AND show the dialog as before. The underlying fault is inside Windows system DLLs (not our code) and is harmless at process exit. Confirm: play a race with internet radio on, Alt+F4 / EXIT GAME repeatedly -> the game closes with NO crash pop-up; log/crash.log may still record the teardown fault (that's expected/benign); an intentional in-game crash still shows the dialog. TD5RE-only (port harness); goldens unaffected.

summary: Stuck-recovery (non-breakdown SELECT) no longer secretly repairs the car
detail: [STUCK-RECOVERY NO-REPAIR 2026-08-05] td5_physics_recover_player called td5_damage_repair_actor_pct on BOTH the breakdown and the ordinary 'I'm stuck' paths, so a plain SELECT press refilled part of the health bar (TD5_MANUAL_RECOVERY_REPAIR_PCT=20) on a car that merely got stuck -- an unwanted free heal. The repair is now gated to from_breakdown only; the ordinary path just un-sticks (position/velocity/heading reset) and leaves damage untouched. The broken-down flag is still cleared unconditionally (no-op unless actually broken down). Confirm by DRIVING: dent a car, get it stuck (not knocked out), press SELECT -> it frees up but the health bar / damage is UNCHANGED; a genuinely broken-down car pressing SELECT still fully repairs. TD5RE-only (CarDamage is a port feature); goldens unaffected.

summary: Split-screen: SELECT-restore snaps camera behind the broken-down car (was sometimes stuck rotated)
detail: [SPLIT-SCREEN RESTORE-CAM 2026-08-05] In split-screen MP, when a car broke down the chase cam spins (cam_finish_orbit_step drifts g_camYawOffset while knocked out), and pressing SELECT to continue is supposed to snap the camera back behind that car (td5_camera_reset_yaw_offset). It SOMETIMES didn't -- pressing the front-view/change-camera button was the workaround. Root cause: recovery_local_view_for_slot (td5_physics_assists.c) resolved the pane to reset with the TD5RE_SPLIT_BTN_ROUTE ternary INVERTED relative to view_for_player (td5_input.c): with routing ON (default) it used the identity pane (vp==slot) instead of the display mapping g_actorSlotForView[vp]==slot. When the MP position picker permutes panes the yaw reset then hit the WRONG pane, so the pane showing the recovered car kept its spun-up yaw; the front-view button uses view_for_player and reset the right pane, hence the workaround. Fix: resolve the pane by g_actorSlotForView[vp]==slot unconditionally (display truth is independent of the button-routing knob), matching the buttons. Confirm by DRIVING split-screen MP (2 players, ideally with the position picker permuting panes): let one car break down (camera orbits), press SELECT -> that pane's camera immediately settles directly behind the car WITHOUT needing the view button; the other pane is unaffected; single-view still works. TD5RE-only (recovery/finish-orbit are port features); render-only, goldens unaffected.

summary: Sun-aligned car lighting + subtle sun glint (HIGH)
detail: [CAR SUN 2026-08-04] Under RT the car was lit by a fixed flat studio 3-point light (td5_render_set_override_daylight) that read dim and ignored the real sun. Replaced with td5_render_set_override_sunlit: the dominant directional is the real scene sun transformed into the car's model frame (lit side follows the sun as the car turns) + a brighter sky ambient; falls back to flat daylight when there's no sun (tunnel/night). Plus a subtle Blinn-Phong sun glint on car body/glass in the RT reflection pass (needs [Lighting] Reflections=1). Knobs: TD5RE_CAR_SUN_DIR/_AMB, TD5RE_RT_CAR_GLINT, TD5RE_SUN_ELEVATE (test-only sun raise). Confirm by DRIVING a sunny track (e.g. Australia span ~200): the car's sun-facing side is brighter than the shadow side and the bright side tracks the sun through corners; a soft glossy glint slides across body/glass. TD5RE-only; goldens unaffected.

summary: FREE CAMERA pause-menu option (dev builds): free-roam / fly camera
detail: [FREE CAMERA 2026-08-04] New DEV-only pause-menu row FREE CAMERA (directly under CONTINUE) closes the menu but KEEPS the sim paused and hands pane 0's camera to a free-roam fly cam. It never feeds the sim (physics/AI/replay untouched -> determinism/golden-safe), overrides at the top of td5_camera_apply_view via SetCameraWorldPosition + OrientCameraTowardTarget, integrates on wall-clock time (td5_plat_time_ms; g_subTickFraction is frozen while paused), and clamps pitch to ~85deg. Controls: keyboard WASD move / arrows look / E-Q up-down / Shift boost; gamepad left stick move / right stick look (newly exposed via TD5_InputState.analog_rx/ry) / A-B up-down / X boost; Esc or Start exits back to the pause menu. Tuning: TD5RE_FREECAM_SPEED (wu/s, def 320) / _LOOK (rad/s, def 2.2) / _BOOST (mult, def 4). Compiled out of RELEASE (row gated + inert stubs). Confirm by DRIVING: pause mid-race, pick FREE CAMERA -> menu closes, world stays frozen, fly around and rotate with pad + keyboard; entering doesn't snap the viewpoint; Esc/Start returns to the pause menu; CONTINUE then resumes the race normally. Split-screen: only pane 0 is controlled (single-view by design). TD5RE-only; goldens unaffected.

summary: Cars default to AUTOMATIC; car-select transmission toggle now drives the gearbox
detail: [GEARBOX DEFAULT 2026-08-04] Cars were driving MANUAL by default because the working-tree td5re.ini had [GameOptions] AutoGearbox=0 (committed default is 1), and td5_input.c's want_manual carried an unconditional !g_td5.ini.auto_gearbox OR-term that forced MANUAL whenever AutoGearbox=0 -- even when the car-select screen showed 'Automatic'. Fixes: (1) restored td5re.ini AutoGearbox=1 (local scaffolding, not committed); (2) td5_input.c -- when the manual-gearbox layer is enabled (TD5RE_MANUAL_GEARBOX default ON) want_manual now comes from drag-race force + the per-player menu pick (td5_frontend_get_player_manual) ONLY, no INI override; the legacy INI/drag-only path is kept for TD5RE_MANUAL_GEARBOX=0; (3) td5_frontend.c -- the single-player s_selected_transmission is now SEEDED from AutoGearbox at both car-select reset points (auto-race + car-select entry) so the INI still chooses the toggle's initial position (auto->0, manual->1) but the menu is authoritative thereafter. Confirm by DRIVING: a fresh Quick Race with AutoGearbox=1 -> car auto-shifts (gear keys ignored); flip the car-select toggle to Manual -> that car honours gear-up/down and no longer auto-shifts; flip back to Automatic -> auto-shifts again. Drag race still forces Manual regardless. Split-screen: each player's own toggle drives their car. Byte-faithful sim path unchanged; goldens unaffected.

summary: TUTORIAL toggle now on RACE OPTIONS for every mode (incl. multiplayer)
detail: [TUTORIAL 2026-07-27] The controller-tutorial TUTORIAL on/off row on the consolidated RACE OPTIONS screen (screen 44) was gated single-player-only (td5_frontend.c td5_raceopts_row_available RO_TUTORIAL: return !c->is_mp). It is now available in every mode, MP included (return 1). Safe because the overlay already supports multiple humans (td5_tutorial.c s_humans + per-player s_ready_mask/s_prev_in[TD5_MAX_HUMAN_PLAYERS], waits on ALL humans ready) and raceopts_commit_persist already applies s_game_option_tutorial->g_td5.ini.tutorial_overlay for all modes. Confirm: enter RACE OPTIONS from a MULTIPLAYER race setup (2+ players) -> a TUTORIAL row (ON/OFF) is present and toggles; single-player RACE OPTIONS still shows it; toggling OFF then launching skips the first-race controller overlay; ON shows it and waits for all players to ready-up. TD5RE-only, frontend-only; goldens unaffected.

summary: Paris/city banners: START + checkpoint gantries render seated, not skewed
detail: [BANNER ALIGN 2026-07-27] The TD6 START-banner road-centre re-alignment (s_banner_align in td5_render_mesh.c, env TD5RE_BANNER_ALIGN) is now DEFAULT OFF. The heuristic shifted a gantry's OVERHEAD panel toward road-centre while leaving its support posts, detaching the panel into a skewed floating quad on Paris (lvl 8). Verified align OFF looks cleaner on BOTH Paris and London (lvl 12, the track it was authored for -- align ON pushed London's START right so it read 'TART'). Knob kept opt-in: TD5RE_BANNER_ALIGN=1 restores the old behaviour. Confirm by DRIVING: Quick Race Paris (and London) -> START/checkpoint banners hang cleanly between their posts, readable, no floating/skewed panels. TD5RE-only; goldens unaffected (render-only).

summary: No daytime headlights on bright tracks flagged rainy (Paris)
detail: [AUTO LIGHTS 2026-07-27] Paris's converted LEVELINF carries weather_type=0 (== rain, also the zero-default of an un-set field) while its sky renders bright (luma ~163), so the auto-headlight weather term forced lights on a plainly sunny track. Added a daytime veto in td5_render_env_is_dark_for_slot (td5_render_mesh.c): the RAIN weather_dark term is suppressed when sky luma >= s_auto_day_thr (default 130, env TD5RE_LIGHT_AUTO_DAY). Genuinely dark/dusk rainy tracks (low sky luma) still get lights; tunnels (per-zone term) are not vetoed. Confirm by DRIVING: Quick Race Paris in daytime -> player + AI car headlights stay OFF on the open sunlit road; a night track (Moscow) still has them ON. race.log w/ TD5RE_LIGHT_AUTO_LOG=1 shows bright=1 weather=0 -> dark=0 on Paris. TD5RE-only; goldens unaffected.

summary: View Replay: race results table keeps its stats after replay
detail: [REPLAY RESULTS STATS 2026-07-27] After watching a View Replay and returning to the post-race RESULTS screen, several results-table columns showed reset/zero values. Root cause: View Replay re-enters the race via g_td5.race_requested -> td5_game_init_race_session, and while capture_replay_results_snapshot/restore_replay_results_snapshot (TD5RE_REPLAY_KEEP_RESULTS, default ON) already preserved s_results/s_metrics/s_slot_state/s_race_order/s_slot_finish_place/s_arrest_time/s_finish_position_display across the replay, the summary screen reads OTHER state the snapshot missed: COLLISIONS + AIR TIME come from g_race_metrics[] (zeroed by td5_physics_reset_metrics during the replay's init, AFTER capture), and AVG SPEED (td5_game_get_result_avg_speed) + HIGHEST POSITION (td5_game_get_highest_position) read live actor fields (actor->average_speed_metric, ->grip_reduction) with no s_results source, while TOP SPEED / ARRESTS fall back to actor->peak_speed / ->special_encounter_state when the snapshot value is 0 -- all overwritten by the replay. Fix (td5_game.c): the snapshot now also captures/restores g_race_metrics[] and those four per-actor fields (peak_speed, average_speed_metric, grip_reduction, special_encounter_state). Confirm by DRIVING: finish a race, note the results summary (avg/top speed, collisions, air time, highest position, arrests), pick View Replay, let it end (or ESC), and back on the results screen every column reads the SAME real-race values as before the replay -- not zeros. TD5RE-only (View Replay is a port feature); goldens unaffected (playback poses from a buffer, sim untouched).

summary: View Replay: smooth playback at high FPS (was stuttering at 30 Hz)
detail: [REPLAY SUB-TICK SMOOTHING 2026-07-27] View Replay posed each car once per 30 Hz recorded frame and ZEROED all six velocities (td5_replay.c replay_pose_actor), so the renderer's per-render-frame sub-tick extrapolation (td5_render_mesh.c: world_pos + linear_velocity*g_subTickFraction for position, display_angles + angular_velocity*frac/256 for rotation) added nothing -- cars visibly stuttered at 30 fps while the top-left FPS/MS overlay (g_td5_display_fps = true wall-clock render fps) read 60+; the mismatch was most obvious at trackside camera angles with fast lateral/rotational motion. Fix: instead of zeroing, reconstruct per-tick velocities from the delta to the NEXT recorded frame -- linear_velocity = next.world_pos - cur.world_pos; angular_velocity = wrap12(next.display_angles - cur.display_angles)*256 (shortest signed path so a yaw wrap doesn't spin the car). On the final frame there is no next frame so velocities stay 0 and playback freezes cleanly. Reuses the existing render extrapolation, no renderer changes. Traffic (vehicle_mode!=0) smooths position but not rotation (renderer uses rotation_matrix directly for those) -- acceptable, the player+AI racers are vehicle_mode==0 and smooth fully. Confirm by WATCHING a View Replay at high fps: cars move as smoothly as live gameplay, no 30 Hz stepping, and the motion matches the FPS counter. TD5RE-only (replay is PORT-ONLY); goldens unaffected (playback poses from a buffer, sim untouched).

summary: Traffic Battle: EVASIVE TRAFFIC option makes traffic dodge you
detail: [TRAFFIC BATTLE 2026-07-23] New EVASIVE TRAFFIC toggle (OFF/ON) in the Traffic Battle race options, replacing the removed SPAWN PERIOD + POWER-UPS rows. ON (mp_mode_config.battle_evasive; SP knob TD5RE_BATTLE_EVASIVE=1) makes each traffic car bias its target sub-lane one step AWAY from the nearest racer at the lane-choice chokepoint (trf_battle_evade_lane in td5_ai_traffic.c, called after the normal chooser, gated by trf_battle_evasive_on). Range window TD5RE_BATTLE_EVADE_RANGE (default 10 spans). Deterministic (replicated actor state + mode only) so netplay/replay agree. Confirm by DRIVING: Traffic Battle with EVASIVE TRAFFIC ON -> oncoming traffic actively swerves out of your path as you approach, noticeably harder to ram; with it OFF traffic holds its lines as before. race.log emits 'trf_battle_evade: slot=.. racer=.. lane X->Y (evasive)'. TD5RE-only; goldens unaffected (battle not in golden set).

summary: Traffic Battle: no power-ups + starting it no longer runs a Drag Race
detail: [TRAFFIC BATTLE 2026-07-23] (1) Power-ups removed from Traffic Battle: battle InitRace forces g_td5.ini.powerups=0 and mp_mode_config.battle_powerup_density=0, so no arcade item boxes or MAGNET appear -- the collision ram mechanic is untouched. (2) FIX: launching Traffic Battle wrongly ran a DRAG RACE. The MP flow never re-runs ConfigureGameTypeFlags, so a stale game_type==9 (DRAG_RACE) leaked through to drag-keyed paths -- notably td5_asset.c level_number loading the drag strip level030.zip. Battle InitRace now forces g_td5.game_type=TD5_GAMETYPE_SINGLE_RACE and level_number excludes battle mode from the drag-strip selection. Confirm: after playing a Drag Race, start a Traffic Battle -> it runs on the chosen normal track with oncoming traffic (NOT the drag strip, no staged lanes), and no floating item boxes appear anywhere. TD5RE-only; goldens unaffected.

summary: Arcade power-up pickup: grab nearest box, tighter reach (chaos mode)
detail: [ARCADE 2026-07-23] Power-up pickup in ARCADE/chaos was unpredictable when several boxes sat close together. Two causes fixed in td5_arcade.c td5_arcade_tick pickup-detection loop: (1) the loop called apply_pickup for EVERY box inside the window without breaking, and the s_effect!=NONE guard is at the top of the SLOT loop not the pad loop, so the effect you ended with was whichever box came LAST in s_pads[] array order -- arbitrary. Now it scans the whole window and collects only the SINGLE nearest box (score = fdiff*(lane_tol+1)+ldiff, longitudinal distance dominates, lateral tie-break, deterministic pad-index tie-break); one box per tick. (2) longitudinal window TD5RE_ARCADE_PICKUP_SPANS default tightened 2->1 span so the reach no longer overlaps adjacent boxes. Lateral gate TD5RE_ARCADE_PICKUP_LANES unchanged (default 1). Confirm: ARCADE race with POWER-UPS on, drive through a cluster of boxes -> you always pick up the box you're closest to, boxes you steer past (>1 span / >1 lane away) are left for others, and you never grab two in one pass. Deterministic (replicated span/lane + config only) so netplay/replay agree. TD5RE-only, no original counterpart; goldens unaffected (arcade not in golden race set).

summary: 7+ player / 7-screen split-screen no longer crashes the GPU driver
detail: [GPU 2026-07-23] Hard crash (0xC0000005 null-deref INSIDE nvwgf2um.dll at Present, device_removed=0 -- NOT a TDR/device-lost, those recover) reproduced by more than 7 players across 7 split-screen panes on Sydney reverse. Crash dumps (log/crash.1.log, crash.3.log) both show ~2230 draws/frame (39.2M draws / 17.6k presents) and current_srv=00000000 bound at Present, after a long tail of 2D HUD quads. Ruled out: pane/player arrays (all clamped to TD5_MAX_VIEWPORTS=9), streaming ring (16MB VB / 4MB IB, no mid-frame wrap at ~285KB/frame). Mitigation in the ddraw wrapper (td5mod/ddraw_wrapper/src/device3.c): Dev3_SetTexture now binds the pre-created 1x1 white SRV (g_backend.white_srv) instead of NULL at every no-texture / missing-SRV / RT-SRV-hazard site and keeps current_srv consistent, and Dev3_DrawPrimitive/DrawIndexedPrimitive add a draw-time safety net that substitutes white when slot-0 current_srv is NULL -- so no sampling draw is ever issued with a null texture. Under PS_MODULATE white*diffuse==diffuse, so untextured coloured geometry (debug lines, solid HUD fills) is visually unchanged. Confirm: play a 7-player race (or headless: --DefaultTrack=2 --DefaultReverse=1 --SpectateScreens=6 --AutoRace=1) on Sydney reverse for several minutes -> no "TD5RE Crash" dialog and no NEW nvwgf2um.dll +0x25CBE1 entry in log/crash.*.log. Also sanity-check a normal 1-2 player race renders identically (no washed-out / all-white geometry).

summary: Manual shift arrows: colour bands (blue/green/red) + amber down arrow
detail: [SHIFT 2026-07-23 PORT ENHANCEMENT] The manual/drag shift arrows are now colour-coded by rev band instead of drawing black. Root cause of the black arrows: the up/down triangle sampled the COLOURS atlas texel (a non-white pixel) and multiplied it by the vertex colour, so texel*colour read as ~black; they now draw on HUD_WHITE_TEX_PAGE (UV 0,0) like the needle/minimap so the vertex colour is exact. Bands (fraction of redline, engine_speed_accum vs carparam+0x72): BLUE >= TD5RE_SHIFT_BLUE_PCT (78) = approaching; GREEN >= TD5RE_SHIFT_UP_PCT (90) = ideal shift-up; RED >= TD5RE_SHIFT_RED_PCT (97) = over-revving (blinks faster). A steady AMBER down triangle shows when lugging (gear>=3 and revs <= TD5RE_SHIFT_DOWN_PCT). td5_hud.c shift-indicator block. Confirm in a DRAG race (forces manual) or any race with AUTO/MANUAL set to Manual: accelerate through a gear and watch the up arrow above the dial go blue -> green -> red as revs climb; the arrow must be clearly COLOURED (not black). In split-screen each pane shows its own. Knobs: TD5RE_SHIFT_INDICATOR=0 hides them; the three *_PCT knobs move the band edges.

summary: Manual shift timing affects the car + pulsating-red over-rev HUD warning
detail: [SHIFT 2026-07-23 PORT ENHANCEMENT] Manual upshift timing now has gameplay consequences, matching the arrow colours. At the manual gear-up event (td5_input.c): shifting BELOW the green band (too early) bogs the revs (~12% of redline dropped, floored at idle) and starts a ~0.5s throttle cut (scaled to 60%) so the car recovers sluggishly; a GREEN-band shift is clean (no penalty); an over-rev (RED) shift knocks ~6% off longitudinal speed (a "money shift"). If the car keeps over-revving in a forward upshiftable gear for TD5RE_OVERREV_WARN_MS (default 1500ms) a pulsating red border is drawn around that pane (td5_hud.c). Gated by TD5RE_SHIFT_TIMING (default ON); band edges via TD5RE_SHIFT_UP_PCT/_RED_PCT. Confirm in a DRAG race or Manual race: (1) short-shift well before green -> car noticeably bogs and is slow to pull; (2) shift right at green -> clean strong pull; (3) hold the throttle bouncing off the limiter without shifting -> after ~1.5s the HUD edges pulse red, and shifting up from deep in the red costs a little speed. Automatic transmission is unaffected. NOTE: this changes physics on the MANUAL player path only; golden traces (auto, slot-0) must remain byte-identical -- verify goldens 51/51.

summary: Drag: no drivable track / stadium stands past the finish line
detail: [DRAG END WALL 2026-07-23] Fixes MP drag leader (and any finished drag car still under throttle) driving forward through the stadium stands at the end of the road. Root cause: td5_track_bind_boundary_sentinels pushes the drag strip's down-track boundary wall (rev sentinel) out to the strip end (ring-2, ~298) so LONG/EPIC drags can use the whole strip, leaving a long drivable corridor past the finish (SHORT finishes at span 170 but could roll to 298, straight through the vanilla stadium wall at 240). Fix: new td5_track_set_drag_end_wall(finish,runoff), called from td5_game.c once the finish span is known (after bind), pulls the down-track wall back to finish+24. Verified via race.log: SHORT wall 298->194 (finish 170+24); EPIC wall 559->415 (=finish 391+24 = end of inserted clean road / tail_end). Guarded by g_td5.drag_race_enabled so non-drag races are byte-identical (sim goldens pose/motion/track green for Moscow+Pelton). Applies to SP and MP drag (shared finish path). Confirm: MP drag, finish first and keep holding throttle -> your car stops shortly past the finish line and does NOT reach/clip the grandstand; repeat for SHORT/MEDIUM/LONG/EPIC distances; also confirm the finish line itself is always reachable (wall never before it).

summary: SP Drag Race: DISTANCE option (SHORT/MEDIUM/LONG/EPIC) in RACE OPTIONS
detail: [SP DRAG DISTANCE 2026-07-23] Single-player Drag Race now exposes a DISTANCE row on the RACE OPTIONS screen, matching the multiplayer drag DISTANCE option. New RO_DISTANCE row (td5_frontend_internal.h enum) with label DISTANCE, values SHORT/MEDIUM/LONG/EPIC mirroring k_cfg_draglen[]; available only when ctx.is_drag && !is_mp (MP drag keeps its own DISTANCE row on the MP config screen). Cycle edits g_td5.ini.drag_length (wraps 0..3), which SP drag already reads via drag_length_level() in td5_game.c. Now persisted to [GameOptions] DragLength in td5_ini_persist_options (main.c). Confirm: Single Race -> DRAG -> pick player car (pass 1) -> pick opponent car (pass 2) -> RACE OPTIONS appears as the pre-launch step and shows a DISTANCE row; cycle SHORT->MEDIUM->LONG->EPIC with LEFT/RIGHT; OK launches and the strip length matches the chosen preset (SHORT clearly shorter than EPIC); BACK from RACE OPTIONS re-enters the opponent car-select (cars preserved) and DISTANCE choice is retained; relaunch the game and the last DISTANCE choice sticks (written to td5re.ini). Verify MP drag DISTANCE still works unchanged (separate row on the MP config screen, reads mp_mode_config.drag_length).

summary: Edinburgh backwards: cars spawn facing forward (not 180 deg wrong)
detail: [SPAWN 2026-07-22] Edinburgh reverse (and any native P2P reverse with rb=0 at spawn spans) had cars spawning facing backward. Root cause: td5_ai_correct_spawn_heading was called for ALL g_td5.reverse_direction tracks (td5_game.c:4127 condition). For native P2P tracks the original STRIPB.DAT geometry heading is already correct (Edinburgh gives 0x000 = north, matching the original binary at 0x434501). But LEFTB.TRK has rb=0 from spans 45-119 at Edinburgh (the entire start area), so the function fell through to the tangent fallback which adds +0x800 to the tangent angle (0x000 north -> 0x800 south = 180 deg wrong). Fixed: condition changed from (g_td5.reverse_direction) to (g_td5.reverse_direction && g_track_is_circuit) -- only circuit tracks (which use a PORT-GENERATED STRIPB with sheared geometry) need the correction; native P2P tracks use original STRIPB whose geometry is already faithful. Confirmed by binary check: LEFTB.TRK rb=0 at spans 53-119 in level016.zip, STRIPB geometry at those spans gives dx=0 dz=-750 -> geom=0x000 -> tangent fallback yields 0x800. Goldens unaffected (P2P reverse is not in the golden race set). Confirm: start Edinburgh reverse -> all 6 cars face the road ahead (not backward); also check Moscow reverse to ensure its spawn direction is unchanged (Moscow LEFTB.TRK has rb=183-188 at spawn spans so it took the primary route-byte path, now falls back to geometry at ~260 deg which matches).

summary: View Replay: broken cars smoke, no damage bar, no phantom traffic shadows
detail: [REPLAY 2026-07-22] Three View-Replay fixes (ghost-replay path, TD5RE_GHOST_REPLAY default on). (1) SMOKE: a ghost replay skips the sim, so g_actor_broken_down[] + the hidden damage-health meter reset to 0 and wrecks stopped smoking on playback. The recorder (td5_replay.c) now captures each actor's broken-down flag + damage-smoke tier (0-3) per tick; td5_replay_actor_broken()/_smoke_tier() feed them back to the render smoke dispatch (td5_render_mesh.c) when g_replay_mode, so the wreck roof-plume + tiered damage smoke reproduce as in the live race. (2) DAMAGE BAR: td5_hud_draw_damage_bars / hud_draw_player_damage_bar early-out on g_replay_mode, and hud_top_center_shift_y returns 0 so top-centre HUD elements reclaim the bar's space. (3) SHADOWS: the shadow pre-pass deliberately skips the body frustum test (harmless under a chase cam), but the far/wide trackside replay camera made frustum-culled cars still cast a ground shadow ("shadows of traffic that isn't on screen"). New replay_actor_body_in_frustum() mirrors the body loop's transform + td5_render_test_mesh_frustum; the pre-pass is gated on it replay-only. Confirm in a mode where cars wreck (Traffic Battle or a CarDamage race): drive/finish, then View Replay from the results screen -> (a) wrecked traffic/cops emit the roof plume and a badly-damaged racer its tiered smoke, at the same moments as live; (b) the top-centre car-health bar is GONE and the other top-centre HUD elements sit slightly higher; (c) as the trackside camera pans, no ground shadows appear for cars whose bodies aren't on screen. Normal-race (non-replay) shadows/HUD/smoke unchanged. Render-only + record/pose buffer changes -> golden traces untouched.
