summary: RACE OPTIONS is now the single game-behaviour screen for every mode (GAME OPTIONS removed)
detail: [CONSOLIDATION 2026-07-21] The GAME OPTIONS screen (13) was deleted and its rows folded into the dynamic RACE OPTIONS screen (44), which every mode reaches from its track-select (button 3) and which is inserted as a pre-launch step for modes with no track-select. RACE OPTIONS now carries: OPPONENTS, TRAFFIC, POLICE, DIFFICULTY, DYNAMICS, CHECKPOINTS, POWER-UPS, CAR TOUGHNESS, DEFORMATION, 3D COLLISIONS, DAMAGE, LANE ASSIST, TUTORIAL. It shows ONLY the rows a given mode needs (td5_raceopts_row_available) and PAGINATES (7/page, PREV/NEXT only when >7 rows). PLAYER NAME moved to its own OPTIONS-hub top row (Enter-to-edit inline). Confirm per mode: (1) open RACE OPTIONS in Single Race / Time Trial / Cop Chase / Drag / Cup / Quick Race and each MP mode (race/cup/traffic-battle/cop-chase/drag) and verify exactly the expected rows appear, cycle, and PREV/NEXT + a PAGE x/y footer show only when >7 rows; (2) checkpoints hidden in MP + cop chase + drag; power-ups hidden in drag; traffic hidden in drag; opponents hidden in drag/cup/traffic-battle; difficulty hidden at 0 opponents / quick race / cup / MP cop chase; lane-assist + tutorial single-player only; (3) OK/BACK/ESC persist to td5re.ini [GameOptions]; (4) SP drag -> car-select pass 2 OK opens RACE OPTIONS then OK launches, BACK re-enters the opponent car-select with cars preserved; MP drag shows it once (no loop); faithful cup shows it only before race 1; (5) OPTIONS hub PLAYER NAME row edits + persists the name; the old GAME OPTIONS row is gone and StartScreen=13 redirects to the hub. Netplay 2-instance: host sets POWER-UPS/COLLISIONS/TOUGHNESS/DAMAGE, client with opposite INI -> both peers match, no desync, client td5re.ini untouched.

summary: crash.log now includes GPU draw-ring forensics on a driver crash
detail: When the SEH crash handler fires (main.c), crash.log now gets an extra "GPU crash diagnostics" section: a live backend snapshot (device/context/swapchain pointers, device_generation, device_removed, present_count, current SRV, rt/target sizes, diag_context) plus the DRAW WATCH ring -- the last 256 draw submissions, each with its primitive/vertex/index counts AND the SRV + device_generation bound AT DRAW TIME. Any recent draw whose gen is BELOW the current device_generation is flagged "<-- STALE (pre-reset resource)" -- the smoking gun for the device-lost stale-bind crash class (nvwgf2um.dll null-deref, access=0). The ring is always-on (a few memory writes per draw, no disk I/O, no env var); it dumps only from the crash handler. Confirm: force a crash (e.g. TD5RE_FORCE_DEVICE_LOST on a build without the in-race self-heal, or any real crash) -> crash.log has the "GPU crash diagnostics" + "DRAW WATCH (SEH crash)" sections, and normal play is unaffected (no perf change, no extra files). This is diagnostics only -- separate from the dev-only D3D debug-layer InfoQueue drain (TD5RE_D3D_DEBUG), which stays out of this build.

summary: In-race HUD survives a GPU device reset (TDR) without crashing to results
detail: A GPU driver reset (TDR / DEVICE_HUNG) DURING a race left the in-race VectorUI shaders dangling and crashed the NVIDIA driver (nvwgf2um.dll null-deref, access=00000000) on subsequent frames -- often surfacing on the race->results transition (the recurring "transition/results crash"). Root cause: the analog gauge dial (s_ps_gauge/s_gauge_cb via td5_vui_gauge) and crisp HUD text (s_ps_msdf via td5_vui_msdf_quad) are frontend-module statics rebuilt only by frontend_ensure_vui_shaders(), which ran ONLY from td5_frontend_render_ui_rects (the frontend loop) -- never in-race. After a device-generation bump those cached shader pointers belonged to the freed device; the draw primitives guarded only against NULL, not a stale non-NULL pointer, so they bound a dead-device shader -> driver deref. Fix (td5_frontend.c): td5_vui_gauge and td5_vui_msdf_quad now call the idempotent frontend_ensure_vui_shaders() BEFORE their NULL guard, so the in-race HUD self-heals on a generation bump exactly like the frontend does (a failed rebuild falls back to the early-out / plain quad). Render-only; no sim/golden impact. Verify: race with TD5RE_FORCE_DEVICE_LOST=<mid-race frame> -> the device recovers and the race continues to results with NO crash.log (pre-fix this wrote crash.log with the nvwgf2um.dll stack and died). Also confirm the speedo/tacho dial and HUD text render correctly for the rest of the race after the forced reset (not blank).

summary: Split-screen FFB follows your own car after a screen swap
detail: Force feedback (crash/gear/landing/terrain/wall/prop/V2V/arrest jolts + steering/redline/drift rumble) in local split-screen was replayed from the wrong car after picking a non-default arrangement on the "CHOOSE YOUR SCREEN" position screen. Root cause: ff_local_actor_slot() (td5_input.c) resolved the actor via g_actorSlotForView[player] -- the pane->displayed-car map, which the position picker PERMUTES -- so player p's wheel/pad felt whatever car pane p happened to show, not the car player p drives (P1 rumbled from other players'/AI cars). The driven-car binding is identity (player p drives actor slot p; original @0x4288E0 has no view indirection), matching the button/camera path's view_for_player(). Fix branches ff_local_actor_slot(): NETPLAY -> td5_net_local_slot() (a client's own car is a non-zero slot, unchanged from the 2026-06-23 fix); LOCAL play (single + split-screen) -> identity (player). Device index (dev=player) and the per-actor physics-side FX arming are unchanged. FFB is output-only so golden traces are untouched. Confirm: 2-player split-screen race, pick a SWAPPED screen arrangement, crash the OTHER car into a wall -> P1's pad stays silent (only reacts to P1's own car). Regression check: netplay-loopback selftest stays green; on a net client the wheel still feels its own (non-zero-slot) car.

summary: RACE OPTIONS power-ups shows OFF / CASUAL / CHAOS
detail: The RACE OPTIONS screen (Screen_RaceOptions, reached from track-select in both single-player and MP split-screen setup) exposed power-ups as a 2-state OFF/ON toggle (td5_raceopts_value/td5_raceopts_cycle used on_off[powerups & 1] and powerups ^= 1), which hid the CHAOS tier even though the arcade backend (td5_arcade.c, g_td5.ini.powerups==2) and the Game Options screen (td5_gameopts, powerups_lv[]={OFF,CASUAL,CHAOS}) already implement all three states. Fixed RO_POWERUPS to mirror the 3-state model: value now reads powerups_lv[clamp(powerups,0,2)] and cycle steps 0->1->2->0. Confirm: open RACE OPTIONS from a split-screen MP race setup, scroll POWER-UPS -> it cycles OFF, CASUAL, CHAOS (not just OFF/ON); pick CHAOS and start the race -> a power-up box appears in every lane (Mashed-style chaos spawn).

summary: Shift-up / shift-down arrow indicators on the rev dial
detail: New PORT enhancement (td5_hud.c, speedometer block): a flashing UP triangle (green) draws just above the rev dial when engine revs reach the top of the range (default top 10%, i.e. revs >= 90% of redline) prompting a shift up; a flashing DOWN triangle (amber) draws when revs fall too low in a forward gear (default <= 25% of redline, gear 2nd/byte-3 or higher = lugging) prompting a shift down. Only one shows at a time, drawn per-pane so each split-screen player sees their own, blinking ~5.5 Hz off td5_plat_time_ms. Active in ALL race modes incl. drag. Gear byte 0=R 1=N 2=1st..7=6th; up shown only in a forward gear below top gear, down only in 2nd gear or higher. Knobs TD5RE_SHIFT_INDICATOR (1=on default,0=off), TD5RE_SHIFT_UP_PCT (default 90), TD5RE_SHIFT_DOWN_PCT (default 25). Confirm: drive with a manual gearbox (drag mode forces manual) -> green up-arrow flashes near the redline, amber down-arrow flashes when bogging the engine in a high gear; verify it appears in every pane of a split-screen race and does not show in neutral/reverse.

summary: Analog steering centre deadzone (no more phantom self-steer)
detail: New PORT fix (td5_input.c, analog Path B): a worn/off-centre analog stick reported a small non-zero X axis with hands off the stick, so the car steered to one side on its own -- reported in 5-player split-screen on player 1. Added a centre deadzone that zeros deflection within +/-DZ of centre, then LINEARLY RESCALES the remaining span back onto the full range so full lock is still reached at full deflection (no loss of steering range -- steering hard off a wall stays responsive). Applies to analog stick steering only; digital/keyboard is untouched. Stacks on top of any platform DirectInput deadzone. Knob TD5RE_STEER_DEADZONE (raw axis units out of ~250, default 20; 0 = faithful/off). Confirm with a controller (ideally the multi-pad 4-5 player split-screen setup that showed the drift): with hands off the stick the car tracks straight in every pane, and steering still reaches full lock and counter-steers off a wall without feeling sluggish. Tune with TD5RE_STEER_DEADZONE if 20 is too much or too little.

summary: Dynamic per-player traffic cap (each racer anchors up to 16, shared pool)
detail: Traffic used to have a single global on-road cap (max 16 = the whole pool). Now each racer (human OR AI) anchors its own traffic bubble and the effective cap = per-anchor volume budget (up to 16) times the number of spatially SEPARATE racer clusters, bounded by the traffic pool. Racers close together fall in one cluster and SHARE a single budget; a racer that pulls more than one bubble-radius away forms its own cluster and opens a fresh budget; once the pool is exhausted separated racers COMPETE for it (a far-ahead racer eats into the others' share). Implementation (td5_ai_traffic.c): trf_anchor_count() enumerates active racers (humans + AI opponents, contiguous low slots); trf_dyn_cluster_count() union-finds anchors within a share radius; trf_dyn_cap() = per*clusters clamped to TD5_MAX_TRAFFIC_SLOTS; min_player_dist + starved_player_span now scan ALL anchors so AI keep/refill their own bubbles; the ACTIVE retire test becomes union-of-bubbles (keep a car within front_keep of ANY anchor) when the feature is on. Traffic pool raised 16->64 (TD5_MAX_TRAFFIC_SLOTS) and the render/per-slot array bound TD5_ACTOR_MAX_TOTAL_SLOTS raised 32->80 in lockstep (static-asserted equal in td5_game.c) so slots 32-79 aren't out-of-bounds in the render loop. The 64 pool = ceiling of ~4 fully-separated 16-car bubbles; concurrent count is dynamic (16 x clusters, clamped to 64), NOT a fixed 64. Knobs: TD5RE_TRAFFIC_PERPLAYER_CAP=0 restores the single global cap; TD5RE_TRAFFIC_SHARE_SPANS=<n> overrides the share radius (default = despawn + scaled spawn-max). Verified: multi-AI Moscow race - clusters=1 bunched (eff_cap=16), and forcing separation gave clusters=2/3/4 -> eff_cap=32/48/64 (16 x clusters, clamped at 64); on_road reached 48 with no crash at up to 80 actors; structure lint clean. NOTE: this changes multi-racer traffic distribution so the golden Moscow/Pelton trace hashes will differ and need re-recording. PERF: watch frame time on a busy split-screen / full-grid race approaching 64 concurrent traffic (up to 80 total actors). Confirm: play with several AI and a split-screen partner - traffic is dense around every driver, thins only when the pool is spread thin across far-apart drivers.

summary: Traffic Battle keeps spawning traffic (wrecks auto-clear after 10s)
detail: In Traffic Battle, traffic volume is forced to Very-High so the concurrent traffic cap is already at the pool max (16). A wrecked traffic car was a PERMANENT wreck (TD5RE_WRECK_PERMANENT default ON -> ticks=-1) that kept its ACTIVE slot and kept counting toward the cap; it was only freed if the distance corridor happened to retire it. When wrecks pile up faster than the corridor clears them (heavy ramming, or a circuit where the corridor wraps) all 16 slots fill with permanent wrecks, on_road pins at the cap, and the dynamic spawner is gated off -> "traffic stops spawning partway through a battle". Fix (td5_ai_traffic.c): in battle mode a wrecked traffic car now ages a per-slot counter (s_trf_wreck_age) while ACTIVE+broken, and once it passes the despawn threshold it is faded out and its slot returned to the pool regardless of distance -- so fresh traffic keeps coming. Default 300 ticks (~10s @30Hz). Knobs: TD5RE_BATTLE_WRECK_DESPAWN=0 restores the permanent wreck; TD5RE_BATTLE_WRECK_DESPAWN_TICKS=<30..1800> tunes the delay. Scoped to Traffic Battle only (other modes keep permanent wrecks). Confirm: start a Traffic Battle, wreck a lot of oncoming cars near a spot / on a circuit -> wrecks visibly fade out ~10s after crashing and new traffic keeps spawning for the whole battle (previously the road went empty). Watch log/race.log for 'traffic_dyn_despawn ... wreck_expired=1'.

summary: Crash screen-shake gated so it doesn't rattle constantly in a crowded pack (UNVALIDATED)
detail: Bisecting a reported SUSTAINED split-screen camera wobble ("keeps going until the end of the race") pointed at the crash screen-shake (td5_camera_compute_crash_shake): td5_physics_get_crash_fx reports only the LATEST crash per slot, so in a 5-6 car pack continuous acute impacts keep resetting the shake's age to 0 and it never decays = a persistent rattle. Added a gate in td5_camera.c: (1) a camera-shake magnitude FLOOR (TD5RE_CRASH_SHAKE_MIN_MAG, default 500000 = 2x the physics acute threshold) so light pack bumps don't shake, only genuine hits; (2) a re-trigger COOLDOWN (TD5RE_CRASH_SHAKE_COOLDOWN, default 18 ticks) after a shake's full decay window before a NEW crash can re-arm, with the armed event cached so its decay is rendered from a stable copy immune to age-reset. Render-only. Whole gate reverts with TD5RE_CRASH_SHAKE_GATE=0. IMPORTANT - UNVALIDATED: this could NOT be confirmed headless because AI cars never crash acutely (0 crash-fx events even with traffic+cops), so the earlier "crash-shake is the wobble cause" bisect was a noise/frame-count artifact and is NOT proven. Needs a REAL crash-heavy 5-player repro to confirm. Confirm: run a crowded split-screen race with lots of contact -> compare default (gated) vs TD5RE_CRASH_SHAKE_GATE=0 (old, rattly) vs TD5RE_CRASH_SHAKE=0 (no shake at all). If the sustained wobble only goes away with CRASH_SHAKE=0 and the gate doesn't help, crash-shake magnitude/duration needs further tuning; if the gate already calms it, ship as-is. If NONE of them change it, the wobble is faithful pack physics (cars knocked around), not crash-shake.

summary: Chase camera no longer wobbles at the start of races after the first (split-screen)
detail: In multiplayer split-screen (5-6 panes) the chase camera could jolt/wobble at the START of the 2nd/3rd race in a session, on one or more panes, sometimes persisting. Root cause: td5_camera_set_preset (the per-race camera init from InitRace) only re-anchored the per-viewport smoothing/pose filters as a side effect of LoadCameraPresetForView, which runs ONLY for panes whose actor lookup succeeds (v < viewport_count, g_actor_table_base set, actor != NULL). Any pane that missed kept the PREVIOUS race's prev-pose, so the new race's first frame glided prev->cur across a teleport = start-of-race wobble, recurring per race per pane. The all-viewport fixer td5_camera_snap_smoothing() existed but was only wired to pause-resume, never race start; the recovery-glide arrays (s_recov_*) and wall-avoid clip ratios (g_camWallClipRatio/Apply) were never reset per race either. Fix (td5_camera.c): td5_camera_set_preset now UNCONDITIONALLY re-anchors smoothing + clears recovery-glide + resets wall-clip ratios to 1.0 for all 9 viewports at every race start. Render-only (camera never feeds the sim) so no physics/AI/replay/golden-trace impact. Knob TD5RE_CAM_RACE_SNAP=0 reverts. NOTE: this targets the START-of-race glide; a SUSTAINED wobble that keeps going through the race is a separate mechanism (FPS-coupled wall-avoid damping and/or crash-shake) not addressed here. Confirm: run several consecutive split-screen races (5-6 players, e.g. Jarash then Italy then Munich) -> no camera jolt at the start of the 2nd/3rd race on any pane.

summary: Device-lost recovery no longer crashes on the first frame back
detail: After a GPU TDR the recovery path (Backend_RecreateDevice + td5_plat_render_recover_textures) logged 'DEVICE RECOVERED ... rendering resumed' but the FIRST post-recovery frame NULL-derefed deep inside the NVIDIA driver (nvwgf2um.dll, crash.log access=00000000, whole stack in the driver). Root cause: recover_textures only refreshes the texture-page registry + main RT, so any other GPU-backed WrapperSurface/WrapperTexture (HUD/fade/frontend textures bound via Dev3_SetTexture) kept a dangling SRV from the freed device and handed it straight to PSSetShaderResources. Seen after a TDR while exiting the attract/demo race. Fix (ddraw_wrapper): Dev3_SetTexture now brings the parent surface device-current (WrapperSurface_EnsureDeviceCurrent, cheap generation early-out) before reading its SRV, rebuilding it from retained CPU pixels; EnsureDeviceCurrent also re-syncs the linked texture wrapper's cached SRV; Surface4_Release nulls the texture's back-pointer so the device-current guard can't deref a freed surface; and cached current_srv pointers (global + rec-ctx) are nulled on device release. Verified with TD5RE_FORCE_DEVICE_LOST=900 on an AutoRace: forced TDR at frame 903 recovered to generation=3/4 and the process kept rendering with NO crash.log (pre-fix this always wrote crash.log and died). Confirm: with TD5RE_FORCE_DEVICE_LOST=<frame> the game blips and keeps running; and a real TDR (e.g. finishing on Montego Bay) recovers without a crash instead of a black-screen/kill.

summary: View Replay cinematic cameras capped view distance (TDR guard)
detail: The trackside/orbit replay cameras view the track from a distance so the whole fwd/back span window is in frame at once (unlike the chase cam), which spiked a single draw past the GPU TDR watchdog ("draw ran too long" -> DEVICE_HUNG) during View Replay at high VIEW distances. td5_render_mesh.c now caps the effective view distance to 0.65 while a ghost replay is actually showing its trackside cameras (g_replay_mode && trackside_ready); live gameplay and the chase-fallback replay are untouched. Knob TD5RE_REPLAY_CAM_VIEW_DIST (default 0.65, clamp [0.15,1.0]; 1.0 disables). NOTE: separate from the recurring nvwgf2um.dll driver crash seen on transition/results screens. Confirm: View Replay on Moscow at ViewDistance=100 shows cinematic cameras without a GPU hang; distant scenery pops a little sooner during the replay only.

summary: View Replay ends at end of recording (no freeze on last pose)
detail: Ghost View Replay poses from a fixed buffer and had no natural stop -- past the last recorded frame it froze on the final pose forever, very visible for a recording cut short by END RACE NOW. It now fades out to results when playback reaches the end of the recording (same path as the ESC abort). Confirm: use END RACE NOW early, View Replay -> it plays the captured portion then returns to results on its own; ESC still exits early.

summary: Dev pause menu: END RACE NOW available in single-player
detail: Dev builds now show END RACE NOW in the pause menu in single-player (release keeps it local-split-screen-MP-only) so QA can force-finish and jump to View Replay without driving the whole race. Confirm in a dev build: SP pause menu has END RACE NOW and it force-finishes to results; a release build still hides it in SP.

summary: View Replay trackside cameras cut between shots again
detail: Ghost-state View Replay skips the sim (physics/track walker), so the actor track-position block at +0x080 (track_span_raw etc.) -- normally produced each tick by the walker -- was frozen at the countdown-end value because td5_replay.c only recorded/restored the pose, not that block. SelectTracksideCameraProfile (td5_camera.c) keys the cinematic trackside replay camera on actor+0x80, so it never switched view for the whole replay; a frozen shot whose look-at kept panning to follow the receding car also looked like the camera "moving around" at the start. Fix: TD5_ReplaySnap now records the +0x080 block (span raw/normalized/accumulated/high-water, contact vertices A/B, sub-lane) each tick and replay_pose_actor restores it, so the span advances during replay. Record path is read-only -> normal sim/goldens unaffected. Confirm: drive a race on a track with authored trackside cameras (e.g. Moscow, Newcastle), hit View Replay -> the camera CUTS between trackside shots as the car advances (not one static/panning shot), and there is no camera drift at the race start.

summary: Frame-rate cap when VSync off (prevents GPU-overload TDR)
detail: The results/frontend loop was presenting effectively unsynced at ~35000 FPS (log: game_state=1, fps~37000, fe_present~0ms), flooding the GPU with back-to-back submissions and no idle -- the submission storm that drove the race->results transition into a GPU DEVICE_HUNG (TDR / black screen). Added a frame-rate cap in td5_plat_present (td5_platform_win32_window.c): when the present is effectively unsynced (caller vsync=0 OR Display VSync off), it paces successive presents to a max FPS via td5_plat_time_us + a sleep(bulk)+spin(remainder) wait. No effect when VSync is on (vblank already paces). Knob TD5RE_FRAME_CAP=<fps>, default 300 (0 = uncapped, e.g. benchmarking). 300 is ~100x below the rate that hung the GPU and imperceptible for play/menus. This is the PREVENTION that pairs with the device-lost RECOVERY shipped the same day. Confirm: run with VSync OFF (Display options or INI VSync=0), sit on the results screen / a menu -> FPS overlay shows ~300 not tens of thousands, GPU load drops, and finishing a Montego Bay race no longer hangs. With VSync ON, FPS still follows refresh unchanged. TD5RE_FRAME_CAP=0 restores uncapped.

summary: GPU device-lost recovery (no more black screen on TDR)
detail: On some tracks (reported on Montego Bay) finishing a 1-lap race caused a GPU DEVICE_HUNG (a Windows TDR: a draw/dispatch ran too long, seen with the results screen running uncapped at ~35k FPS). The D3D11 wrapper already latched the removed device to avoid a driver NULL-deref crash (Backend_NoteDeviceRemoved -> g_backend.device_removed) but had NO recovery, so the screen went black permanently and the process had to be killed (log/gpu_device_lost.log). Added Backend_RecreateDevice() in the wrapper: on a latched device-lost, the present path (plat_try_recover_device in td5_platform_win32_window.c) releases all backend-owned GPU objects, recreates the D3D11 device + swap chain + render targets + shaders + state objects + buffers (shared Backend_InitDeviceResources so create/recreate can't drift), bumps a new g_backend.device_generation, then rebuilds every game texture from its retained CPU copy (sys_buffer) -- eagerly for the texture-page registry + main RT (td5_plat_render_recover_textures), lazily for any other surface via a generation stamp checked in WrapperSurface_FlushDirty/EnsureDeviceCurrent. Recovery is rate-limited (~every 30 frames) and capped (240 attempts) so a truly dead adapter doesn't spin forever. Test with TD5RE_FORCE_DEVICE_LOST=<frame> (dev builds) to simulate a TDR. Confirm: finish a race on Montego Bay and other tracks -> no permanent black screen; and with TD5RE_FORCE_DEVICE_LOST set, the game blips and keeps rendering with textures intact (check log for 'DEVICE RECOVERED').

summary: View Replay reproduces the driven race exactly (ghost-state)
detail: View Replay was a deterministic re-simulation (recorded only the two player-input DWORDs + the per-race RNG seed, then re-ran physics/AI/dynamic-traffic-spawn hoping for an identical result). It drifted: FP accumulation over thousands of ticks plus spawn-cadence coupling made opponents and traffic diverge ("not the race I drove"). Replaced with a full ghost-state recorder (new td5_replay.c): during the real race every actor's per-tick transform (world_pos, rotation_matrix, euler/display angles, speed/slip/gear/brake/wheel angles) is snapshotted for the player, all AI opponents AND traffic; on View Replay the sim (td5_ai_tick + race-end brake + td5_physics_tick + metrics + arcade) is skipped entirely and actors are posed straight from the buffer with velocities zeroed. Traffic is not spawned by logic -- its exact per-tick draw alpha is recorded and re-applied via td5_ai_traffic_replay_force, so which traffic cars are on-road (and their fade-in/out) reproduces precisely. Memory-only (no disk). Knob TD5RE_GHOST_REPLAY=0 reverts to the legacy input re-sim. Confirm: drive a race with traffic + AI opponents (e.g. Moscow and a circuit like Newcastle), hit View Replay -> every opponent and traffic car follows the same path/positions as the driven race, no drift; also confirm split-screen and a traffic-heavy track.

summary: Headlights stay off in daytime on Montego Bay / Tokyo
detail: The auto-headlight sky-darkness threshold (s_auto_sky_thr in td5_render_mesh.c) was 110, calibrated only on Moscow(63.5) vs a ~124 daytime reference. It wrongly flagged bright DAYTIME tracks whose average FORWSKY luma lands in the 95-117 band -- Montego Bay (95.6) and Tokyo (104.4) -- as "dark everywhere", so those cars ran headlights the whole race in broad daylight. Re-measured all 19 native FORWSKY averages: genuinely dark = Washington 35.6, Moscow 63.5; bright daylight starts at Montego 95.6. Lowered the threshold to 80 (midpoint of 63.5 and 95.6). Confirm: race Montego Bay and Tokyo in daytime -> car headlights OFF (no auto-glow), while Moscow and Washington still auto-light. Knob TD5RE_LIGHT_AUTO_SKY overrides.

summary: Uphill slope slow-down softened 65% (cars hold speed on climbs)
detail: The PORT-ONLY gravity-along-slope uphill deceleration term (td5_physics.c section 14a-slope, knob TD5RE_SLOPE_DECEL) had its default multiplier lowered from 2.0 to 0.70, i.e. the uphill decel "debuff" is now 65% less effective (0.70 = 35% of the old 2.0 strength). Downhill (accelerating) side is untouched (always x1). The gear-1-free crawl, top-speed light scale, and mass-relative weight scale all still compose on top. Restore the old feel with TD5RE_SLOPE_DECEL=2.0. NOTE: this changes the SIM, so the Moscow + TD6 Pelton golden traces must be re-recorded (TD5RE_TRACE_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1). Confirm on a hilly track (e.g. Courmayeur/Scotland) that climbing a grade bleeds off noticeably less speed than before, and that downhill behaviour is unchanged.

summary: Self-test render-golden layer catches visual regressions
detail: New dev/QA net in td5_selftest.c: the two golden races (race-golden-moscow, race-golden-pelton) now also read back the composited backbuffer at 4 fixed sim ticks (130/220/310/400) via Backend_RequestCapture/GetCapture, reduce each frame to a coarse 16x16 luma grid, and compare against td5mod/src/td5re/render_goldens.txt with L1 + per-cell distance thresholds (TD5RE_SELFTEST_RENDER_L1/_CELL). Golden races run the debug overlay off and use dynamic fast-forward (cruise at the suite FF through the countdown and between capture points, drop to 1x only in a short runway around each capture tick) so the captured frame is reproducible without paying full real-time for the whole race. A 'V' verdict row is added to selftest_report.{csv,md}. Re-record with TD5RE_TRACE_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1 (same run records both trace + render goldens). This is the class that catches the recent race-end wipe translucency + banner z-fight bugs. Confirm: full suite records goldens on the first update run, a clean rerun reports the 'V' rows PASS, and deliberately regressing a visual (e.g. force the wipe translucent) makes the matching 'V' row FAIL with a nonzero exit code.

summary: Game Options save on Back exit (TUTORIAL off sticks)
detail: Game Options previously only committed s_game_option_* into g_td5.ini when the OK button was pressed; leaving via Back/Escape silently discarded every toggle. Root-caused from a TUTDIAG log: toggling TUTORIAL off then backing out left tutorial_overlay=1, so the overlay still armed at race start. The commit is now shared (td5_gameopts_commit) and also runs on the Back path (frontend_central_return_back when leaving GAME_OPTIONS). Confirm: Game Options -> TUTORIAL -> OFF, leave with Back (NOT OK), start a race -> overlay does NOT show; toggle ON + Back -> it returns; also confirm other rows (Traffic, Cops, Damage, etc.) persist across Back and a relaunch.

summary: Breaking down no longer loses the race (force-recovery + ghost)
detail: With CAR DAMAGE on, a knocked-out human car no longer counts as done (the race waits instead of ending around you). A centred CAR BROKE DOWN / PRESS <R or SELECT> TO CONTINUE prompt shows; pressing recovery tows the car 30 spans back (TD5RE_BREAKDOWN_SPANS_BACK), fully repairs it (TD5RE_BREAKDOWN_REPAIR_PCT), glides the chase camera to the new spot (TD5RE_RECOVERY_CAM_MS), and grants a ~3s invulnerable translucent ghost that flickers before ending (TD5RE_GHOST_TICKS/_BLINK_TICKS/_ALPHA). Ordinary stuck (not broken) recovery is unchanged (in-place, partial). Net path routes the request through the merged control_bits so every peer recovers on the same lockstep round - NEEDS A LAN TEST to confirm no desync. Confirm: crash until broken down, prompt appears, press to continue -> 30 spans back + camera glide + blinking ghost + invulnerable during ghost; race does not end while you sit broken down.

summary: Montego Bay countdown camera fly-in restored
detail: Montego Bay (level 39) was the only track excluded from the race-start orbiting fly-in cinematic (k_flyin_blocked_levels safety net) because the camera dipped underground / through the water during the 3-2-1. That root cause (cold-spawn garbage linear_velocity_y amplified into the camera eye + car mesh) was fixed by the |vy| clamp, so Montego is un-blocked and now runs the normal fly-in. Confirm on a Montego race (single-player AND split-screen) that the countdown camera sweeps in like other tracks and the car/eye never sink below the ground or water.

summary: Race-end wipe (when NOT finishing 1st) is solid black, not see-through
detail: The directional race-end wipe (black bars closing in for any non-1st finish / quit-to-menu) rendered ~50% translucent so the race showed through it. Root cause: the bars used a textured OPAQUE_LINEAR draw with the color-keyed FADEWHT page, which tripped the foliage-AA classifier (Backend_IsFoliageAA: alpha-test on + has_alpha + blend off), and Backend_ApplyStateCache then OVERRODE the opaque blend with SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA. Fixed by drawing the bars via td5_plat_render_draw_tris_flat (BLEND_OPAQUE, alpha-test off, bypasses the state cache/classifier). Confirm by losing/quitting a race and watching the wipe fully cover the screen, single-player AND split-screen, with foliage AA on.

summary: Fences/foliage/scenery render both sides, not one-face / missing textures
detail: Native-banner geometry scan (td5_track_scan_banner_pages) is now OFF by default (TD5RE_BANNER_PAIR_CULL=1 to re-enable). It was detecting 'coincident reverse-wound panels' to one-sided-cull native overhead banners, but false-flagged double-sided fences/guardrails/foliage - and pages SHARED with scenery - so the cull removed their camera-facing side: fences appeared on one side only and scenery lost textures on every native track. TD6 tracks unaffected (keep the k_td6_banner_pages hand list). Trade-off: native TD5 overhead START/sign banners (Tokyo/Moscow) may z-fight/mirror again - confirm whether that's acceptable or needs the narrower per-page fix. Confirm on Scotland/Edinburgh + Moscow + Tokyo + a few others: fences render both sides, no missing-texture faces on scenery, and check the START banners.

summary: Police reliably start chasing when you speed past a cop
detail: The cop ACQUIRE window was widened (gap [0,15]->[-8,60] spans, TD5RE_COP_TRIGGER_LO/HI) and the acquire speed relaxed to 85% of the speeding threshold (TD5RE_COP_TRIGGER_SPEED_PCT). Diag showed 329/330 idle-cop rejects failed the old gap gate (cops sat 250-290 spans away). Confirm in a Cops-on race that driving fast past a cruising cop actually triggers a chase, on both human single-player and split-screen.

summary: Crashed cops recover and re-engage instead of staying wrecked
detail: A cop that takes a hard hit no longer becomes a PERMANENT wreck; it gets a self-clearing recovery timer (TD5RE_COP_WRECK_RECOVER, TD5RE_COP_WRECK_TICKS, default ~5s) like a racer, so it rejoins the chase. Regular traffic still permanently wrecks. Confirm a cop that rams you and crashes gets going again and resumes pursuit rather than parking for the race.

summary: Traffic changes lanes smoothly (no rapid flip-flop)
detail: Lane-change hysteresis added to the smart-traffic chooser (TD5RE_TRAFFIC_LANE_HYST, MARGIN, COOLDOWN): a car commits to a target lane and holds it until a clearly better lane appears + a cooldown lapses. Diag showed 398 lane-flips with cars alternating lanes every ~2 ticks. Confirm traffic no longer jerks side-to-side and the flow looks natural.

summary: Wedged/stuck traffic frees itself instead of blocking the road
detail: Universal unstick backstop (TD5RE_TRAFFIC_UNSTICK, default on): any non-cop traffic car with zero span progress for ~3s is reset in place (realigned, velocity cleared, progress reseeded) so it rejoins the flow. Diag showed 24/36 stalls were low-speed wedges that AntiFreeze/collision-escape never caught, with 3 cars stuck permanently. Confirm cars no longer sit frozen at track hotspots.

summary: End-of-race transition is opaque; race doesn't bleed through RESULTS
detail: At race end the RESULTS/menu screen no longer shows the fading race scene through it (the player car dissolving over the results table). Root cause was the D3D11 flip-model swapchain retaining stale race frames when the clear-skipping frontend took over; now a forced clear runs for the first frames after a screen entry. Confirm the race->RESULTS handoff is a clean opaque cut on single-player AND split-screen MP. NOTE: a separate race-START edge-smear at non-default window/DPI is still under investigation.

summary: START/FINISH banners + track signs render solid, not 50% see-through
detail: Native TD5 track type-2 texture pages (START/FINISH gantry banners, signs, pennants) previously rendered ~50% translucent; now solid, matching the original (BindRaceTexturePage type-2 = color-key opaque, z-write off). Confirm on Montego + Moscow start lines and other tracks' signage.

detail: Drive through a track's authored lighting zones (dusk section, tunnel) and confirm the intended colour tint actually shows, rather than looking uniformly lit everywhere.

summary: Lighting v2: headlights don't shine through walls (N.L)
detail: At night with headlights on, put a wall/building between the headlight and a surface behind it -- the beam should NOT shine through; lighting should respect the surface normal (N.L) and be occluded by geometry.

summary: Lighting v2: Mode=0 looks identical to the old build (A/B)
detail: A/B test: set [Lighting] Mode=0 and confirm the scene looks the same as before the lighting v2 rework -- this mode is a faithfulness fallback, so any visible difference here is a regression.

summary: PLAYER NAME option: results row + high-score prefill
detail: Set your player name in Game Options, finish a race, and confirm your typed name (not 'PLAYER 1') appears in the results row; also check the high-score name-entry screen prefills with the same name instead of starting blank.

summary: Damage bar: top-centre + pause-style blue-red fill
detail: In a race with car damage on, confirm the health bar sits top-centre and fills/drains using the same blue-to-red gradient style as the pause menu's bars, not a plain solid colour.

summary: Damage bar on: checkpoint timer sits below it
detail: With the damage bar visible and checkpoint timers enabled, confirm the checkpoint timer is positioned below the damage bar rather than overlapping or sitting above it.

summary: Police pullover: brakes hold all the way through (no coast gap)
detail: Get pulled over by a cop and watch the deceleration -- braking should be continuous all the way to a stop, with no gap where the car coasts freely partway through the sequence.

summary: Pause menu: END RACE NOW only in local split-screen MP (not SP/net)
detail: Open the pause menu in single-player and in a networked race and confirm END RACE NOW is absent in both; open it in local split-screen MP and confirm it IS present there.

summary: Pause menu: RESTART/QUIT/EXIT/LOBBY ask YES/NO confirm in split-screen MP
detail: In local split-screen MP, open the pause menu and pick RESTART, QUIT, EXIT, or LOBBY -- each should raise a YES/NO prompt before acting, not execute immediately.

summary: Pause menu (single-player): RESTART/QUIT/EXIT act immediately, no confirm
detail: In single-player, open the pause menu and pick RESTART, QUIT, or EXIT -- these should act immediately with no YES/NO prompt, unlike split-screen MP.

summary: END RACE NOW: next race camera starts normal (was stuck shifted)
detail: Use END RACE NOW to force-finish a race, then start the next race and check the chase camera begins in its normal default position, not stuck shifted from the forced finish.

summary: Track walker: no span warp on degenerate quads (race normally)
detail: Race normally on any track and watch for a sudden position 'warp'/teleport as the car crosses a span boundary -- degenerate (malformed) track quads used to snap the walker incorrectly.

summary: Headlights: per-pixel beams flood the road (deferred light pass)
detail: At night with headlights on, confirm the beam is a proper per-pixel lit cone flooding the road (via the deferred lighting pass), correctly lighting bumps/curves, not a flat decal.

summary: Headlights auto-on in rain/overcast/dusk, off in bright daylight
detail: Drive across different weather/time conditions without touching the headlight control -- they should switch on automatically in rain/overcast/dusk and stay off in bright daylight.

summary: Headlights: verify on a sunny track they stay OFF (Maui/Sydney)
detail: Race Maui or Sydney (bright, sunny reference tracks) and confirm headlights stay OFF the whole race -- the negative-case check for the auto-headlight logic above.

summary: Split cup: later-race player can always accelerate (was camera-only)
detail: In a split-screen cup with multiple races, check a non-lead player's car in race 2+ can accelerate normally -- a bug had only the camera advancing correctly while the car itself stayed throttle-limited.

summary: Pause menu: END RACE NOW force-finishes (YES/NO confirm; any player)
detail: Open the pause menu as ANY player (not just host) in split-screen and pick END RACE NOW; confirm it raises a YES/NO prompt and, on YES, force-finishes for everyone.

summary: END RACE NOW: places ranked by current track progress, no DNFs
detail: After using END RACE NOW, check results rank every player by how far along the track they'd actually gotten -- nobody should show as DNF; everyone gets a placed result.

summary: END RACE NOW: net race ends + shows results on all machines together
detail: In a networked race, have one player trigger END RACE NOW and confirm the race ends and the results screen appears at roughly the same time on every connected machine.

summary: Alt+Enter fullscreen uses the display's native refresh, not 60Hz
detail: Press Alt+Enter to toggle fullscreen during gameplay and check the observed refresh rate matches your monitor's native refresh (e.g. 120/144Hz), not capped at 60Hz.

summary: Paint: SELECT CAR PAINT panel - secondary colour + pattern + 32 presets
detail: Open SELECT CAR PAINT and confirm it offers a secondary colour picker, a pattern selector, and roughly 32 preset combinations, not just the single primary-colour picker from before.

summary: Paint: Two-Tone/Stripes/Split show in BOTH menu preview and in-race body
detail: Pick a Two-Tone, Stripes, or Split pattern in the paint panel and confirm it renders on both the car-select preview AND the actual car body once in a race -- one-place-only is a bug.

summary: Lane Assist at a fork: picks one branch a few spans early, not the divider
detail: Turn Lane Assist on and approach a fork -- it should commit to one branch a few spans BEFORE the fork rather than aiming at the physical divider/wall between the branches.

summary: Split: one pad seen as 2 gamepads no longer joins as 2 players (cam bleed)
detail: If you have a controller Windows enumerates as two devices, confirm the split-screen lobby only lets it join as ONE player -- it could previously join as two, causing camera/input bleed between panes.

summary: Reset car (split-screen): resets in place, no teleport-to-start/wall
detail: In split-screen, press reset-car on a stuck/wedged car and confirm it resets IN PLACE (same spot, corrected orientation), not teleporting to the track start or into a wall.

summary: Reset car: fully repairs (health+dents); un-sticks a knocked-out car
detail: With damage on, wreck/knock out a car, then reset-car and confirm it comes back with full health AND cleared dents -- specifically test un-sticking a fully knocked-out car, not just a lightly damaged one.

summary: Tutorial overlay now shows at the START of every race (was once-ever)
detail: Start several races in a row (gamepad connected) and confirm the controller tutorial overlay appears at the start of EACH one, not just the very first race ever played.

summary: Game Options: new TUTORIAL on/off row turns the overlay off
detail: Open Game Options, find the TUTORIAL row, toggle it OFF, then start a race and confirm the tutorial overlay no longer appears (toggle back ON to confirm it returns).

summary: Game Options paginated (2 pages, < PREV / NEXT >); all rows fit, values/arrows OK
detail: Open Game Options and confirm it's split across 2 pages with < PREV / NEXT >, every row is fully visible with nothing clipped, and each row's value + selector arrows still work after paging.

summary: Car defaults to your PROFILE colour (TD6 exact / TD5 nearest); PAINT overrides
detail: Set an accent colour on your profile, pick a car without touching PAINT -- it should default to your profile colour (exact match for TD6, nearest available for TD5). Then set PAINT and confirm it overrides the profile default.

summary: MP profile: typed-but-unsaved NEW name auto-saves when the race starts
detail: On the MP profile screen, type a new profile name but do NOT explicitly save, then start the race -- the typed name should auto-save as a real profile rather than being discarded.

summary: Celebrity leaderboard: unraced tracks show celeb names (not Frank/Ben)
detail: Look at the leaderboard for a track you have never raced -- default names should be celebrity-style (e.g. Michael, Lewis, Ayrton) rather than the old generic Frank/Ben. Detection is exact-match against the original default names, so a track with a real saved score should be unaffected.

summary: Celebrity leaderboard: CelebrityNamesAPI=1 → fetches from randomuser.me
detail: Set CelebrityNamesAPI=1 (needs internet) and confirm celebrity names are fetched live from randomuser.me instead of the built-in static table; check the log for a successful fetch and that names apply and flush to the save immediately after load.

summary: Pause menu RADIO slider (row 2) sets radio volume live
detail: Open the pause menu during a race with radio playing, find the RADIO slider on row 2, and move it -- volume should change live, not just on menu close.

summary: Radio: quiet by default + mutes when minimized/paused/in menus
detail: Confirm the radio starts quiet by default and mutes automatically when the window is minimized, the game is paused, or you're back in frontend menus.

summary: Radio: live station plays during a race (needs internet)
detail: With internet available and radio enabled, start a race and confirm a live internet radio station actually plays audio during the race -- needs a real network connection to verify.

summary: Music seam wired: no audio regression (jukebox/race/pause)
detail: Move through jukebox/menu music, into a race, and into the pause menu, listening for any regression -- no missing tracks, no jarring cutoffs, no failure to resume across states.

summary: Traffic: visible ~60% further on open tracks (no short-range pop-out)
detail: On an open (non-TD6) track, watch traffic ahead as you approach at speed -- it should become visible noticeably further away (~60% further) rather than popping in at short range. Knob: TD5RE_TRAFFIC_VIEW_DIST (default ~1.6x); TD6 tracks are perf-capped separately, so test on a faithful TD5 track like Moscow.

summary: Damage Bar VISIBLE for every split-screen player (was invisible before)
detail: In split-screen with car damage on, confirm EVERY player's pane shows their own damage bar -- some panes could previously have an invisible/missing bar.

summary: Damage Bar OFF (Game Options): no top bar, no wreck-out; dents stay
detail: In Game Options turn the damage bar OFF, then race and take damage -- the top bar should be hidden and the car should never wreck/knock out from zero health, but dents should still appear normally.

summary: Damage Bar toggle is global: every split-screen player gets it or none
detail: In split-screen, toggle the damage bar and confirm it applies to ALL players' panes at once -- it's a single global setting, not per-player.

summary: Cops: accel rubber-band out-drags a faster car on straights (catch up)
detail: Get chased by a cop while driving a notably faster car and watch a long straight -- the cop should accelerate hard enough to close the gap despite lower top speed (an acceleration rubber-band, not a top-speed cheat). Knob: TD5RE_COP_CHASE_ACCEL (default 280). Headless verification needs TD5RE_COP_CHASE_AI=1 + PlayerIsAI=1 + AutoThrottle=0 since cops normally only chase HUMAN slots.

summary: Cops: tougher (300%); chasing cop shrugs off wall scrapes (no chase-end)
detail: Deliberately clip a chasing cop into a wall -- with durability boosted 300%, it should shrug the scrape off and keep chasing rather than the chase ending from a minor bump.

summary: Cops: ease off for corners instead of flooring into the outside wall
detail: Watch a chasing cop through a sharp corner -- it should visibly ease off the throttle for the corner rather than flooring it into the outside wall. Knob: TD5RE_COP_CORNER_EASE.

summary: Cops: pass a cluster and ALL of them chase you (no 1-cop limit)
detail: Drive past a cluster of multiple cop cars and confirm ALL of them start chasing, not just one -- the original one-chaser-per-target cap was removed.

summary: Cops: longer chase leash (110 spans) + 200% catch-up; harder to shake
detail: Get chased, then try to lose the cop by pulling ahead -- it should take noticeably longer/further to shake it: the chase persists up to a 110-span gap and catch-up is boosted 200%, so the cop keeps closing rather than giving up quickly.

summary: Traffic: stuck car no longer fades in front of you (gates on render dist)
detail: Watch traffic ahead for a car that gets stuck -- it should NOT despawn/fade while still within your render distance in front of you; the despawn gate now respects the render-cull distance (front_keep) instead of a fixed shorter range.

summary: Drag MP mode: SELECT GAME MODE -> DRAG RACE (no track pick, no AI)
detail: In multiplayer, open SELECT GAME MODE and pick DRAG RACE -- confirm it skips the normal track-selection screen entirely and adds no AI opponents; drag race MP is humans-only.

summary: Drag MP options: TRAFFIC on/off, DISTANCE, EXTRA LANES
detail: On the drag MP options screen, toggle TRAFFIC, pick a DISTANCE preset, and set EXTRA LANES, confirming each choice actually changes the race you get.

summary: Drag LONG/EPIC: strip+stadium truly extend, finish moves down it
detail: Pick LONG or EPIC and confirm the strip and stadium geometry are PHYSICALLY extended (not just a further finish marker on the original strip) -- you drive further over newly-inserted road/stadium tiles before the finish.

summary: Drag race: strip widens to one lane per car (field-size lanes)
detail: Start drag races with different player counts and confirm the strip width scales to one lane per car -- a 2-car race should be narrower than a 6-car race.

summary: Drag race: tap left/right to CHANGE LANES (NFS-Underground feel)
detail: During a drag race, tap left/right and confirm your car snaps into the adjacent lane with a quick, arcade lane-change feel, not a slow drift or no response.

summary: Drag race: longer race via TD5RE_DRAG_LENGTH (existing road reused)
detail: Set TD5RE_DRAG_LENGTH higher and confirm the drag race is proportionally longer, reusing existing road geometry rather than needing new assets.

summary: Lane Assist: road-centre aid, firmer further off; avoids grass
detail: Turn Lane Assist on, drift toward the road edge, and feel the correction -- gentle near centre, firmer further off-centre, always aiming for the drivable road (never the grass/slow lane) even at a fork. Baked constants: STRENGTH=900, MAX_YAW=400; feel previously user-confirmed 'perfect'.

summary: Lane Assist toggle: SP Game Options / MP Profile screen / L key
detail: Confirm Lane Assist can be turned on/off from THREE places -- single-player Game Options, the MP Profile screen (next to AUTO/MANUAL), and the L key live in a race -- and all three reflect the same setting.

summary: Traffic Battle: MP split-screen mode (below CUP) + solo (TD5RE_BATTLE=1)
detail: In multiplayer split-screen, find TRAFFIC BATTLE below CUP on mode-select; separately set TD5RE_BATTLE=1 and confirm you can also play it solo.

summary: Traffic Battle: WIN option MOST WRECKS or CHECKPOINTS (catch-up deadline)
detail: In Traffic Battle options, choose the win condition -- MOST WRECKS or CHECKPOINTS (a catch-up deadline) -- and test both, confirming the results/winner logic matches the chosen mode.

summary: Traffic Battle: oncoming traffic, no rivals/cops, spawn mid-track
detail: Start a Traffic Battle race and confirm traffic spawns oncoming (toward you), there are no AI rivals or cops, and players spawn mid-track rather than at a normal start line.

summary: Traffic Battle: crashes wreck at ANY angle/speed; airborne cars wreck too
detail: Hit a traffic car at various angles and speeds (including glancing hits) and confirm each registers as a wreck; also confirm a car airborne on impact still wrecks correctly.

summary: Traffic Battle: wrecked cars go translucent + pass-through (drive thru)
detail: After wrecking a traffic car, confirm its wreck goes translucent and you can drive straight through it, rather than it staying solid and blocking the lane.

summary: Traffic Battle: live WRECKS HUD; results sort/label by WRECKS
detail: During Traffic Battle confirm a live WRECKS counter is on the HUD; at the end confirm results sort/label by WRECKS rather than the normal race-position columns.

summary: Arcade: new power-ups SHIELD/EMP-FREEZE/MAGNET/ROCKET/REPAIR (HAZARD off)
detail: Play an Arcade race and grab boxes until you've seen SHIELD, EMP-FREEZE, MAGNET, ROCKET, and REPAIR; confirm each does something distinct and the old HAZARD (oil) no longer appears.

summary: Game Options: CAR TOUGHNESS + DEFORMATION levels (Low/Norm/High)
detail: Open Game Options, set CAR TOUGHNESS and DEFORMATION to different Low/Normal/High combinations, and confirm crashes feel/look different accordingly.

summary: Car damage ON all races: dents+scuff, smoke, wreck, finish orbit cam
detail: Race with damage on and confirm the full chain: dents/scuff accumulate, smoke appears on a badly damaged car, the car can wreck/knock out, and finishing triggers the orbit finish cam.

summary: Chase cam: no vertical jitter at race start on high-refresh (120/144+)
detail: On a high-refresh display, watch the chase camera closely in the first second or two of a race start -- it should be smooth with no vertical jitter/bounce. Fallback if it persists on a given rig is a terrain-tilt IIR filter, not fully confirmed on every setup.

summary: MP car select: host X/TAB menu sets everyone's car (same/slow/avg/fast)
detail: As host on MP car-select, open the X/TAB quick menu and pick 'same car', 'slowest', 'average', or 'fastest' -- confirm it reassigns EVERY player's/AI's car, not just your own.

summary: MP cup: player 1 keeps chosen car on race 2+ (no pre-cup car revert)
detail: Start an MP cup, have player 1 pick a specific car, complete race 1, and check race 2 onward -- player 1 should keep the chosen car rather than reverting to a pre-cup car.

summary: ARCADE: power-up timer bar shows the full duration (not last secs)
detail: Grab a timed power-up in Arcade and watch its HUD timer from the moment you grab it -- it should show the FULL duration counting down, not only appear in the last few seconds.

summary: ARCADE: item boxes spawn one lane closer to track centre
detail: In Arcade, compare item box placement to the road edges -- boxes should sit one lane closer to centre than the very outer edge, making them easier to reach without hugging the wall.

summary: ARCADE: power-up effects last 20% longer (NITRO/GHOST/WRECK)
detail: Grab NITRO, GHOST, and WRECK in Arcade and time each effect -- each should run about 20% longer than the previous baseline duration.

summary: Power-ups now ARCADE-only: SIMULATION shows no item boxes
detail: Start a race with Dynamics set to SIMULATION and confirm NO item boxes spawn anywhere -- power-ups are strictly Arcade-only. Watch for a dynamics-commit timing edge case where a late mode switch could still let boxes through.

summary: MP splitscreen: gold HOST tag on profile/screen/mode/car selectors
detail: As session host in split-screen MP, check the profile, position, mode-vote, and car-select screens -- your selector should show a gold HOST pill badge on all four, not just some.

summary: Split car-select 5+ players: big car + buttons|stats two columns; 7-9p car stays big
detail: Join a split-screen car-select with 5+ players -- each narrow pane should show a big car preview on top with buttons/stats in two columns below, and the preview should stay reasonably large even at 7-9 players rather than shrinking to a thumbnail.

summary: Tutorial overlay: Xbox pad diagram (gamepad only); ALL players press to start; every race
detail: Start a race with a gamepad connected -- the overlay should show a real Xbox pad diagram with arrows from each control to its action; in split-screen, the race shouldn't start until ALL players press a button, and this should happen every race, not just the first.

summary: Tutorial overlay: TutorialOverlay=2 forces (bypass gamepad gate); =0 off; never in MP/replay/trace
detail: Set TutorialOverlay=2 and confirm the overlay shows even on keyboard-only (bypassing the gamepad-only gate); set =0 and confirm it never shows. Confirm it also never appears during networked MP, replay playback, or a trace/benchmark run regardless of the setting.

summary: MP cop chase: suspects can now pick TD6 cars, not just TD5
detail: In an MP cop chase lobby, as a suspect, open car select and confirm TD6 cars are selectable alongside TD5 -- suspects were previously restricted to TD5-only.

summary: Reverse direction now works on the 7 lap circuits (Newcastle etc)
detail: Pick a 7-lap circuit (e.g. Newcastle) with Reverse enabled and confirm the race runs correctly for the full lap count -- checkpoints, finish detection, and AI routing all working, not just the first lap or two.

summary: Controller: Y changes camera; horn moved to L3 (stick click)
detail: On a gamepad, press Y and confirm it cycles the camera view; click the left stick (L3) and confirm it sounds the horn -- horn was moved off its old binding onto L3.

summary: Time trial on city tracks (HK/London): mid-track start no insta-end
detail: Run a Time Trial on a TD6 city track (Hong Kong or London) that starts mid-track via a P2P checkpoint layout, and confirm the run does NOT instantly end right after starting.

summary: Replay no longer counts as a race (MP cup keeps real results)
detail: Play back a replay and confirm it isn't counted as an actual race; specifically, watching a replay between MP cup races should NOT affect or overwrite the real cup standings.

summary: MP cop chase: bust arrow shows only when you crash a suspect
detail: As a cop, ram a suspect and confirm a bust arrow/indicator appears tied to that crash event -- it should not show from mere proximity without a crash.

summary: MP cop chase: other players' name labels hidden
detail: In MP cop chase, look at other players' cars and confirm their floating name labels are hidden -- this mode intentionally suppresses labels, unlike normal MP racing.

summary: MP cop chase: no 1st/2nd; top shows per-cop ARRESTS scoreboard
detail: Check the top HUD during MP cop chase -- it should show a per-cop ARRESTS scoreboard, not a normal 1st/2nd/3rd race-position indicator.

summary: MP cop chase: arrest needs SIREN ON; else 'turn on siren' msg
detail: As a cop, try to arrest a suspect with siren OFF -- it should NOT count, with a 'turn on siren' message; turn the siren on and confirm the same crash now registers as a valid arrest.

summary: MP cop chase: HORN toggles each cop's own siren
detail: As a cop, press HORN and confirm it toggles YOUR OWN siren (light + sound) independently of any other cop's siren state in the same race.

summary: MP mode vote: A=vote -> profile-colour border ring on mode
detail: During an MP mode vote, press A on a mode option and confirm a border ring appears around it in YOUR profile's accent colour, marking your vote.

summary: MP mode vote: more voters = more nested rings; host decides
detail: Have multiple players vote for the same mode and confirm each voter adds another nested ring (their own colour) rather than just one ring total; confirm the HOST ultimately picks the winning mode.

summary: MP mode vote: arrow disappears once a player casts their vote
detail: Before voting a player's pane shows a selection arrow; once they vote (press A), confirm that arrow disappears for them (their vote now shows via the coloured ring instead).

summary: Time Trial after a cup: no instant end / right car on Race Again / no rivals on your lane
detail: Finish an MP cup, then start a Time Trial (or Race Again) -- confirm the run doesn't instantly end, you're driving the expected car (not a leftover cup car), and no AI rivals share your lane.

summary: Snow tracks (Bern) easier: ice surface grips more, less slide
detail: Race Bern and compare handling on the icy surface -- grip should be noticeably higher and the car should slide less than the original unmodified ice physics.

summary: Snow grip boost OFF on dry tracks (tarmac feel unchanged)
detail: Race a normal dry/tarmac track and confirm handling feels exactly as before the snow-grip change -- the ice-grip boost should apply ONLY to snow/ice surfaces.

summary: MP CUP podium: humans show profile colour, CPU shown in grey
detail: Finish an MP cup and check the podium -- human players show their own profile accent colour, CPU/AI opponents show grey, so humans are easy to tell from bots at a glance.

summary: Cops re-chase after you crash (was: 1 chase then never, esp. MP)
detail: Get chased, deliberately crash, recover, and keep driving -- a cop should be willing to chase you again; previously a cop would chase once and never re-engage for the rest of the race, especially in MP.

summary: Split MP: reset car resets YOUR car, not the other player
detail: In split-screen, have player 2 press reset-car and confirm ONLY player 2's car resets -- player 1 is completely unaffected.

summary: Split MP: change-camera affects YOUR pane, not the other
detail: In split-screen, have one player change camera view and confirm only THEIR pane's camera changes -- other panes keep their own independent camera.

summary: Split MP: rear-view affects YOUR pane (positioned panes)
detail: In split-screen (including non-default 'positioned' pane layouts), hold rear-view as one player and confirm only their pane shows it, regardless of pane arrangement.

summary: MP profile DELETE asks 'DELETE <name>? A=YES B=NO' first
detail: On the MP profile screen, select DELETE on a profile and confirm a prompt names that exact profile ('DELETE <name>?') with A=YES / B=NO, rather than deleting on the first press.

summary: Profile delete removes ONLY the named/selected profile
detail: Create a few profiles, delete one via the confirm prompt, and confirm ONLY that profile is removed -- all others (and anyone holding one) are unaffected.

summary: MP setup: ARCADE/SIM selector only on track select (not mode opts)
detail: Go through MP setup and confirm the ARCADE/SIMULATION selector appears on track-select and does NOT also duplicate on the mode-options screen.

summary: ARCADE: ~2x as many item boxes spawn along the track
detail: Compare item box density along the track in Arcade mode -- roughly twice as many boxes should spawn along the route, so you should rarely go long without seeing one.

summary: ARCADE: power-up effects last 2x longer (GHOST/WRECK/oil)
detail: Grab GHOST, WRECK, or the oil HAZARD in Arcade and time the duration -- each should last roughly double the original baseline (an earlier, larger duration pass than the later 20%-longer tweak).

summary: ARCADE NITRO: sustained 2.5x acceleration boost (~5s), not instant
detail: Grab NITRO and watch acceleration -- it should ramp into a sustained ~2.5x boost lasting about 5 seconds, not an instant one-shot speed jump that fades immediately.

summary: Collisions hug car silhouette (hull) - tight contact, no gap
detail: Clip the side of another car or wall at a shallow angle -- collision should trigger right at your car's visual silhouette/convex hull, no visible-but-no-collision gap.

summary: AI un-wedges without driving off-track (steers to interior)
detail: Watch an AI car that gets wedged against a wall or another car -- its recovery steering should aim toward the track interior, never driving off-track while un-wedging.

summary: AI steers away when wedged vs car/player (no infinite grind)
detail: Deliberately wedge an AI car against your own car and watch how long it stays stuck -- it should actively steer away to break the wedge, not grind indefinitely with no progress.

summary: ARCADE airborne launch dialled way down (was too high/unplayable)
detail: Hit a jump/ramp in Arcade and compare the airborne launch height/distance -- should be noticeably tamer than an earlier version that launched cars unplayably high.

summary: ARCADE power-ups now floating boxes you drive through
detail: Confirm item boxes in Arcade are floating cubes you simply drive INTO to collect, not a target you shoot or press a button on.

summary: Item box: glowing spinning pulsing cube w/ kind icon
detail: Look closely at an item box before grabbing it -- it should be a glowing cube that's both spinning and pulsing, with a small icon indicating which power-up kind it holds.

summary: Grabbed item box vanishes, respawns after 5 seconds
detail: Grab an item box, note its position -- it should vanish immediately then reappear in roughly the same spot about 5 seconds later, not stay gone or respawn instantly.

summary: One power-up at a time; can't grab another until it ends
detail: While holding a power-up, drive over another item box and confirm you can NOT pick up a second one until the current effect ends.

summary: Box frequency scales with human player count (100-300)
detail: Compare item box spawn frequency between a 1-human race and one with several humans -- more humans should mean noticeably more boxes (roughly a 100-300% scale), not a fixed rate.

summary: 5+ players: chance of paired boxes (left + right shoulder)
detail: With 5+ players, watch for item boxes spawning in PAIRS -- one on each shoulder of the road at roughly the same point -- as an extra spawn variant that starts at this player count.

summary: HAZARD oil (3 lanes): hit it = drift uncontrollably ~2.5s
detail: Hit a HAZARD oil slick (should span roughly 3 lanes) and confirm it causes an uncontrollable drift for about 2.5 seconds before you regain full control.

summary: Game Options: POWER-UPS on/off toggle (persists)
detail: In Game Options toggle POWER-UPS off, race and confirm no boxes spawn; restart the game and confirm the OFF state persisted rather than resetting to default.

summary: Item boxes start after span 100, sit low near the road
detail: Note where the first item box appears -- should not spawn before roughly span 100, and boxes generally sit low, near road height, not floating high above it.

summary: Item boxes sit on road edges; steer over to grab one
detail: Confirm item boxes sit along the road EDGES (not the centre), so you must steer toward one side to collect them rather than driving straight through the middle.

summary: Car SILHOUETTE glows the effect colour (not a blob)
detail: Grab a power-up with a visual effect (e.g. GHOST) and look at your car -- the glow should trace your car's actual silhouette/shape, not appear as a generic blob detached from it.

summary: GHOST: car turns translucent, passes through traffic
detail: Grab GHOST and drive into a traffic car or wall -- your car should turn visibly translucent and pass through it without colliding, for the effect's duration.

summary: Effect name shows centred below the checkpoint timer
detail: Grab any power-up and check the HUD -- the active effect's name should display centred, positioned below the checkpoint timer, not overlapping it or off to a side.

summary: Quick Race PHYSICS row toggles ARCADE/SIMULATION + fits OK/Back
detail: Open Quick Race and find the PHYSICS row -- toggling ARCADE/SIMULATION should actually change the race's dynamics, and the row should fit on screen alongside OK/BACK with no overlap.

summary: Minimap: on a branch both fork tracks render (not just dots)
detail: Drive up to a fork with the minimap visible -- both branches should render as actual road geometry, not just a couple of disconnected dots marking the branch point.

summary: MORE STATS: POWER captioned (engine output); WEIGHT under GRIP
detail: Open MORE STATS for a car and confirm POWER has a caption clarifying it's engine output, and WEIGHT sits under GRIP in the layout, not its old position.

summary: MORE STATS BALANCE shows a visual front/rear weight split bar

summary: game_client.py crashed on ConnectionResetError during launch/boot-wait (FIXED)
detail: [MCP CONTROL finding 2026-07-21 claude3] On Windows, sending a UDP datagram to port 37060 before the game has bound it returns an ICMP port-unreachable, surfaced by recvfrom as WSAECONNRESET (WinError 10054). game_client.GameClient.command() only caught socket.timeout, so the very first ping during the launch/boot wait raised an unhandled ConnectionResetError and aborted the whole driver instead of retrying. FIX APPLIED: command() now also catches ConnectionResetError (treat as no-listener-yet, 0.1 s backoff + retry within the existing retries loop); added import time. Re-verified: launch_game boot-wait now polls cleanly until the socket answers. Confirm the fix holds if server.py is driven via MCP (same client path).

summary: start_race sticky game_type leaks across races -> hard crash (drag mode + traffic/cops on a non-drag track)
detail: [MCP CONTROL finding 2026-07-21 claude3] start_race/cs_apply only overwrite the scenario fields the caller supplies (documented "unset fields keep their INI value"). Consequence: after a drag race (game_type=9), a follow-up start_race(track=2, traffic=1, cops=1) that omits game_type inherits game_type=9, so the engine loads the drag strip (level030.zip) for track_index=2, runs the drag lengthen/widen path, then places traffic+cops slots on that mangled strip and CRASHES: 0xC0000005 at td5re.exe+0x3E731 (access=300aa16a), engine.log shows repeated "level_number: drag race (game_type=9 mp_drag=0) -> level030.zip" for track_index=2. Not a control-transport defect (the module faithfully applied the leaked config) but a sharp MCP footgun + a latent engine crash for the drag-mode + traffic/cops + non-drag-track combo. RECOMMEND one of: (a) start_race resets mode-defining fields (game_type/dynamics) to an explicit default unless supplied; (b) the engine rejects/guards game_type=9 with traffic/cops on a non-drag track instead of dereferencing; (c) at minimum document the sticky-field semantics in server.py/handoff. Workaround today: always pass game_type explicitly. Verified arcade case passes once game_type=0 is passed. [ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED 2026-07-21 claude3 via addr2line/nm on the unstripped DEV exe: crash is a USE-AFTER-FREE in td5_ai_refresh_route_state_slot (td5_ai.c:1650, EIP td5re.exe+0x3E731) reached from td5_ai_set_route_tables. Chain: td5_track_load_routes (td5_track.c:6848) on a level RELOAD frees the old s_route_left/right buffers (6852-6858 + drag-extend free(old) at 6916) then calls td5_ai_set_route_tables(new) at 6925 -> td5_ai_refresh_route_state (td5_ai.c:1239) loops every active slot -> refresh_route_state_slot PATH 2b (default, td5_ai.c:1571-1574) leaves rs[RS_ROUTE_TABLE_PTR] UNCHANGED = the PREVIOUS race buffer, just freed; line 1650 route_table[span*3+1] then derefs the freed ptr (0x300aa010). The index is bounds-clamped (1642-1647) but the BASE pointer is not validated. Latent because: normal levels leave the freed buffer mapped in the CRT heap (garbage, no fault) while the drag EXTEND path mallocs/frees LARGE buffers that get individually mapped+unmapped -> hard fault; needs two consecutive drag-level loads + traffic/cops raising active-slot count so a stale PATH-2b slot is processed; selftest never hits it (drag runs solo, arcade-tr-cops uses single-race game_type). SURGICAL FIX: in refresh_route_state_slot, after resolving route_table (line 1582), if route_table is neither g_route_tables[0] nor g_route_tables[1] it is stale -> resync rs[RS_ROUTE_TABLE_PTR]=g_route_tables[selector] (and route_table) before any deref. Preserves byte-faithful PATH 2b for the live-pointer case (goldens unaffected) and only intervenes cross-level. Optionally also add an upstream config guard rejecting game_type=9 with traffic|cops on a non-drag track. REQUIRES golden re-verify (td5_ai.c is golden-guarded). [FIX ATTEMPT 2026-07-21 claude3 — REVERTED, goldens broke: the naive equality guard (resync rs[RS_ROUTE_TABLE_PTR] when it != g_route_tables[0]/[1]) FAILS the golden suite (race-golden-moscow pose/motion + rgold L1 growing 2451->6041). Reason: the golden baseline DEPENDS on the premature refresh. In the selftest (many races in ONE process), when a golden race's level loads, td5_ai_set_route_tables -> td5_ai_refresh_route_state runs while rs[] still holds the PREVIOUS scenario's just-freed (but still-mapped) route ptr; the baseline derefs that stale-but-mapped buffer and writes garbage-derived rs fields (RS_FORWARD_TRACK_COMP, boundaries, g_actor_forward_track_component[]) that init_runtime does NOT fully overwrite, so the golden ENCODES the garbage-read initial state. The guard instead reads the new valid table -> different initial state -> chaotic sim divergence. Equality can't tell freed-stale from a legit table anyway (both are one of the two tables; per-tick code at td5_ai.c:3198 relies on rs==g_route_tables[0] to mean primary route). CORRECT FIX (golden-preserving, own /fix session): buffer-LIFETIME reorder in td5_track_load_routes (td5_track.c) — DEFER free() of the old s_route_left/right (and the drag-extend free(old) at 6916) until AFTER the new tables are installed + refreshed, instead of freeing at 6852-6858/6863 up front. The premature refresh then reads the SAME bytes (free doesn't zero freed memory, so golden-identical) but the page stays mapped so the drag large-buffer case can't fault. Touches golden-guarded td5_track.c -> full golden re-verify required. Root-cause investigation + failed-attempt evidence complete; implementation deferred.

Across normal + forced-recovery + a real crash, the InfoQueue drained EXACTLY ONE error class: sev=1(ERROR) cat=9(EXECUTION) id=378 ID3D11Device::RemoveDevice DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG (TDR: the GPU took too long / hung; 'fallback to less aggressive use of the display hardware'). Combined with the DRAW WATCH ring (fault in IDXGISwapChain_Present on a recovered gen-2 device, clean current-gen draws, valid SRVs), the conclusion is DEFINITIVE: our D3D11 API usage is VALID; the 0xC0000005 is the NVIDIA UMD (nvwgf2um) hard-faulting in Present during/after a hardware TDR, massively amplified here by an abnormal device-recreation storm (this test session drove gen to ~4/scenario). NO app-side API fix exists (debug layer would have flagged one). Mitigation, not cure: keep reducing GPU load (frame cap, per-race FF warm-up, device-lost recovery already do this) + survive via the crash-capture harness. To reduce residual rate, consider a fresh-GPU baseline + possibly lowering the default frame cap or adding a short settle after Backend_RecreateDevice before the first present.

summary: DRAW WATCH ring is empty during real gameplay (Backend_NoteDraw only on the legacy Device3 path)
detail: [FORENSICS GAP 2026-07-22] The SEH crash dump prints DRAW WATCH total_draws=0 even after thousands of presents, so the culprit-draw ring (meant to name which draw tripped the driver) is dead weight exactly when needed. Cause: Backend_NoteDraw is called only from d3d11 wrapper device3.c DrawPrimitive/DrawIndexedPrimitive (the legacy DDraw-wrapper API), but the source-port renderer (td5_plat_render_* -> d3d11 backend pipeline) issues its draws directly and bypasses Device3, so nothing feeds the ring in normal play. FIX: call Backend_NoteDraw (or equivalent) from the port's actual draw submission path so the ring captures real gameplay draws + their bound SRV/generation.

summary: Self-test race-drag-solo silently runs KESWICK, not a drag race (+ drag leaves sticky cross-race state)
detail: [FOUND 2026-07-22 by watching the run] The selftest 'race-drag-solo' step renders Keswick, not the drag strip. Cause: RaceScenario (td5_selftest.c) has NO game_type field, so the row only sets track=19; 19 is out of range for the 19-entry schedule table and falls through to level001 (=Keswick), and the drag-strip override (level030) keys on game_type==DRAG_RACE which the selftest never sets. VERIFIED the mechanism: a control-socket drag (game_type=9) logs 'level_number: drag race -> level030.zip' correctly. FIXING the selftest is NOT trivial: adding a game_type field + drag-solo=9 (so it really runs the strip) breaks the moscow/pelton golden SIM hashes, for TWO reasons: (1) a drag race leaves sticky route/mode-config/finish state that contaminates a SUBSEQUENT race's determinism (same class as drag route-table UAF 9b1c0691 + sticky-game_type), and (2) the golden harness is ORDER-SENSITIVE (goldens recorded against the exact committed scenario sequence; see 2026-07-11 note) so changing/moving/removing ANY pre-golden scenario shifts the hashes. PROPER FIX SEQUENCE: (a) reset drag runtime globals on race init (route buffers, drag field size, mp_mode_config drag fields, finish/extension) so drag->normal is clean; (b) add RaceScenario.game_type + set drag-solo=9; (c) re-record trace_goldens. Change was diagnosed + REVERTED 2026-07-22 (broke goldens).

summary: Auto-track G3: major height differences (Scotland/San Francisco scale)
detail: [R8 SHAPE G3 2026-08-30] TD5RE-only, td5_trackgen.c, DEFAULT ON (TD5RE_R8_SHAPE_RELIEF=0 for an A/B). Track 60, seeds 99991 and 777. The elevation profile was two sines of amplitude 6000 drawn at 2..6 waves over the whole track, i.e. nearly the entire grade budget spent at HIGH frequency for a peak-to-peak of only ~10-12k world units -- undulation, not topography. ROOT INSIGHT: range and grade are different axes. The cap (TD5_TG_MAX_GRADE 0.12) bounds |dY| per SPAN, and a sine term of amplitude A over w waves contributes A*2*PI*w/N of slope, so halving the frequency buys twice the height for the same slope. Raising the grade cap was NOT done and must not be -- it was once cut to 0.035 on an inverted reading of the airborne mask and had to be restored.
